proposals.defect: None provable: EN "upright or inverted" is delivered by "pagtindog o bali" as the corpus itself uses those words for image orientation.
proposals.attestation: Finding refuted. `--bis bali` (20 bodies): the two sibling image-characteristic cards render exactly this contrast with bali — dcard-08765 "Ang upright image dili bali, samtang ang inverted image bali o baliskad" (EN: upright/inverted) and dcard-11226 "ang inverted image morag bali o balit-ad" (EN: inverted); dcard-11226 also uses nagatindog for upright, matching this card's pagtindog. bali is also used for bone fracture elsewhere, but in the image context the corpus attests it for inverted, so the Cebuano already delivers the English. Any remaining doubt is a teacher's call, not a defensible edit.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang skeletal system mosuporta sa lawas, moprotektar sa mga internal organs sama sa kasingkasing ug baga, motabang sa paglihok, magtipig ug minerals sama sa calcium, ug maghimo ug red ug white blood cells.
proposals.defect: EN lists "enables movement" as one of the five skeletal functions; the Cebuano item "magpaliwat" names breeding/propagating, so the movement function is stated nowhere on the card.
proposals.attestation: `--bis paliwat`: 0 Cebuano BODIES — NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY, so the existing word is unsourced. Replacement taken from the corpus's own parallel function-list card dcard-00603 (EN "helping movement"): "mosuporta kini, motabang sa paglihok, moprotektar sa mga internal organs...". `--bis motabang`: 517 bodies. `--bis paglihok`: 616 bodies (e.g. dcard-01527 "nagtabang sa lawas sa paglihok" for EN "helps the body to move"). Only the one word changed; emphasis span "skeletal system" intact.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang mga butang magkalahi sa usag usa base sa mga physical property sama sa kagahi, pagkasinaw, ug pagka-stretchable, nga atong maobserbahan gamit ang atong mga igbalati.
proposals.defect: EN names "shininess" as the second property and "our senses" as the means of observing; the Cebuano gives the non-word "pagkakasaw" and narrows senses to "panan-aw" (sight), so shininess is unrecoverable and the card claims hardness and stretchability are seen with the eyes.
proposals.attestation: `--bis pagkakasaw`: 1 body = this card itself; `--bis kasaw`: 0 bodies (NOT ATTESTED). Replacement from the parallel physical-properties card dcard-04618 (EN "like being hard, flexible, or shiny"): "sama sa pagkagahi, pagka-flexible, o pagkasinaw"; `--bis sinaw`: 58 bodies for shiny (ffct-00295 "sinaw nga agi", ffct-08386 "sinaw nga panit"). For senses, `--en "our senses"` gives igbalati as the top content word (6) — ffct-04315 "lima ka organ sa igbalati: ang mata, dalunggan, ilong, dila, ug panit", ffct-05285 "5 ka nag-unang igbalati"; the exact phrase "mga igbalati" is attested in 3 bodies (ffct-00123, ffct-02871, ffct-06181), and ffct-00123 shows panan-aw is only one member of the set ("mga igbalati sama sa panan-aw ug pandungog"). Two word swaps only; span "physical property" intact.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Mga katunga sa radiation sa adlaw ang ma-reflect o masuyop sa mga panganod ug atmosphere sa dili pa kini moabot sa yuta.
proposals.defect: EN says half the radiation is "reflected or absorbed" (i.e. turned back or taken in); the Cebuano "maaninag" names light passing THROUGH a translucent body, so the reflected half is described as transmitted and the blocking is lost.
proposals.attestation: `--bis aninag`: 3 bodies, all transmission — ffct-15053 "Ang salamin aninag, mao nga makaagi ang kahayag" (EN: glass is transparent), ffct-15064 (EN: not transparent), ffct-16625 (EN: transparent). `--bis maaninag`: 2 bodies = this card and its twin dcard-03118 only, so it never vouches for itself. Replacement `--bis ma-reflect`: 5 bodies, including the same atmosphere fact in dcard-08794 "ang uban ma-reflect sa kawanangan ug ang uban ma-absorb sa atmosphere" (EN: some is reflected into space) and ffct-26990 "Ang pula nga kolor ma-reflect" (EN: is reflected). masuyop (60 bodies, absorb) kept unchanged; span "radiation" intact.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang reflection adunay duha ka kahulugan: ang imahe nga makita nimo sa samin, ug ang kinaiya sa light nga motalbog gikan sa sinaw nga butang.
proposals.defect: EN defines the second meaning as light "bouncing off a shiny surface"; the Cebuano verb mopalta (Sp. falta = to be absent/lacking) does not name bouncing, and on a definition card the verb is the entire fact.
proposals.attestation: `--bis mopalta`: 4 bodies only, none of them a definition of reflection (dcard-07176, ffct-38285, ffct-39398) — a fringe form, not the corpus's word. The corpus word for light bouncing off a surface is motalbog: `--bis motalbog` 20 bodies, including the reflection definition itself, ffct-22648 "Ang reflection mahitabo kung ang kahayag motama sa usa ka ibabaw ug motalbog pabalik" (EN: reflection happens when light hits a surface and bounces right back), and ffct-22652 "ang kahayag motalbog gikan niini" (EN: light bounces off them) — the exact frame "motalbog gikan" is attested in 2 bodies (ffct-22652, dcard-00344). "samin" left alone: 27 bodies for mirror (ffct-26869 "patag nga samin"). One word changed; span "reflection" intact.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon paghimo ang bubbles sa precipitate test?

Ang matag mixture bahinon ngadto sa duha ka gagmay nga bottles, takpan og hugot, ug uyogon gamit ang pareho nga kusog ug oras.
proposals.defect: EN's first procedure step is "each mixture is halved into two small bottles"; the Cebuano verb bahaon is the corpus's word for a sneeze, so the dividing action is never correctly named.
proposals.attestation: `--bis bahaon`: 4 bodies — the only non-defective one is ffct-13186 "Ang usa ka bahaon mopakatap og liboan ka gagmayng tulo" (EN: one sneeze sprays thousands of droplets); the other two (dcard-07592, dcard-07603) are the same split/halve slip, so they cannot vouch for it. Replacement `--bis bahinon`: 41 bodies for divide/split, including the identical frame "bahinon ngadto sa duha" in ffct-11501 "mahimong bahinon ngadto sa duha ka dakong grupo" (EN: split into two big groups), plus ffct-16187 "bahinon ang basura" (EN: separate trash). One word changed; span "bubbles" intact.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang uban nga mga tanom adunay baho ug daotang lasa, nga mga specialized structures nga makapugong sa mga predator sa pagkaon kanila.
proposals.defect: EN says the plants have a bad smell AND a bad taste as defences; the Cebuano "lami" means good flavour, so the card tells the child the plants taste delicious and still repel predators.
proposals.attestation: `--bis lami`: 332 bodies, consistently positive/neutral flavour — ffct-00167 "lami nga pagkaon" (EN: a tasty food), ffct-00156 "Mas lami kan-on ang rambutan" (EN: best eaten fresh) — so bare lami cannot carry EN's "bad". Replacement is the corpus's own rendering of the exact English phrase: ffct-18141 EN "remove bad tastes and odors" -> BIS "tangtangon ang daotang lasa ug baho". Component words independently attested: bare "lasa" = taste in 24 bodies (ffct-14617 "nagtinabangay ang lasa ug amoy" for EN taste and smell; ffct-02081 "daot ang lasa nila" for EN predators warned the prey tastes bad), and daotan/daotang in 30 bodies for EN harmful/bad (ffct-00137 "daotang bacteria"). Sibling defence cards use the same idea (ffct-12156 "makahilo o dili lami" for EN "poisonous or taste bad"). baho kept as-is (dcard-04071 uses it for EN bad smells). One word replaced; span "specialized structures" intact.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang himsog nga mga tanom adunay itom-berde nga mga dahon ug lig-on nga tul-id nga mga tangkay, nga nagpakita nga nakakuha sila ug igong kahayag sa adlaw, tubig, ug hangin.
proposals.defect: EN's second health sign is "sturdy upright stems"; the Cebuano "mga sanga" names branches, a different plant part, so the stem is never mentioned on the card.
proposals.attestation: `--bis sanga` (bare): 283 bodies, uniformly branch — ffct-00052 "nagkiskis sa iyang nawong sa mga sanga" (EN: rubs its face on branches), ffct-00196 "salag ... sa sanga sa kahoy" (EN: nest in a tree's branches). Replacement `--bis tangkay`: 104 bodies for stem/stalk, e.g. ffct-00871 "sa tumoy sa tangkay" (EN: at the top of its stem), ffct-00926 "sa sulod sa tangkay ug dahon" (EN: in its stems and leaves); the plural "mga tangkay" is attested in 17 bodies (ffct-01412 "taas nga mga tangkay" for EN tall stalks). `--en stems` ranks punoan (58) and tangkay (32) as the corpus's stem words; tangkay is also already in this card's own terms list. One word changed; span "itom-berde nga mga dahon" intact.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang hemophilia usa ka X-linked recessive trait diin ang dugo mamuo hinay kaayo o dili gyud, busa bisan gamay nga samad mahimong delikado.
proposals.defect: EN defines hemophilia as blood that "clots very slowly or not at all"; the Cebuano "mobag-o" says the blood changes slowly, so clotting — the entire definition — is absent from the card.
proposals.attestation: Replacement `--bis mamuo`: 22 bodies, all blood clotting — ffct-03958 "protina nga makatabang nga mamuo ang dugo" (EN: proteins that help your blood clot), ffct-03062 "nagapugong sa dugo nga mamuo" (EN: keeps blood from clotting), ffct-04425 "Motabang ang bitamina K aron mamuo ang dugo" (EN: helps your blood clot); the exact collocation "mamuo ang dugo" appears in 6 bodies. Related forms confirm the root: momuo 2 bodies (ffct-06487 platelets "motabang niini nga momuo"), pagmuo 4 bodies (ffct-10798 "pagmuo sa dugo" for EN clotting). One word changed; span "hemophilia" intact.

proposals.defect: None provable: EN "thin strands" is delivered by "nipis nga mga hilo", which is the corpus's own wording for thin threads/fibres.
proposals.attestation: Finding refuted. `--bis hilo`: 362 bodies — poison is one sense, but thread/fibre is squarely attested in the same corpus: ffct-00202 "ang nipis nga hilo na lang ang mabilin" for EN "only thin, strong threads remain" (the exact phrase nipis nga hilo this card uses), ffct-00158 "Ang seda usa ka natural nga hilo" for EN "silk is a natural fiber", ffct-00171 "ang hilo sa seda" for EN "silk thread", ffct-00206 "hilo nga seda" for EN "a thread of silk", ffct-01896 "Ang hilo sa abaka" for EN "abaca fiber". The card also names optical fibers in English immediately before, so the referent is not left ambiguous. Choosing tanod (6 bodies) or hibla (52) over an attested reading would be a style edit, which is out of scope.

proposals.defect: None in the body: fact_bis states plants give firewood and defines it as "ang kahoy nga gisunog aron makahimo ug init sa pagluto ug pagpainit sa balay", which is exactly what fact_en says.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the suyop defect the finding describes is in title_bis ("Tanom alang sa Suyop") and in the terms list, not in fact_bis, and this task repairs fact_bis only. The body carries no wrong word — it keeps "firewood" in English and then glosses it correctly with kahoy/gisunog, so a child does get the fact. Introducing sugnod or gatong into the body would also break the emphasis span "firewood", which renders by exact substring match. The title needs a Cebuano teacher (or a title-scoped pass).

proposals.defect: None in the body: fact_bis already says the shoots grow from buds "sa punoan sa parent plant", which is EN's "at the base of a parent plant's stem".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the tungkod (walking cane) defect is confined to title_bis "Suckers sa Tungkod"; the finding itself states the body uses the correct word. punoan is the corpus's stem/base word (`--en stems` ranks punoan first at 58 occurrences: ffct-00705 "Ang punoan sa tanom moliko" for EN "a plant's stem bends"), so fact_bis needs no edit. Rewriting it would risk the emphasis span "suckers" for no gain; the title is out of scope here.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Kanus-a kanunay mobangga ang asteroid sa Earth?

Halos kausa sa usa ka tuig, usa ka asteroid nga sama kadako sa sakyanan ang mobangga sa atmosphere sa Earth, apan masunog kini sa dili pa makaabot sa yuta!
proposals.defect: The English says the asteroid HITS Earth's atmosphere, but the Cebuano says it 'motagbaw' (is sated/satisfied), so the collision the card is about is never stated.
proposals.attestation: `motagbaw` --bis: 1 body = this card itself, so it is self-vouching and unsourced; `tagbaw`/`katagbaw` = 0 bodies. Replacement `mobangga` --bis: 22 bodies, collision sense (ffct-21915 'magdikit ang mga butang human mobangga' = objects hit; ffct-18250 'particle nga padayon nga nagbangga sa mga dingding' = particles hitting walls), and the corpus uses it for this exact concept on sibling impact cards: dcard-05743 'kon ang meteorite mobangga sa usa ka planeta o bulan' and dcard-05744 'kon mobangga ang comet o asteroid'. Only the two motagbaw tokens changed; emphasis span 'kausa sa usa ka tuig' kept verbatim. (The weaker 'Kanus-a kanunay' for 'How often' left alone — the span restores the frequency and it is not the provable defect.)

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang tephra kay mga tipik nga volcanic debris nga kusganong gipagawas sa atmosphere panahon sa explosive eruptions, ug kini makaabot ug tinagpulo ka mga kilometro sa taas sa bulkan.
proposals.defect: The English says the column extends TENS of kilometers (open-ended), but 'napulo ka' is the cardinal TEN, so the Cebuano states one fixed, smaller number.
proposals.attestation: Replacement `tinagpulo` --bis: 1 body, and it is the corpus's rendering of this exact English construction — ffct-39675 EN 'a sudden jump of tens of centimeters' / BIS 'kalit nga lukso nga tinagpulo ka centimeters'. Rejected alternatives checked: `pinulo-pulo` = 0 bodies and `pulo-pulo` = 0 bodies (NOT ATTESTED, unusable); `liboan` (174) / `gatusan` (84) are thousands/hundreds, wrong magnitude. Single token changed; emphasis span 'tephra' untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang pagbaliko sa glowstick nagtugot sa duha ka kemikal sa sulod nga mo-react ug magpagawas og kahayag, usa ka pananglitan sa luminescence.
proposals.defect: The English says BENDING the glowstick is what lets the two chemicals react; the Cebuano 'pagbalik' is returning/going back, so the trigger action the card is titled after is missing.
proposals.attestation: `pagbaliko` --bis: 9 bodies, bending sense, including the corpus's own glowstick card ffct-04265 EN 'when you bend a glow stick to make it light up' / BIS 'sama sa pagbaliko sa glow stick aron mosiga'; also ffct-36665 'Kini nga pagbaliko gitawag nga diffraction' for wave bending. Root `baliko` --bis: 70 bodies (curved/hooked beak, curved horns). One token changed (restores the dropped -o); emphasis span 'luminescence' untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang mimicry mao ang pagsundog sa usa ka dili peligroso nga mananap sa dagway, baho, lami, kolor, o tingog sa usa ka peligroso nga mananap aron panalipdan ang kaugalingon.
proposals.defect: The English defines mimicry as the harmless animal COPYING the dangerous animal's look/smell/taste/colour/sound; 'pag-ila' means to identify/recognise, so the Cebuano defines mimicry as merely recognising it.
proposals.attestation: `pag-ila` --bis: 61 bodies, identify/recognise on every sampled one (ffct-02438 'Unsaon pag-ila kung buhi ang usa ka butang' = how do you tell; ffct-05926 'maglisod sila pag-ila sa pipila ka kolor' = trouble telling colours apart) — never copy. Replacement `pagsundog` --bis: 10 bodies, copy/imitate, and the corpus uses the identical frame for this exact definition: ffct-08522 'ang mimicry mao ang pagsundog sa mas peligroso nga hayop'; also ffct-03402 'pinaagi sa pagsundog sa palibot'. One token changed; emphasis span 'mimicry' untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang mga itom nga butang maayo nga mosuyop ug mopagawas sa radiation, samtang ang puti o sinaw nga butang mas mopabalik sa init ug magpabiling mas bugnaw ilalom sa adlaw.
proposals.defect: The English says white or shiny objects REFLECT more heat; 'mopalta' (< Sp. falta) means to be lacking/missing, so the absorb-vs-reflect contrast the card teaches is never stated.
proposals.attestation: Replacement `mopabalik` --bis: 2 bodies, both the bounce-back sense with the same 'mopabalik sa X' frame — ffct-02746 'salamin ... nga mopabalik sa kahayag' (EN 'bounces light back out'), ffct-14264 'tubig mopabalik sa tingog diretso' (EN 'bounces its sound straight back'). Same stem as `magpabalik` --bis: 5 bodies, incl. the near-identical card ffct-22191 EN 'white clothes, which reflect more of the rays' / BIS 'puti nga magpabalik sa mas daghang silaw'; --en 'reflect' also gives ffct-21948 'ang puti nagbalik sa halos tanang kahayag'. mo- prefix chosen to match the sentence's existing mosuyop/mopagawas. One token changed; emphasis span 'itom' untouched.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis delivers everything fact_en says — male butterfly finds the female by detecting the chemical scent she releases, called a pheromone.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis only ('Senaryo' for 'Signal'), and this task repairs fact_bis. The body never uses senaryo and loses no fact from the English, so there is nothing in it that is provably wrong. Title fix belongs to the title pass.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis gives all three signs the English gives — more noise, louder and more frequent meowing, very affectionate toward people.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is a title-only defect ('Senaryo' for 'Signs'); the word senaryo does not occur in the body. The finding itself concedes 'Body describes the signs'. Nothing in fact_bis is refutable against fact_en.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis lists all five behaviours the English lists — weaving in and out of legs, rubbing, shaking the pelvis, rolling on the floor, flagging the tail.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ('Batas' = law, for 'Behavior'); the body contains no batas and drops no fact. 'mag-flag sa iyang ikog' is a clumsy borrowing but carries the English 'flags her tail', and clumsiness/register is out of scope.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis keeps the correct term 'carbon fixation' and delivers the attachment to RuDP, the unstable six-carbon molecule, and the immediate split into two PGA.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding's own text states the defect is in title_bis ('Pag-ayo' = repair) and that 'The card's OWN body keeps the correct term'. Body verb 'ikabit' --bis: 13 bodies, attach/connect (dcard-05836 'ammeter ... kinahanglang ikabit nga naka-series'), which is what the English 'is attached to' says.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Kadaghanan sa mga PGAL molecules gamiton aron ma-regenerate ang RuDP, ang sinugdanan nga molecule, aron magpadayon ang pagtuyok sa Calvin cycle ug makakabit pa ug mas daghang carbon dioxide.
proposals.defect: The English says the cycle can FIX more carbon dioxide (attach it to RuDP); 'maka-ayo' means can heal/repair, so the Cebuano says the cycle repairs CO2, and this card never contains the term 'carbon fixation' to correct it.
proposals.attestation: Replacement `makakabit` --bis: 1 body, exactly this attach sense — dcard-04146 EN 'a carbon with a double bond can attach to only two other groups' / BIS 'carbon nga adunay double bond makakabit lamang sa duha ka laing grupo'. Same stem is the corpus's word for carbon fixation itself: --en 'carbon fixation' returns dcard-07990 'ang carbon dioxide sa hangin ikabit sa usa ka five-carbon molecule' (`ikabit` 13 bodies) and dcard-03363 'gikuha ug gitaod sa usa ka five-carbon sugar'. `mokabit` --bis: 1 body, also attach (dcard-11346). One token changed; emphasis span 'RuDP' untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon nimo pagtandi ang duha ka butang sa usa ka higayon?

Ang Venn diagram mogamit ug nagsapaw nga mga lingin aron ipakita kung unsa ang pareho ug unsa ang lahi sa duha ka set!
proposals.defect: The English says the circles OVERLAP — the overlap is where 'what is similar' goes — but 'magkatapad' means placed beside each other, so the mechanism the card teaches is lost.
proposals.attestation: `magkatapad` --bis: 2 bodies; the only non-self one is ffct-14522 'Nganong magkatapad ang mata sa iring' (EN 'Why are a cat's eyes both up front?') = side by side, not overlapping. Replacement `nagsapaw` --bis: 6 bodies, and it is the corpus's word for this exact English: ffct-09423 EN 'overlapping plates' / BIS 'nagsapaw nga mga plate'; ffct-12424 EN 'overlapping scales' / BIS 'nagsapaw nga himbis'. The 'nagsapaw nga mga X' frame is attested verbatim. One token changed; emphasis span 'Venn diagram' untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Lainlain ang paagi sa paglihok sa mga mananap depende sa ilang habitat ug istruktura sa lawas - ang uban molakaw, molukso, moambak, molupad, mokamang, o molangoy.
proposals.defect: The English lists JUMP among the ways animals move; 'motipdas' is built on tipdas, the word for measles, so the Cebuano puts a disease word in the list and the 'jump' item is never given.
proposals.attestation: `tipdas` --bis: 6 bodies, measles on every one (ffct-00148 'Ang tipdas usa ka makatakod nga sakit nga gipahinabo sa usa ka bayrus' = measles is a contagious viral disease; ffct-02161 'bata nga adunay tipdas o bulutong-tubig'). `motipdas` --bis: 1 body = this card itself, so unsourced. Replacement `moambak` --bis: 9 bodies, jump/leap (ffct-00883 'moambak ang sailfin lizard sa tubig' = jumps into the water; ffct-04402 'Moambak kini aron dakpon ang iyang biktima' = it leaps onto its prey). Chosen over molukso because molukso is already the card's 'hop', so moambak keeps hop and jump distinct. One token changed; emphasis span 'paglihok' untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang scanning electron microscope nagpabalik sa electron beam sa surface sa usa ka sample aron makahimo ug three-dimensional nga imahe sa gawas niini.
proposals.defect: The English says the SEM bounces the electron beam off the sample's surface, but the Cebuano says it BOILS the beam (nagpapabukal, also in a Tagalog-shaped nagpapa- form), so the reflect-off-the-surface mechanism is never delivered.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: nagpabalik. `--bis nagpabalik` = 11 Cebuano bodies, all reflect/return sense, incl. ffct-22107 'Ang salamin nagbawi o nagpabalik sa kahayag nga moigo niini' for EN 'A mirror reflects, or bounces back, the light that hits it' -- same agent-bounces-a-beam frame. Defect side verified independently: `--bis pabukal` = 37 bodies, every one boiling (ffct-04385 'pabukalon ang tubig' = boil water). `--bis patalbog` = NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY, so the talbog causative was rejected even though bare motalbog exists. Emphasis span 'scanning electron microscope' present verbatim; one-word diff.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang thermosphere adunay ionosphere, usa ka bahin sa charged gas particles nga nagpabalik sa radio waves ug naghimo sa nagdan-ag nga auroras duol sa mga polo.
proposals.defect: The English says the ionosphere's charged particles bounce radio waves, but the Cebuano says they boil them (nagpabukal), so the reflection fact is lost and nothing else in the card restores it.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: nagpabalik. Near-exact corpus twin ffct-30467: 'Ang ionosphere adunay mga charged particles nga nagpabalik sa radio waves' for EN 'The ionosphere has charged particles that bounce radio waves back down' -- same subject, same verb slot. Also ffct-22107 (mirror bounces back light). `--bis nagpabukal` = 4 bodies: geyser, geothermal, boiling-water convection, and this card -- i.e. boiling only. Emphasis span 'ionosphere' untouched; one-word diff.

proposals.defect: The English is about dragonflies hunting other insects, but the Cebuano body names tambubuyog (a bee), so the subject of the fact is wrong.
proposals.attestation: HOLD on the EMPHASIS rule, not on doubt about the defect. The defect is real and the fix is attested -- `--bis alindahaw` = 23 Cebuano bodies, all dragonfly (ffct-01239 'Usahay ang alindahaw mokaon sa nadakpan niini nga insekto'), while `--bis tambubuyog` = 1 body and 1 title, both this card. But emphasis_bis is exactly ['tambubuyog'], the single word that must change; any correct repair deletes the span verbatim-match and silently kills the bold. Since the span cannot be kept and the word cannot stay, this goes to a Cebuano teacher who can retarget emphasis_bis to 'alindahaw' (and the title 'Mga Pako sa Tambubuyog') in the same pass.

proposals.defect: The English says the Sun's rays strike the ground at a steep angle, but the Cebuano 'titipid ang anggulo' says the angle is economized/reduced -- the opposite reading -- so the steep-angle fact is not delivered.
proposals.attestation: HOLD on the EMPHASIS rule. Defect confirmed: `--bis titipid` = 1 Cebuano body, this card itself, so the word has no Cebuano attestation at all; the corpus word for steep is tarik (`--bis tarik` = 35 bodies, ffct-08245 'batoon o tarik nga yuta' for EN 'rocky, steep ground'). But emphasis_bis is exactly ['titipid'] -- the defective word IS the bolded span, so no repair can keep it verbatim. Needs a Cebuano teacher who can move the span to the replacement (tarik/matarik) at the same time.

proposals.defect: No defect in the body: fact_bis 'Sa dili pa molinog, sunda ang local disaster readiness plan...' delivers everything fact_en says about acting before an earthquake.
proposals.attestation: Finding refuted for the body -- it is about title_bis ('Sa Dili Pa Mout-og'), which is out of scope here. The body's verb is the corpus standard: `--bis molinog` = 10 Cebuano bodies, and `--en 'before an earthquake'` returns dcard-00096 and dcard-00119 both rendering it 'sa dili pa molinog', identical to this card. Safe spots / emergency kits / meeting places are all present. Nothing to change in fact_bis; the title still needs a separate title-scope fix.

proposals.defect: No defect in the body: fact_bis keeps the term 'nitrogen fixation' and states the N2-to-nitrates/ammonia conversion, bacteria and lightning exactly as fact_en does.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang metallic character, ang abilidad sa usa ka element nga mohatag og outer electrons ug magpakita og luster ug conductivity, motaas samtang mopaubos ka sa usa ka group ug pawala sa usa ka period.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang kinaiya sa surface nakaapekto sa resulta sa collision, busa mas taas motalbog ang bola sa gahi nga semento kaysa sa humok nga carpet.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Giunsa nimo pag-atiman ang mga tanom sa imong tanaman?

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang larvae mapusa gikan sa itlog apan dili parehas sa mga adult nga insekto, ug paspas silang motubo mao nga makadaghan silang mag-molt sa dili pa mahimong pupa.

proposals.new_fact_bis:

proposals.new_fact_bis: Mas mubo ang kinabuhi sa worker ant kaysa sa reyna — daghang worker ang mabuhi lang ug pipila ka bulan, samtang ang reyna mabuhi og pipila ka tuig kay gikan kaniya ang tanang bag-ong hulmigas.

We sweat to cool down" -> "Nganong mosingot ta? ... mo-alisngaw ang singot sa panit", ffct-02966 fan/sweat evaporation). proposals.new_fact_bis: Kung manukol ang putakti, mobuga kini og espesyal nga baho nga magtawag sa ubang putakti aron mosulong sab — mao nga delikado ang paghasi sa salag!

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsa gyud ang sulod sa hilo sa putakti?

Dili lang usa ka butang ang hilo sa putakti. Sagol kini sa lain-laing kemikal ug protina nga maghatag og kasakit ug paghubag — mao nga mura'g nagdilaab human matusok.

The corpus draws the distinction itself in ffct-03517: "Ang putakti ug hornet dili maghimo og dugos — ang tam-is nga dugos gikan ra sa putyukan". `--bis putyukan` = 89 bodies, overwhelmingly bee (beekeepers ffct-00248, queen ffct-00465, honey ffct-00574). Card's own title_bis already says "Putakti", so the repair matches the card. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Para unsa ang antennae sa hulmigas?

Ang duha ka antennae sa worker ant sama sa ilong ug kamot niini — gamiton niya kini aron makapanimaho, makahikap, ug makig-istorya sa ubang hulmigas!
proposals.defect: The English is about an ant's antennae and ants talking to other ants, but the Cebuano question asks about "antennae sa langgam" and closes with "ubang langgam" — in Cebuano langgam is a BIRD, so the card tells a child that birds have antennae.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: `hulmigas`. `ceb_usage.py --bis hulmigas` = 99 Cebuano BODIES, 58 titles, all ant (ffct-00110 EN "How many ants are there for every person?" -> "Pila ka hulmigas ang naa para sa matag tawo?"; ffct-00630 "Sa sulod sa kolonya sa hulmigas"). `--en "worker ant"` = 29 cards, frequency table led by hulmigas 19, e.g. ffct-00398 EN "Worker ants each have a job" -> "Ang matag trabahanteng hulmigas adunay kaugalingong buluhaton". The exact phrase I introduce, "ubang hulmigas", is attested verbatim in ffct-01858 (EN "so other ants can follow the path to the food" -> "aron masubay sa ubang hulmigas ang dalan paingon sa pagkaon"). `--bis langgam` = 697 bodies, bird throughout. Mid-sentence English "worker ant" left untouched, matching ffct-00574/ffct-00821 which also keep it. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano gaan ang bukog sa langgam?

Puno sa humok nga marrow ang bukog sa tawo nga naghimo og dugo. Gamay ra ang marrow sa hawan nga bukog sa langgam — mao nga sila gaan.
proposals.defect: The English is entirely about BONES (human bones packed with marrow, a bird's hollow bones), but the Cebuano says "buto" three times, which in Cebuano is seed/burst (and vulgar slang), not bone — so "buto sa tawo" does not deliver "human bones".
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: `bukog`. `ceb_usage.py --bis bukog` = 447 Cebuano BODIES, 206 titles, bone throughout (ffct-00002 EN "What connects your muscles to your bones?" -> "Unsa ang nagsumpay sa kaunuran sa bukog?"). Corpus-wide count over cards whose ENGLISH says bone/bones: 439 cards, 399 use bukog vs 21 using buto — buto is the 5% defect tail, not the corpus word. On the two neighbouring topics: `--en marrow` (17 cards) frequency table = bukog 15 vs buto 3, and all 3 buto hits are this card itself (ffct-00441 "sa sulod sa pipila ka dagkong bukog", ffct-02824 "kinauyokan sa bukog"); `--en "hollow bones"` gives the sibling ffct-00557 EN "How are hollow bird bones so strong?" -> "Giunsa paglig-on ang guwang nga bukog sa langgam?". `--bis buto` = 46 bodies, dominated by the seed sense (ffct-03179 seeds with hooks, ffct-03048 mangrove seeds). Kept every other word, including "hawan" and "marrow", which the card already used; no emphasis spans.

proposals.defect: None in the body: EN "Your skin releases sweat to cool your body down when you're feeling hot or tired" is delivered by "Ang panit magpagawas og singot aron pabugnawon ang lawas kon init o gikapoy kita".

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Makakontrol ba sa hunahuna sa hulmigas ang fungus?

Ang Ophiocordyceps nga fungus mosulod sa lawas sa carpenter ant ug mokontrol sa iyang gawi — mopugos sa hulmigas nga mokatkat sa piho nga gitas-on sa tanom sa dili pa mamatay, dayon molabas og mga spore gikan sa ulo niini.
proposals.defect: EN asks whether a fungus can control an ANT's mind and says it forces the ant to climb; the Cebuano question and the climbing clause both say `langgam` (bird), so the two clauses a child actually reads are about a bird.
proposals.attestation: Introduced one word, twice: `hulmigas`. Same evidence as ffct-04539 — ceb_usage.py --bis hulmigas = 99 Cebuano BODIES, all ants (ffct-00475 'Giunsa pagdakop sa antlion larva ang hulmigas?' / EN 'How does an antlion larva trap ants?'); --bis langgam = 697 bodies, all birds. Both replacements are the one-word slot swap; I deliberately left the untranslated 'carpenter ant' alone as the minimal diff, and `hulmigas` now glosses it for the reader. Emphasis span 'Ophiocordyceps' untouched and present verbatim (verified).

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang patola usa ka nagakatay nga utanon nga ginaluto samtang bata pa, ug kon tugotan nga mohinog, ang gahi nga lanot niini mahimong natural nga panghugas.
proposals.defect: EN says the loofah's dried FIBERS become the scrubbing sponge, but the Cebuano says `himbis`, which is animal scales, so the sponge is attributed to a hard scaly rind rather than fibers.
proposals.attestation: Introduced one word: `lanot`. ceb_usage.py --bis lanot = 47 Cebuano BODIES, plant fiber throughout (ffct-00202 'Ang lanot sa pinya' / EN 'Pineapple fiber'; ffct-00648 'limpyo nga lanot sa abaka' / EN 'clean abaca fiber'; ffct-01270 'humok, puti nga lanot' / EN 'soft, white fibers'). --en fiber ranks `lanot` as the top native rendering (43 hits across the 236 fiber cards, behind only the untranslated English 'fiber/fibers'). --bis himbis = 73 bodies, all scales (pangolin ffct-00810 'gahi nga himbis', fish/reptile ffct-01182), confirming the flag. Single-word swap: I left 'gahi' and everything else alone since the provable defect is fibers-vs-scales. Emphasis span 'patola' untouched (verified).

proposals.defect: EN says worker ANTS are sterile females that guard the nest and tend eggs and larvae; the body says `manggagawang langgam` (worker bird) twice and `pugad` (bird nest), so the answer text teaches it about birds.
proposals.attestation: HOLD on the emphasis rule, not on the language. The defect is real and the fix word is attested (--bis hulmigas = 99 Cebuano BODIES, all ants; ffct-00398 'Ang matag trabahanteng hulmigas' / EN 'Worker ants each have a job'; --bis langgam = 697 bodies, all birds). But emphasis_bis is ['manggagawang langgam'] — the bolded span IS the defective phrase. Correcting it to 'manggagawang hulmigas' leaves the span with no exact substring match, so the bold silently stops rendering; keeping the span verbatim would keep the bird. The repair needs emphasis_bis edited in the same commit, which is outside new_fact_bis, so this goes to the Cebuano teacher with the fix pre-identified. (For the record, title_bis 'Mamumuo nga Hulmigas' is already correct.)

proposals.defect: No defect survives the corpus check — the body does say a moth's feelers/antennae are bushy and feathery, which is what the English says.
proposals.attestation: The finding is refuted by the tool. --bis kabkab = 11 Cebuano BODIES and 5 of them are MOTH cards where kabkab renders moth: ffct-02117 'Managhigala ba ang alibangbang ug kabkab?' / EN 'Are butterflies and moths related?'; ffct-02174 'Daghang kabkab ang kolor brown o abuhon' / EN 'Many moths are brown or gray'; ffct-03612 / EN 'When moths rest, they spread their wings out flat'; ffct-03704 / EN 'Most moths fly at night'; ffct-05790 'kumpara sa kabkab' / EN 'than their cousins, the moths'. --en moth also ranks `kabkab` in its characteristic-word table. So kabkab is an attested corpus rendering of moth, not a cassava cracker intrusion; the toad uses (ffct-05158, ffct-06098) and the cracker use (ffct-18262) make it polysemous, but polysemy is a variation issue and Rule 1 puts that out of scope. `anunugba` (22 bodies) and `gamu-gamo` (18) are alternatives, not corrections. No word introduced.

Zero body uses as ape/monster. --en toad confirms the corpus is genuinely split (baki, kabkab, bakulaw, kabakaba all appear), and choosing among competing attested variants is standardisation, not defect repair — Rule 1 puts regional variation out of scope. proposals.new_fact_bis:
Dautan ra ba nga bakterya ang gipatay sa antibiotiko?

Dili diay — mapatay usab niini ang maayong bakterya sa atong tinai, mao nga usahay magkalibang ang moinom niini.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang mga dust mite sa higdaanan nga wala hugasi nagpagawas og mga protina nga makapukaw og hika ug allergy sa sensitibong mga bata.
proposals.defect: fact_en says the dust mites hide in UNWASHED bedding; fact_bis says 'dili hugot nga higdaanan' (bedding that is not tight), which asserts a different attribute and drops the washing fact entirely.
proposals.attestation: --bis hugot: 170 bodies, all tight/firm (ffct-00190 EN 'grip' -> 'makupot og hugot'; ffct-00383 EN 'tightly packed leaf sheaths' -> 'hugot nga leaf sheath'), so as written the Cebuano means 'not tight'. Replacement: --en unwashed returns only 2 cards, and the other one, ffct-08841 EN 'if you eat unwashed vegetables or fruit' -> 'utanon o prutas nga wala hugasi', is the corpus rendering of exactly this English concept; --bis hugasi = 41 bodies, --bis hugasan = 43. Word order follows that attested postposed pattern ('nga wala hugasi', 35 postposed 'nga wala X-i' hits vs 9 preposed, none with hugasi). 'higdaanan' is the card's own word and is the corpus word for bedding (--en bedding: higdaanan 5 of 6 cards). emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang krill, gagmay nga crustacean nga morag hipon, mao ang pundasyon sa food chain sa dagat — nagsalig kaayo ang mga balyena, penguin, ug seal niini isip pagkaon.
proposals.defect: fact_en names three animals that rely on krill — whales, penguins and seals — but fact_bis renders the seal as 'selyo', which in this corpus means a stamp or safety seal, so the third animal is never named.

Replacement: --bis seal = 22 bodies with the animal kept as the English loan (ffct-08672 EN 'hunted by enemies like seals and orcas' -> 'sama sa seal ug orca'; ffct-12132 EN 'swims well to hunt seals' -> 'mangayam og seal'; ffct-11331 EN 'baby seal' -> 'anak sa seal'). The card's own tl body also uses 'seal'. One word changed; emphasis span 'pundasyon' kept verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsa ang ocean acidification?

Kon ang carbon dioxide gikan sa hangin matunaw sa dagat, mapaubos ang pH niini — nagpalisod sa mga shellfish ug coral sa paghimo sa ilang mga kabhang.
proposals.defect: fact_en says acidification makes it harder for shellfish and coral to build their SHELLS; fact_bis says 'balhibo', which is fur/feathers/body hair, and the body never names a shell.
proposals.attestation: --bis balhibo: 273 bodies, all hair/feather (ffct-00030 EN 'body hair stand up' -> 'balhibo nga motindog'; ffct-00221 EN 'birds lose their feathers' -> 'mangahulog ang balhibo sa langgam'), so it cannot carry 'shell'. Replacement kabhang: --bis kabhang = 142 bodies used for exactly this (ffct-00331 EN 'Why does a hermit crab borrow a shell?' -> 'Nganong nanghulam og kabhang ang hermit crab?'; ffct-00258 EN 'had an outer shell' -> 'naay gawas nga kabhang'), and --en shells (191 cards) ranks kabhang 65 as the top Cebuano word. One word changed; emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Makalukso ba ang toad sama sa baki?

Dili kaayo — mas mubo ang paa sa toad mao nga kasagaran mokamang lang o gamay ra molukso, lahi sa layo nga lukso sa baki.
proposals.defect: fact_en contrasts a toad with a frog, but fact_bis names the toad twice as 'kabakaba', a word no other Cebuano body in the corpus uses for any animal, so the animal being compared to the 'baki' is never named.
proposals.attestation: --bis kabakaba: 1 Cebuano body corpus-wide and it is this card itself, i.e. unsourced by the tool's own standard (it also sits in the term lists of two butterfly cards, ffct-06764 and ffct-13032). Replacement: --bis toad = 9 bodies keeping the English loan for exactly this animal, including the twin card ffct-11999 (same English title, EN 'Toads usually make short little hops... while true frogs leap much farther' -> 'Kasagaran mubo ra ang lukso sa toad sa yuta, samtang mas layo... ang lukso sa daghang tinuod nga baki') and ffct-00232 'Ang baki o toad'; --bis baki = 290 bodies, so 'baki' cannot be reused here without collapsing the contrast. The card's own tl body already uses the loan ('ng toad'). Two words changed, nothing else; emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong mas makatipig og kusog ang paglupad-lupad?

Mas makatipig og kusog ang paglupad-lupad kaysa tinuod nga paglupad kay dili na kinahanglan ikampayng mga pako.
proposals.defect: English says gliding (staying airborne without flapping) saves energy, but the Cebuano names the activity 'pagdagan-dagan' (running/scampering about), so no airborne motion is ever named on the card.
proposals.attestation: 'dagan-dagan': 0 Cebuano BODIES -- NOT ATTESTED, so the current word is unsourced. Introduced 'paglupad-lupad': 3 Cebuano bodies, all three for gliding -- ffct-01171 EN 'Gliding helps an animal escape predators' -> BIS 'Ang paglupad-lupad nagatabang sa hayop nga makaikyas sa mga manunukob'; ffct-11155 (Draco 'can glide between trees'); ffct-12398 (kagwang 'uses it to glide through the air'). Chose it over 'pagdahili' because the question sentence names no animal and 'pagdahili' is landslide/erosion in 10 of its 11 body hits, while 'paglupad-lupad' is 3/3 gliding. 'paglupad' (true flying) and 'ikampayng mga pako' left verbatim; emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsang mammal lang ang tinuod nga makalupad?

Ang kabog! Dili sama sa colugo nga modahili lang, ang kabog lamang ang mammal nga makalupad gyud.
proposals.defect: English contrasts the bat with 'the colugo, which only glides'; the Cebuano says the colugo 'nagdagan-dagan lang' (just runs around), a false claim about the colugo that the card never corrects.
proposals.attestation: 'dagan-dagan': 0 Cebuano BODIES -- NOT ATTESTED. Introduced 'modahili': 45 Cebuano bodies, the corpus's word for glide, incl. the near-identical sentence ffct-10136 EN 'a colugo can only glide downward' -> BIS 'modahili lang ang colugo paubos', and ffct-04343 which draws this exact bat/colugo contrast ('a bat flaps its wing to truly fly, while the colugo's patagium can only glide down' -> 'molupad ... modahili'). One word swapped; emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.defect: None in the body -- English 'has no ribs around its belly ... so nothing stops it from puffing up' is delivered by 'walay gusok sa tiyan ... mao nga walay makababag aron modako'.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the 'gukod' finding is a title_bis defect, out of scope here. The body already uses 'gusok', attested for ribs in 24 Cebuano bodies (ffct-00431 'The ribs protect your lungs and heart' -> 'Ang mga gusok manalipod sa baga ug kasingkasing'). Nothing to change.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Giunsa pagsaka sa tubig sa sulod sa kahoy?

Samtang moalisngaw ang tubig sa stomata, naghila kini og tubig pataas sa xylem gikan sa gamot — sama sa paghigop sa tubig gamit ang straw!
proposals.defect: English has water EVAPORATING OUT of the leaf pores, which is what pulls water up the xylem; the Cebuano 'nagsuyop ang tubig sa stomata' says water is being sucked IN at the stomata, reversing the direction and dropping evaporation entirely.
proposals.attestation: 'nagsuyop': 50 Cebuano bodies, every one of them intake/absorption (ffct-00946 'Roots soak up water' -> 'Nagsuyop ang mga gamot og tubig'; ffct-01079 plants 'nagsuyop og carbon dioxide'), so it cannot carry 'evaporates'. Introduced 'moalisngaw': 49 Cebuano bodies for evaporate (ffct-14065 'When sweat evaporates from your skin' -> 'Kon moalisngaw ang singot gikan sa panit'; ffct-14951 puddle 'evaporates into the air' -> 'moalisngaw ang tubig ngadto sa hangin'), and the exact 'samtang + evaporate' frame is attested in ffct-01291 'as sweat evaporates from our skin' -> 'samtang mo-alisngaw ang singot sa panit'. One word swapped; xylem/gamot/straw left verbatim; emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.defect: English names two plants, ginger and galangal; the Cebuano's second plant is 'lagkaw', which is not a plant name, so the galangal example is lost.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: no attested replacement exists. 'langkawas' (the galangal word the finding proposes): 0 Cebuano BODIES -- NOT ATTESTED. Bare 'galangal' as a loan: 0 Cebuano BODIES. 'lagkaw': 1 body, this card only, and --en 'galangal' returns exactly 1 card (this one), so the corpus has no galangal precedent at all to copy. Repairing would require inventing Cebuano, which Rule 2 forbids -- send to a Cebuano teacher. (Also note emphasis_bis 'rhizome' sits in this sentence.)

proposals.new_fact_bis: Panahon sa baha sa Pilipinas, usahay masagol ang hugaw sa imnonon nga tubig. Ang germs sa hugaw nga tubig makahatag og cholera ug typhoid — mao nga luwas ra imnon ang tubig kon pabukalon o paagion sa filter.
proposals.defect: English gives two safety measures, 'boiling or filtering'; the Cebuano's first measure is 'pakuanon', which is not a word for boiling, so on a flood/cholera card the child is left with filtering only.
proposals.attestation: 'pakuan' is unsourced as a verb for boil (the finding's only other corpus hit is the filler 'kuan'). Introduced 'pabukalon': 23 Cebuano bodies, and used for exactly this drinking-water-safety act -- ffct-03774 'we cook food and boil water we're unsure is clean' -> 'lutoon ang pagkaon ug pabukalon ang tubig nga dili sigurado kung limpyo'; ffct-04385 'Why should you boil water before drinking it?' -> 'Nganong kinahanglang pabukalon ang tubig una imnon?'. One word swapped; emphasis span 'cholera ug typhoid' verified present verbatim in the new text.

Editing the body would not touch the flagged defect, and emphasis span 'kemikal' would be at risk for nothing.

Send to a Cebuano teacher; the flagged 'kuko' defect is in the title anyway.

proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the 'lupad' (flies) finding is a title_bis defect, out of scope for a body repair; the body already uses 'molutaw' for float. Nothing to change.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsa ang Palawan pangolin?

Ang Palawan pangolin usa ka nagmeligro nga mananap nga adunay talagsaon nga kaliskis ug mokaon og hulmigas ug anay — sa makasubo, usa kini sa labing gipamaligya nga mananap sa kalibutan.
proposals.defect: English says the pangolin 'eats ants and termites'; the Cebuano says 'mokaon og langgam ug anay' -- langgam is BIRD in Cebuano -- so the card claims the pangolin eats birds, and ants appear nowhere on it.
proposals.attestation: 'langgam': 697 Cebuano bodies, all BIRD (ffct-00138 'A goose is a large water bird' -> 'Ang gansa usa ka dako nga langgam sa tubig'), confirming the Tagalog ant sense does not apply. Introduced 'hulmigas': 99 Cebuano bodies for ant (ffct-00105 'ants, mosquitoes, spiders' -> 'hulmigas, namok, lawalawa'), and it is the corpus's word in this exact pangolin frame -- ffct-02238 'to find ants and termites' -> 'mangita og mga hulmigas ug anay'; ffct-03009 echidna 'ants and termites' -> 'mga hulmigas ug anay'. One word swapped, 'anay' kept; emphasis span 'Palawan pangolin' verified present verbatim.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis "walay pagkampay sa pako — hinay-hinay ra monaog ang mananap samtang naglihok sa hangin" delivers everything fact_en says (no wing-flapping, slow drift down while moving through air).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is explicitly title-only (title_bis "Walay Pakpak" = without wings), and this task repairs fact_bis. The sweep itself concedes `pagdagan-dagan` for gliding is the corpus-wide rendering (colugo/flying-fish cards), so it is not a per-card defect. No word introduced.

proposals.defect: None in the body — "napulo ka tiil — walo alang sa paglakaw ug duha nga sipit" matches fact_en exactly (ten legs, eight walking, two pincers).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: defect is in title_bis only (`bitay` = hanging). Body uses `tiil` correctly and the emphasis span "napulo ka tiil" is intact; editing the body would risk the span for no gain. No word introduced.

proposals.defect: None in the body — "baga nga panit nga nagapanalipod sa buhi nga bahin niini, bisan adunay sunog sa lasang" carries thick bark shielding living tissue during a forest fire.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: `dagkot` (light/kindle) is in title_bis only; the body already uses `baga` for thick, which the finding itself accepts. No word introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa parasitism?

Sa parasitism, makabenepisyo ang parasite samtang masakitan ang host—sama sa garapata nga magsupsop sa dugo sa iro.
proposals.defect: fact_en states the parasite BENEFITS, the host is HARMED, and the tick SUCKS blood; fact_bis carried all three on hapax non-words (`makiginabaw`, `naano-ano`, `nangihap` = counting), so the defining relationship and its example were absent from the Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: `makabenepisyo` = benefits: 28 Cebuano bodies, incl. the parallel parasitism card ffct-00218 "Sa parasitismo, makabenepisyo ang parasito... samtang masakitan ang host". `masakitan` = is harmed: 28 bodies, same card. `magsupsop` = sucks: 23 bodies contain supsop; ffct-05338 is the same fact verbatim — "Ang garapata nga magsupsop sa dugo sa iro" for EN "A tick sucking a dog's blood". (--bis supsop reports 1 only because its \b anchor misses the mag- prefix; a direct regex over the pool finds 23.) Replaced words confirmed defective: `makiginabaw` 1 body, `naano-ano` 1 body, `nangihap` 1 body — all this card. `parasite`/`host`/`garapata`/`iro` kept verbatim; emphasis span "parasitism" still present.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Kanunay ba bugnaw ug danlog ang panit sa bitin?

Dili tinuod! Tungod kay cold-blooded ang bitin, gituohan sa daghan nga kanunay bugnaw ug danlog ang panit niini — apan human magpa-adlaw, init gani kini, uga ug hamis nga himbis, dili danlog.
proposals.defect: fact_en's myth is skin that is "cold and slimy" and the correction is "not slimy at all"; fact_bis rendered slimy as `pisot` (uncircumcised) in all three places, so the myth the card exists to bust was never stated or denied in Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: `danlog` = slippery/slimy: 39 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus word for exactly this predicate on animal skin — ffct-02546 "Danlog ba ang panit sa iho? ... adunay danlog nga uhog sa panit" (EN "Is shark skin slimy"), ffct-00149 fish-mucus skin, ffct-00133 pitcher-plant rim. `pisot`: 1 Cebuano body, 0 titles — this card alone. Only the three `pisot` tokens changed; emphasis span "cold-blooded" untouched and still present.

proposals.defect: The card's headline rule ("look, don't touch") IS delivered by the body — "tan-awa lang, ayaw hikapa"; only the second clause is doubtful, where EN "never grab or step on" becomes "Ayaw hikapa o tumbi".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the flagged defect (lost negation, `dali`) is in title_bis, out of scope here. The one body-level doubt, `tumbi`, is a hapax (1 body, this card) but I cannot prove from fact_en that it fails to mean "step on" — it is plausibly a regional form of `tumban`, and dialect variation is out of scope. The corpus idiom would be `ayaw tunobi` (ffct-07850 "ayaw tunobi nga walay sapin" for "never step on them barefoot"; `tunob*` 19 bodies; `matumban` also attested in ffct-04836/12333), so a Cebuano teacher can settle it cheaply. Not rewriting on an unprovable defect.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Pareho nga mokaon og hulmigas ug anay ang armadillo ug pangolin — pero mogamit ang pangolin og taas nga pilit nga dila, samtang maghukay ang armadillo gamit ang kuko ug mokaon gamit ang ordinaryong baba.
proposals.defect: fact_en says the pangolin uses a long STICKY tongue (the mechanism that catches ants); fact_bis said `lapok nga dila` = a MUDDY tongue, and nothing in the card corrects it.
proposals.attestation: `pilit` = sticky: 104 Cebuano bodies, 99 of them inside cards whose English contains "sticky"; the exact collocation for a sticky tongue is attested in ffct-00972 "mogamit og pilit nga dila" (EN "shoots out a sticky tongue"), also ffct-00098 "pilit nga laway", ffct-00538 "dili pilit nga hilo". `lapok` = mud in all 364 bodies checked (ffct-00038 mangrove mud, ffct-00430 wild pigs in mud). One word changed; no emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.defect: None in the body — "Ngano halos ngitngit ang salog sa rainforest? Kay gisala sa baga nga canopy sa ibabaw ang kadaghanan sa kahayag!" delivers dark floor, thick canopy, most sunlight stopped, less light further down.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: `mabug-at` (heavy) is in title_bis only; the body already uses `ngitngit` for dark. `gisala` (filtered/strained out) is attested 27 bodies for screening something out (ffct-03751 kidneys filtering blood, ffct-02607 barnacles straining seawater) and conveys the canopy stopping most light, so it is clumsy at worst, not a lost fact. No word introduced.

proposals.defect: None in the body — "matulog, molalin, o mausab ug motago" lists all three survival strategies fact_en gives (sleeping, travelling/migration, changing and hiding).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: `lubad` and `kaupod` are in title_bis only; the finding itself states the body lists the three strategies correctly. No word introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang mga detritivore sama sa ipis ug millipede mokaon og patay nga butang ug gisi-gisonon kini sa gagmay nga tipik aron paspas nga mabungkag sa bakterya.
proposals.defect: fact_en names the detritivores as cockroaches and MILLIPEDES; fact_bis said `ulahipan`, the centipede — a predator — so the Cebuano teaches that centipedes eat dead matter, the opposite of the corpus's own centipede cards.
proposals.attestation: The corpus never coins a native Cebuano word for millipede: it keeps the English inside Cebuano bodies — `millipede` 40 Cebuano bodies, 18 titles (ffct-00135, ffct-00644, ffct-02591 "ang hinay nga millipede mokaon og malata nga tanom"), and reserves `alupihan` (41 bodies) for the centipede, contrasted explicitly in ffct-01041 "Unsay kalahian sa millipede ug alupihan?". `ulahipan` is a hapax: 1 body, this card. One word changed; emphasis span "detritivore" still present.

proposals.defect: None in the body — "Ang panghuyab usa ka lawom nga pagginhawa nga mopuno sa imong baga og dugang nga hangin!" is exactly fact_en.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: `hiyaw` (a shout) is in title_bis only; the body uses `panghuyab` for yawn correctly, as the finding concedes. No word introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang gagmayng bakterya sama sa E. coli morag gagmayng trabahante — dali silang paladakon sa mga syentista ug ma-engineer aron makahimo og tambal, protina, ug enzymes!
proposals.defect: fact_en says the bacteria are reprogrammed to make MEDICINES; fact_bis said "makahimo og gamot", and in Cebuano `gamot` is a plant ROOT, so the Cebuano-only reader is told E. coli is engineered to make roots.
proposals.attestation: `gamot`: 495 Cebuano bodies, and a direct check of their English shows 487 are about roots versus 7 about medicine — the corpus's own sense is overwhelmingly ROOT (ffct-00038 mangrove roots, ffct-00053 "Ang gamot mao ang nagasuyop og tubig"). `tambal` = medicine: 285 Cebuano bodies, used for manufactured medicine exactly as needed here (ffct-00137 "Ang antibiotic usa ka tambal", ffct-00225 antibiotics as `tambal`). Caveat recorded: the Tagalog-ism `gamot`-for-medicine does recur in a handful of bodies (e.g. ffct-04469 "paghimo og gamot, bakuna, ug antibiotics"), so this is a disambiguation toward the corpus norm rather than a nonce-word fix; only the one word changed, no emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_en's claim (eye snaps shut fast as a protective reflex, before you decide) is delivered by fact_bis ("kusog nga mopiyong ang mata nga paspas kaayo isip reflex aron manalipod, bisan dili nimo tuyo").
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is explicitly title-only ("kislap" is in title_bis, not fact_bis) and title_bis is not the field under repair. Body word 'piyong/mopiyong' is attested for closing the eyes (ceb_usage.py --bis piyong: 3 bodies, ffct-03116 "Sulayi og piyong ang usa ka mata" = "Try closing one eye", ffct-04242, ffct-09614), so nothing in the body needs changing.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_en (a color blind person may struggle with traffic lights or telling if fruit is ripe by color) is fully delivered by fact_bis, which says "ilaw sa trapiko" and "hinog na ba ang prutas pinaagi sa kolor".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the 'sugnod' (firewood) substitution the finding describes occurs only in title_bis; the sweep itself concedes "Body is correct (\"ilaw sa trapiko\")". No fact_bis defect is provable from fact_en, so no word was introduced and no lookup was needed.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_en (each sex cell gets half the chromosomes, one from each pair in the parent cell) is delivered verbatim in sense by fact_bis: "makadawat lamang og katunga sa kromosoma — usa lang sa matag paris gikan sa selula sa ginikanan".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: 'kalimot' (forgetting) appears only in title_bis; the body already uses 'katunga' for half, which the finding itself confirms is correct. Nothing in fact_bis is refutable against fact_en, so no replacement word was introduced.

proposals.defect: None that is provable in the body — fact_en (birds use feather color to hide from enemies or to attract a mate with bright colors) is delivered by fact_bis, which already uses 'balhibo' for feathers, 'motago gikan sa kaaway' for hiding, and 'makadani og kapikas gamit ang hayag nga kolor' for attracting a mate.

The only residual gaps are 'duha ka paagi' (two ways) for "two reasons" and the unrendered "by blending in" — register/compression, not a wrong fact, and repairing them would mean adding words rather than correcting them, which MINIMAL EDITS forbids.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang yogurt adunay aslom nga lami ug texture tungod sa duha ka klase sa bakterya — ang Lactobacillus bulgaricus ug Streptococcus thermophilus — nga magtinabangay sa paghimo niini.
proposals.defect: fact_en says yogurt's taste is TANGY (sour), but fact_bis says "pait nga lami" = bitter, a different taste that nothing later in the card corrects.
proposals.attestation: One word introduced: 'aslom'. ceb_usage.py --bis aslom = 88 Cebuano bodies, all sour/tangy (ffct-00775 "Nganong aslom ang yogurt?" for EN "Why is yogurt sour?"; ffct-02514 lists the five tastes as "tam-is, aslom, parat, pait, ug umami", which separately confirms 'pait' = bitter, not tangy). ceb_usage.py --en tangy returns 6 cards and 'aslom' is the top content word (4 hits) — ffct-08966 renders EN "sour, tangy taste" as "aslom nga lami" and dcard-10888 renders EN "thick, tangy food" (yogurt) as "baga ug aslom nga pagkaon". The exact phrase "aslom nga lami" occurs in 5 Cebuano bodies (ffct-00775, 08966, 10276, 16788, 19316). Only 'pait'→'aslom' changed; emphasis span "Lactobacillus bulgaricus" is present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Pila ka hulmigas ang mahimong mopuyo sa usa ka kolonya?

Ang usa ka kolonya sa leafcutter ant mahimong adunay hangtod walo ka milyon ka mga trabahante nga hulmigas, nga nagpuyo sa ilawom sa yuta nga nag-abot og 30 ka square meters!
proposals.defect: fact_en counts ANTS ("How many ants…", "eight million worker ants"), but fact_bis says 'langgam' twice, which in Cebuano is a BIRD — the card asserts eight million worker birds in underground tunnels.
proposals.attestation: One word introduced: 'hulmigas'. ceb_usage.py --bis langgam = 697 bodies, uniformly bird (ffct-00138 goose, ffct-00196 nest-building bird), confirming the false friend. ceb_usage.py --en "ant colony" = 16 cards with 'hulmigas' the top word (21 hits); ffct-03925 is the near-twin of this card — EN "How many ants can live in one colony?" → "Pila ka hulmigas ang naa sa usa ka kolonya?" — which attests the exact question frame. ceb_usage.py --bis hulmigas = 99 bodies. The worker phrasing is attested too: "trabahante nga hulmigas" in 3 bodies (ffct-05449, 05608, 07936), "trabahanteng hulmigas" in 3 more (ffct-00398, 02652, 04501), and ffct-00982 uses the identical frame for wasps ("trabahante nga putakti"). Only the two 'langgam' tokens changed; emphasis span "walo ka milyon" is present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Naay tunok ba ang makahiya?

Wala diay tunok sa tangkay niini! Gipanalipdan sa makahiya ang kaugalingon pinaagi sa dali nga pagtiklop sa mga dahon kon mahikap nimo kini.
proposals.defect: fact_en says the makahiya protects itself by quickly FOLDING its leaves, but fact_bis says "pag-uyog sa mga dahon" = by shaking/vibrating them, which is a different mechanism and is the card's only fact.
proposals.attestation: One word introduced: 'pagtiklop'. ceb_usage.py --bis uyog = 216 bodies and the sense is vibrate/shake/rock throughout (ffct-01639 sound is "pag-uyog"; ffct-02659 vibrating air; ffct-09577 a ripple in water), so 'uyog' cannot carry "fold". ceb_usage.py --bis pagtiklop = 3 Cebuano bodies and all three are makahiya-folding cards: ffct-12879 contains the exact target string "ang pagtiklop sa mga dahon sa makahiya" for EN "a makahiya's leaves fold", plus ffct-08566 and ffct-13010. The finite form is corroborated by --bis motiklop = 8 bodies (ffct-02884 "kapaspas motiklop" for EN "how fast it folds up", ffct-02182). ceb_usage.py --en makahiya also ranks 'motiklop/mutiklop' (10+10) among the corpus's words for this plant. Note 'tikom' was checked and rejected: NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY. Only 'pag-uyog'→'pagtiklop' changed; emphasis span "tunok" is present verbatim (twice).

proposals.defect: fact_en says the manta ray has two horn-like FINS on its head, but fact_bis says "morag-sungay nga bagolbagol sa ulo" = horn-like SKULLS on its head — a different body part.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: emphasis constraint, not doubt about the defect. emphasis_bis is ["morag-sungay nga bagolbagol"] and the defective word sits inside the span, so any correction destroys the exact-substring match and silently kills the bold at render time; the rule says keep the span verbatim or HOLD, and keeping it verbatim means keeping the error. For the record the corpus confirms both sides — ceb_usage.py --bis bagolbagol = 7 bodies, every one the skull (ffct-03252 brain/helmet, ffct-04633 "gahi nga bukog sa ulo", ffct-02849 skull bones); ceb_usage.py --bis kapay = 61 bodies for fish fins (ffct-01620 "Ang mga kapay sa kilid ug likod sa isda" for EN "The fins on a fish's sides and back"). So the fix ('bagolbagol'→'kapay') is known and attested; it needs the span updated alongside the text, which is a job for the Cebuano teacher with edit rights to emphasis_bis.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga daghan pang naluwas ang anunugba nga kolor-kahoy?

Kay lisod sila makita sa langgam! Ang anunugba nga kolor mohaom sa panit sa kahoy mao nga mas daghan ang maluwas ug manganak — mao kini ang natural selection.
proposals.defect: fact_en is about MOTHS that survive and reproduce, but fact_bis twice names 'anuplos', the stinging hairy caterpillar (Tagalog higad) — a different animal and a different life stage from the one the English says reproduces.
proposals.attestation: One word introduced: 'anunugba'. ceb_usage.py --bis anuplos = 1 Cebuano body, and that one body is this card itself, so it has no independent corpus support. ceb_usage.py --bis anunugba = 22 bodies, all unambiguously moth: ffct-03405 "Ang anunugba usa ka insekto nga kasagaran molupad sa gabii ug madani sa kahayag" for EN "A moth is an insect that usually flies at night and is drawn to light"; ffct-00875 moths around lamps; ffct-03195 moths hearing bats; ffct-01201 pairs it with 'alibangbang' for EN "butterflies and moths". ceb_usage.py --en moth ranks 'anunugba' as the leading Cebuano animal word across those cards (29 hits). 'langgam' in the second sentence is left alone because fact_en really does say "Birds can't spot them!". Only the two 'anuplos' tokens changed; emphasis span "natural selection" is present verbatim.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_en (nutmeg spice comes from the dried seed inside the nutmeg tree's fruit, prized for its warm fragrant flavor) is delivered by fact_bis: "usa ka panimpla nga gikan sa uga nga liso sulod sa bunga sa kahoy nga nutmeg — ilado tungod sa humot ug init nga lami niini".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the 'paminta' (black pepper) mis-categorisation is in title_bis only, and the sweep concedes "this is title-only". The body already uses 'panimpla' for spice. No fact_bis defect is provable from fact_en, so no word was introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga paryente ang coral ug dikya?

Kay ang galamay sa coral polyp adunay gagmayng manunusok nga selula — sama sa gamayng pana — nga gigamit sa pagdakop ug pagpaalup sa gagmayng tukbonon, sama sa dikya!
proposals.defect: fact_en asks why coral and jellyfish are RELATIVES (kin), but fact_bis asks "Ngano nga managhigala ang coral ug dikya?" = why they are FRIENDS, replacing a kinship claim with a nonsense social one.
proposals.attestation: One word introduced: 'paryente'. ceb_usage.py --bis managhigala = only 3 Cebuano bodies (this card, ffct-02117, ffct-09878), all three cases of the same English word "relatives", so it has no independent support as a kinship term; higala is 'friend'. ceb_usage.py --bis paryente = 82 bodies, all kinship/taxonomic relatedness (ffct-00485 termites are "paryente … sa ipis, dili sa hulmigas" for EN "actually [relatives of] cockroaches"; ffct-00717 dugong "duol nga paryente sa manatee" for EN "close relative"; ffct-00246 scorpion "paryente kini sa lawalawa"). ceb_usage.py --en "are.{0,15}related" makes 'paryente' the top word across those 20 cards, and ffct-06340 attests the exact question frame — EN "Are pangolins and armadillos related?" → "Paryente ba ang pangolin ug armadillo?"; the near-twin coral card ffct-02209 renders EN "They're relatives of jellyfish" as "Kaparyente kini sa dikya". proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong kataw-anan ug matayog ang imong boses human moginhawa og helium?

Mas gaan ang helium kaysa hangin, mao nga mas paspas ang tunog! Nagpataas kini sa pitch sa boses, nga kataw-anan!
proposals.defect: fact_en asks why your voice sounds funny "after breathing helium", but the Cebuano "pagkahaplos og helium" says after STROKING/TOUCHING it (haplos = touch with the palm), and no other line in the body mentions breathing or inhaling, so the card names a mechanism that is simply false.
proposals.attestation: The corpus renders this exact concept with ginhawa, not haplos: ffct-15815 EN "Why does breathing helium make your voice sound squeaky?" -> BIS "kung moginhawa og helium". ceb_usage.py --en breathing (198 cards) ranks pagginhawa 95 / moginhawa 37 / ginhawa 36 as the characteristic words; --bis moginhawa = 114 bodies (ffct-00416 "malisod moginhawa" for "hard to breathe", ffct-00431 "matag moginhawa ka" for "each time you breathe in"). I checked and rejected singhot: --bis singhot = 0 bodies, NOT ATTESTED, so it may not be used. "human" for EN "after" is attested at --bis human = 853 bodies in the same pre-verb shape, e.g. ffct-00112 "human manghugas" for "after washing". Only "pagkahaplos" changed; no emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Bisan dili nato makita ang hangin, nahibaloan nato nga anaa kini! Mabation nato kini sa paghuyop sa hangin, nagpadako kini sa balloon, ug nagpugong kini sa tubig sa nakabaliktad nga baso.
proposals.defect: fact_en's third proof is an "upside-down glass", but the Cebuano "nakatungkab nga baso" says a PRIED-OPEN/broken-into glass (tungkab = to pry open), so the inverted-glass demo the child is meant to picture is not on the card.
proposals.attestation: tungkab: ceb_usage.py --bis tungkab = 0 Cebuano bodies, NOT ATTESTED (the only occurrence in the whole corpus is this card's own "nakatungkab"), so it cannot vouch for "upside-down". baliktad: --bis baliktad = 20 bodies / 33 titles, all inverted (ffct-11516 "mokaon ... baliktad" for "eats upside down", ffct-13288 "Baliktad ba ang hulagway sa mata nimo?" for "Does your eye see things upside-down?", ffct-13767 "bisan baliktad" for "even upside down"); the exact form I use is attested as well, --bis nakabaliktad = 2 bodies, ffct-00294 "Dili tanang larva sa lamok nakabaliktad" for EN "Not all mosquito larvae hang upside-down". One word changed; no emphasis spans on this card. Note left for the teacher: fact_en's "underwater" is still absent, but restoring it would mean adding text beyond the defective word.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa tradisyonal nga langis sa niyog?

Pinaagi sa pagkulo sa gata! Samang nagkulo, ang tubig nagsingaw ug ang langis nabilin. Kini naggamit og evaporation aron ihiwalay ang langis gikan sa tubig.
proposals.defect: fact_en answers that coconut oil is made "by boiling COCONUT MILK", but the Cebuano answer line says "pagkulo sa gatas" — boiling (animal) milk — and the method is the entire answer of the card.
proposals.attestation: The corpus keeps gata (coconut milk) and gatas (animal milk) apart, and ffct-07620 states the distinction outright: EN "Are coconut water and coconut milk the same?" -> BIS "Managsama ba ang tubig sa buko ug ang gata?". Standalone \bgata\b = 25 Cebuano bodies, all coconut milk (ffct-00141 "giluto sa gata" for "cooked in coconut milk", ffct-02442 "Ang gata sa lubi" for "Coconut milk", ffct-05644 "tam-is nga gata" for "sweet coconut milk"), while gatas in bodies is animal milk (ffct-00339 "nagapasuso ... og gatas", ffct-00078 milk and small fish for calcium). One letter changed; emphasis span "evaporation" untouched and still present verbatim.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis carries all of fact_en — limescale inside kettles, calcium and magnesium dissolved in hard water, and the minerals left behind as a solid deposit when the water evaporates.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is against title_bis "Tulo sa Takure" only, and only fact_bis can be returned here. The body keeps the English keyword "limescale" verbatim, and the emphasis span "limescale" would be at risk from any needless rewording, so the body is held as-is.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong nagiging malutong ang okoy?

Kini nga prito nga hipon ug utanon giluto sa init kaayo nga mantika, nga magpauga sa gawas aron mahimong malutong!
proposals.defect: The English names the outcome "crispy" twice (question and answer), but the Cebuano says "kuyamis" both times, which is not the word this corpus uses for crispy anywhere else.
proposals.attestation: ceb_usage.py --bis kuyamis -> 1 Cebuano BODY, 0 titles, and that single body is this card itself (ffct-18611), so it is self-vouching and unsourced. Replacement word 'malutong': --bis malutong -> 8 Cebuano BODIES for crisp/crunchy (ffct-08386 'malutong, tubigon nga unod' = 'crisp, watery flesh'; ffct-12419 'malutong ug presko' = 'crunchy, juicy'). --en crispy -> 18 cards; the closest parallel is ffct-17999 EN 'This dries out the skin and turns it crispy' BIS 'Mamala ug malutong ang panit', and ffct-18086 EN 'golden brown and crispy on the outside' BIS 'mahimong kayumanggi ug malutong ang gawas' -- the exact 'mahimong ... malutong' frame this edit uses. Only the two occurrences of the defective word were changed; the Tagalog-flavoured 'nagiging' was LEFT ALONE (it is attested in 7 Cebuano bodies incl. ffct-15815, ffct-18000, and it is not a meaning defect). Emphasis span 'init kaayo nga mantika' is present verbatim in the new text (verified by substring check).

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga mo-yellow ug mo-tam-is ang mga mangga sa Guimaras kung mahinog?

Adunay kemikal nga pag-usab kung mahinog! Nag-convert kini sa starch ngadto sa simple nga asukal.
proposals.defect: The English makes ripening the condition for the yellowing/sweetening and for the chemical change ("as they ripen"), but the Cebuano says "kung mamala" (when they dry out) in both places, naming drying as the cause instead.
proposals.attestation: ceb_usage.py --bis mamala -> 55 Cebuano BODIES, every one of them 'dry/dry out' (ffct-02319 EN 'waits for them to dry'; ffct-08712 EN 'dries it out as the water inside escapes'; ffct-08849 EN 'When the salt dries'). Replacement 'mahinog': --bis mahinog -> 21 Cebuano BODIES meaning ripen (ffct-00272 EN 'Where does a peanut actually ripen?' BIS 'Asa gyud mahinog ang mani?'; ffct-02910 EN 'when it ripens it turns red' BIS 'kon mahinog na kini mahimong pula'). --en ripen -> 62 cards, top Cebuano words hinog 28 / mahinog 18 / mohinog 11, and ffct-00620 EN 'As fruit ripens' BIS 'Samtang mahinog ang prutas'. Only the verb changed; the card's own 'kung' particle, wording, and all facts/units kept. No emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Kung initan ang solid butter, ang molecules makakuha ug igo nga enerhiya aron mabungkag ang hugot nga structure ug mo-flow isip liquid!
proposals.defect: The English says "When you add heat to solid butter", but the Cebuano says "Kung pasabugan" (when it is blown up/scattered), so heat -- the entire cause of melting -- appears nowhere in the Cebuano body.
proposals.attestation: ceb_usage.py --bis pasabugan -> 1 Cebuano BODY, 0 titles, and that body is this card itself (ffct-19921): unsourced. Replacement 'initan': --bis initan -> 20 Cebuano BODIES, all 'when heated', including the exact melting frame -- ffct-14923 EN 'When heated or cooled, solid melts to liquid' BIS 'Kung initan o bugnawon, matunaw ang solid ngadto sa liquid'; also ffct-14933 'Ngano modako ang mga butang kung initan' (EN 'when heated'), ffct-15807 'kung initan ang likido' (EN 'when the liquid is heated'), ffct-15981 'Kung initan, mas paspas molihok ang mga particle' (EN 'When heated'). Cross-check --en 'add heat' -> 4 cards; the sibling ffct-15963 renders it 'dugangan kini og kainit', which confirms the concept but is a larger diff than the one-word 'initan', so the single-word swap was taken. One word changed, nothing else. No emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Pila ka kilo ang kayang i-lift sa usa ka cubic meter sa helium gas?

Mas gaan kaysa hangin ang helium gas, mao nga usa ka cubic meter makaalsa og mga usa ka kilo!
proposals.defect: The English says one cubic metre can LIFT roughly one kilogram, but the Cebuano says "makapabug-at og mga usa ka kilo" (makes about a kilo heavy), reversing the buoyancy fact and contradicting "mas gaan kaysa hangin" in the same sentence.
proposals.attestation: Replacement 'makaalsa': ceb_usage.py --bis makaalsa -> 8 Cebuano BODIES, all 'can lift', in the same 'makaalsa og <load>' frame this edit uses -- ffct-22465 EN 'a lever can lift something much heavier' BIS 'makaalsa og butang nga mas bug-at pa'; ffct-07019 EN 'it can hold up a heavy object' BIS 'makaalsa kini og bug-at nga butang'; ffct-25716 EN 'A small effort ... lifts a heavy load' BIS 'makaalsa sa bug-at nga butang'. Cross-check --en lift -> 389 cards with 'pag-alsa' (62) among the most characteristic Cebuano words (ffct-00154 EN 'to lift it' BIS 'aron alsahon'). The repair also matches the card's own question stem 'kayang i-lift'. One word changed; the number, unit and the rest of the sentence untouched. No emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.defect: The English says water EXPANDS when it freezes, while the Cebuano says "Mogawas ang tubig" (the water comes out/escapes) -- a different, physically false mechanism that also contradicts the next clause about sealed bottles bursting.
proposals.attestation: HOLD on the emphasis-span rule, not on doubt about the defect. emphasis_bis is exactly ["Mogawas"], i.e. the single defective word IS the bolded span, and spans render by exact substring match. Any correct repair (e.g. the sibling wording 'Mo-expand' in ffct-19920/ffct-19946) deletes 'Mogawas' from the body and silently kills the bold, and there is no truthful sentence that keeps 'Mogawas' verbatim, since nothing escapes a closed bottle. proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang solid modeling clay pwede hulmahon og bag-ong shapes! Magpabilin kini nga solid kay dili mausab ang iyang definite volume.
proposals.defect: EN says the clay can be MOLDED into new shapes, but the Cebuano verb hubaron means untie/unplug/interpret, so the body never states the molding action.
proposals.attestation: hubaron: --bis hubar = 5 bodies, all non-molding senses (ffct-22148 'hubaron kini sa atong utok' = brain INTERPRETS; ffct-24478 'hubaron ang TV' = UNPLUG; dcard-05255 'ipasabot o hubaron' = interpret). Replacement hulmahon: --bis hulmahon = 23 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus word for exactly this English concept — ffct-16413 EN 'can be shaped, blown, or molded' -> BIS 'mahimong hulmahon, huypan, o porma-on'; ffct-06425 EN 'easy to shape into different forms' -> BIS 'sayon kining hulmahon sa lain-laing porma'; ffct-15056 'ang salamin mahimong huypan o hulmahon'. Frame 'pwede + -on verb' is attested (13 bodies: 'pwede dakpon' ffct-00047, 'pwede gamiton' ffct-17466, 'pwede usbon' ffct-20266). Only the one verb changed; no emphasis span on this card.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Kung ibutang ang mga lansang nga puthaw sa ulan, mo-react kini sa oxygen ug mahimong bag-ong substance nga kalawang!
proposals.defect: EN's rusting object is iron NAILS, but the Cebuano says 'mga pako nga puthaw', and pako in Cebuano is a wing/fern, so the body rusts a different object.

Replacement lansang: --bis lansang = 44 bodies, and it is the corpus word in this card's own rust set — ffct-15177 'ang lansang sa tubig' EN 'a nail in water', ffct-16425 EN 'Which nail rusts in the jar experiment' -> 'Unsa nga lansang ang motaya', ffct-16426 'lansang samtang motaya'. The exact phrase 'lansang nga puthaw' for EN 'iron nail' = 4 bodies (ffct-16309 'solido nga lansang nga puthaw' EN 'a solid iron nail'), and the plural 'mga lansang nga puthaw' for EN 'iron nails' = dcard-02384. proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo ngano nga parat kaayo ang West Philippine Sea?

Kini usa ka homogeneous mixture! Ang sodium chloride nag-dissolve gyud sa liquid water, mao nga perpekto ang sagol.
proposals.defect: EN asks why the West Philippine Sea is so SALTY; the Cebuano asks why it is 'asalom' (sour), so the body's premise is a different taste than the dissolved-salt fact that answers it.
proposals.attestation: asalom: --bis asalom = 1 body, which is this card itself (self-vouching, so unattested). The nearest real word aslom = 88 bodies, all SOUR (ffct-00775 'Nganong aslom ang yogurt' EN 'Why is yogurt sour'; ffct-00780 calamansi 'gamay ug aslom nga prutas' EN 'small, sour citrus'; ffct-02085 burong isda). Replacement parat: --bis parat = 176 bodies and is the corpus word for English salty — ffct-00602 EN 'What does salty taste like' -> 'Unsa man ang lami nga parat'; ffct-00245 EN 'too much salty food' -> 'sobra nga parat'; ffct-00955 EN 'salty water' -> 'parat nga tubig'. Collocation 'parat kaayo' = 10 bodies (ffct-10112). One word changed; the paragraph break and the emphasis_bis span 'homogeneous mixture' are present verbatim (verified by substring check).

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang HEPA air filters modakop sa solid dust particles ug pollen gikan sa indoor air gas mixture!
proposals.defect: EN says HEPA filters TRAP dust particles and pollen, but the Cebuano verb mopakpak means to flap/clap (pakpak = wing), so the card's only fact — the trapping — is absent.
