Replacement modakop: --bis modakop = 62 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus word for trapping dust specifically — ffct-01025 EN 'traps dust and germs' -> BIS 'modakop sa abog ug mikrobyo'; ffct-01943 EN 'trapping germs and dust' -> 'modakop sa mikrobyo ug abog'; ffct-01084 'modakop og mikrobyo' for filtering germs. Frame 'modakop sa' = 28 bodies, so the existing 'sa' needs no change. --en trap ranks nagdakop/dakop family top-25 across 426 cards. One word swapped; emphasis_bis span 'HEPA air filters' kept verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Kung mo-decompose ang mga nahulog nga dahon sa narra sa yuta, moagi kini og chemical change aron mahimong nutrient-rich organic compost!
proposals.defect: EN says the decomposing leaves 'undergo a chemical change to become' compost, but the Cebuano drops the chemical-change clause entirely, leaving only 'leaves rot into compost' — the card's curriculum point is unrecoverable.
proposals.attestation: Clause restored with the corpus's own wording for this exact English, from the nearest sibling: ffct-19731 EN 'fallen mango leaves rotting... They undergo a chemical change as microbes break them down' -> BIS 'Nag-agi kini og chemical change samtang...'; ffct-20128 'moagi og chemical change nga gitawag og tarnishing'; ffct-19924 'nag-agi og chemical change nga gitawag og decomposition'. Phrase 'moagi og chemical change' = 6 bodies. --bis moagi = 659 bodies. Purpose frame 'aron mahimong' = 379 bodies, and it renders this same 'undergo a change to become X' shape in ffct-20013 EN 'undergoes a physical change to become solid basalt rock' -> 'mo-undergo og physical change aron mahimong solid basalt rock'. proposals.defect: The English forbids two places during lightning — "Never stand under tall trees or in open fields" — but the Cebuano forbids only the trees; the open-field prohibition is dropped entirely and no other sentence restores it.
proposals.attestation: Introduced "o sa hawan nga dapit", taken verbatim from the corpus's own rendering of this exact English clause in the sibling lightning card ffct-30664: EN "Never stand under a tree or in an open field during a storm." -> BIS "Ayaw pagtindog ilalom sa kahoy o sa hawan nga dapit panahon sa bagyo." (ceb_usage.py --en "open field"). Word checks: --bis hawan = 28 Cebuano BODIES (e.g. ffct-08734 "itanom ang punla sa hawan nga mga dapit"); --bis dapit = 561 bodies. I deliberately did NOT touch "Pag-ingat sa sulod sa balay" although the sweep also flagged it: --bis ingat shows it is attested in Cebuano bodies (ffct-28533 "mag-ingat sa pagpreno", ffct-36015 "busa pag-ingat"), fact_tl reads the same way ("Mag-ingat sa loob ng bahay na may bubong"), and "stay safe inside a house with a roof" delivers the English clumsily — Rule 1 says leave it. emphasis_bis span "kilat" is untouched and still matches verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Gipakita ni Galileo nga ang bug-at ug gaan nga mga butang mahulog nga dungan kung walay hangin nga mobabag!
proposals.defect: The English condition is that no air SLOWS the objects down (air resistance is absent); the Cebuano "walay hangin nga moabag" says no air HELPS them, inverting the role of air — abag is to assist, so the child is told air helps things fall.
proposals.attestation: One word changed, 'moabag' -> 'mobabag'. ceb_usage.py --bis mobabag: 41 Cebuano BODIES in exactly the obstruct/block sense (ffct-07401 "mas mobabag sa agianan sa hangin" / EN "block the airway"; ffct-07956 "mobabag sa kahayag sa adlaw" / EN "block the sun"; ffct-10890 "ang nalit-ag nga hangin mobabag sa katugnaw" / EN "that trapped air blocks the cold"), against 'moabag' which appears in exactly 1 body — this card itself (--en "air slows" shows the same). The card's fact_tl confirms the intended sense: "kapag walang hangin na humahadlang". emphasis_bis span "mahulog nga dungan" is untouched and still matches verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang kubing usa ka nindot nga lumad nga instrumento gikan sa Mindanao! Gigamit sa pagsugilanon, pangulitawo, ug pagpahulay, kini nindot nga panig-ingnan sa physics sa tunog sa kulturang Pilipino.
proposals.defect: The English lists the kubing's uses as "storytelling, courtship, and relaxation"; the Cebuano's middle item, 'panguliyaw', is shouting/hollering, not courtship, so the list names a use the English does not have and drops the one it does.
proposals.attestation: One word changed, 'panguliyaw' -> 'pangulitawo', taken from the corpus's rendering of this exact English concept on the sibling kubing card: ceb_usage.py --bis pangulitawo -> ffct-23794 BIS "ang kubing gigamit sa pangulitawo" / EN "the kubing is used for courtship" (1 body, 1 title). --en courtship corroborates the courtship field generally (ffct-00665 "panahon sa panguyab" / EN "courtship season"; ffct-07095 "aron manguyab" / EN "to court"), while 'panguliyaw' occurs in 1 body only — this card — and --bis guliyaw returns 0 bodies. fact_tl says "panliligaw". emphasis_bis span "kubing" is untouched and still matches verbatim.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis says the feathers (balhibo) press together on the downstroke and open slightly on the upstroke, which is exactly what fact_en says.
proposals.attestation: HOLD: the sweep's own finding scopes the defect to title_bis ("Buhok sa Hangin"), and I am repairing fact_bis. The body already uses balhibo for "feathers" twice (`--bis balhibo` = 509 Cebuano bodies), so nothing in fact_bis is refutable against fact_en. Title repair belongs to the title pass, not here.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis states that a trip that once took months by ship now takes only hours, matching fact_en's claim about planes changing travel.
proposals.attestation: HOLD: the finding is explicitly title-only ("Eroplano sa wala pa Barko" turns a speed comparison into chronology) and the finding itself says "the body is correct". Checking fact_bis against fact_en confirms it: kaniadto mag-abot og mga bulan pinaagi sa barko / mahimo na sa pipila lang ka oras / layong mga nasod all map onto the English. Nothing to rewrite in fact_bis.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Matag balik sa kahayag sulod sa tinulo, naay gamay nga mogawas. Tungod kay duha ka balik ang kinahanglan sa ikaduhang bahaghari, gamay na lang ang nabilin — mao nga mas luya kini!
proposals.defect: fact_en concludes the second rainbow always looks DIMMER, but fact_bis ended "mas labong kini" — labong is lush/thick in Cebuano, so the Cebuano asserted the opposite of the card's only claim and contradicted its own preceding clause ("gamay na lang ang nabilin").
proposals.attestation: One word changed: labong -> luya. `--bis labong` meaning confirmed by corpus bodies that use it for lushness (ffct-00393 bamboo shoot, ffct-13102 "mas labong nga berde", ffct-29010 "labong nga kalasangan") — never for faintness. `--bis luya` = 53 Cebuano bodies, and `--en dimmer` shows the corpus using it for exactly this concept: ffct-30798 "nagtabon sa luya nga mga bituon" = "hide the dimmer stars". The two sibling rainbow cards use the same word for the same English "faint": ffct-23948 "Mao nga mas luya ug mas taas kini sa langit" (EN "looks fainter") and ffct-23955 "luya na kaayo ang kolor" (EN "colors become very faint"). emphasis_bis span "duha ka balik" is untouched and still present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong adunay friction bisan sa hamis nga nawong?

Bisan morag hamis, adunay gagmay nga umbok ug lawom ang mga nawong kung tan-awon pag-ayo! Kung magdausdos, magsangit kining gagmay nga umbok, mao nga maglisod molihok — mao kana ang friction!
proposals.defect: fact_en's mechanism is that surfaces have tiny BUMPS that catch on each other, but fact_bis called them "libtong" (a deep pool/hollow — a dip, not a bump), so the raised feature that does the catching is never named in Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: One word changed, in both of its occurrences: libtong -> umbok. `--bis libtong` = 1 Cebuano body, and that one body is THIS card (ffct-24123) — i.e. the word is unsourced everywhere else in 47,056 cards. `--bis umbok` = 8 Cebuano bodies, all for a raised lump (ffct-05247 Adam's apple "bump in your neck", ffct-05293 "bumps of bone", ffct-10172/ffct-12384 camel's hump, ffct-31763 tidal "bulges"). Decisive precedent: the corpus's own friction twin ffct-22978 renders the identical English "tiny bumps and dips on surfaces ... they catch on each other" as "gagmay nga umbok ug buho sa nawong! Magsangit kini...". `--en "tiny bumps"` also ranks umbok/bukol as the corpus words for this concept. I left "lawom" (for "dips") alone: clumsy but it still delivers the depressions, and minimal-diff applies. emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang magnet mobira lang og puthaw sama sa lansang, pero ang static charge makabira og papel, buhok, o tubig! Lahi sila nga puwersa.
proposals.defect: fact_en's one example of iron is "nails", but fact_bis said "puthaw sama sa pako" — pako is WING in Cebuano, so the card's only concrete instance of a magnetic object reads as "iron like a wing" and is never corrected in the two-sentence body.
proposals.attestation: One word changed: pako -> lansang. `--bis pako` = 359 Cebuano bodies and every sampled one is a wing/fin/fern (ffct-00006 bat wings, ffct-00021 bee wings, ffct-00405 "pako sa kabog"), never a nail. `--bis lansang` = 44 Cebuano bodies used precisely for nails, including iron nails: ffct-16309 "solido nga lansang nga puthaw" (EN "a solid iron nail"), ffct-12617 "gamay nga lansang" (EN "a small nail"), ffct-15177 nail-in-water rusting experiment. ffct-23115 even pairs it with this card's domain ("kupot sa tornilyo kaysa sa lansang"). emphasis_bis span "static charge" is untouched and still present verbatim.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis says the feathers close on the downstroke to catch air and part slightly on the upstroke so air slips through without dragging, which is what fact_en says.
proposals.attestation: HOLD: the finding is title-only ("Buhok sa Downstroke"), and the finding itself concedes "the body correctly uses [balhibo] twice". Re-derived against fact_en: magsira/madakpan ang hangin, moabli og gamay, moagi ang hangin nga dili mobira all match. No defect is provable in fact_bis.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis names the seesaw, calls it a real lever, identifies the middle resting point as the fulcrum and states that one end goes down as the other goes up, i.e. everything fact_en says.
proposals.attestation: HOLD: the sip-sip (= to suck, per ffct-16285 "Kung mosipsip ka sa straw") defect is confined to title_bis; fact_bis says "Ang seesaw sa lingawan usa ka tinuod nga lever", using the same loanword every other seesaw card in the corpus uses. emphasis_bis span "lever" is present in the unchanged text. Nothing in fact_bis to repair.

proposals.defect: Arguably none — fact_en itself writes "A kite or bati", so the body's "bati ... gipugong sa pisi" delivers the English term the card offers; only the un-rendered "tilted" is missing, which is an omission rather than a wrong word.
proposals.attestation: HOLD: the langgam (= bird) error is in title_bis, not fact_bis. I cannot rewrite the body without either (a) inventing a kite word — `--bis tabanog`/saranggola do not appear in this card and substituting them would be retranslation, not a minimal fix — or (b) adding "tilted", which would be adding a fact-bearing word the body never had. The body's own key term "bati" is licensed by fact_en verbatim. Title repair plus the missing "tilted" nuance is exactly the kind of judgement call that belongs with a Cebuano teacher.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Hunahunaa ang tubig sa tubo! Ang boltahe kay presyon nga nagtulod, ang kuryente kay gidaghanon sa tubig nga nagaagas, ug ang resistensya kay pig-ot nga tubo nga nagpahinay.
proposals.defect: fact_en defines resistance as a NARROW pipe slowing the flow, but fact_bis said "sip-on nga tubo" — sip-on is nasal mucus/a cold in Cebuano — so the constriction that the whole analogy exists to teach is absent from the Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: One word changed: sip-on -> pig-ot. `--bis sip-on` = 64 Cebuano bodies, uniformly mucus or the common cold (ffct-00027 cold symptoms, ffct-00108 "pilit nga sip-on" = sticky mucus, ffct-00545 "Ang sip-on gipahinabo sa virus") — zero "narrow" usage. `--bis pig-ot` = 47 Cebuano bodies meaning narrow (ffct-03181 "pig-ot nga ear canal", ffct-07948 "pig-ot kaayong han-ay sa pH" = narrow pH range, ffct-09041 "pig-ot nga puwang"), and `--en "narrow pipe"` returns the exact collocation: ffct-38778 "sama sa hangin sa pig-ot nga tubo" = "just like air rushing through a narrow pipe". Both emphasis_bis spans ("boltahe", "kuryente") are untouched and still present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang windlass nga gamiton sa balon usa ka wheel and axle! Pag-ikot nimo sa crank handle, molikos ang lubid ug moakyat ang bug-at nga timba.
proposals.defect: fact_en says turning the crank WINDS the rope (the rope coils on the axle — the wheel-and-axle mechanism the card teaches), but fact_bis said "mosinaw ang lubid", i.e. the rope becomes shiny, so the mechanism is missing from the Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: One word changed: mosinaw -> molikos. `--bis sinaw` = 58 Cebuano bodies, all shiny/glossy (ffct-00295 "sinaw nga agi sa uhog", ffct-07862 "sinaw nga kapa" of a pearl) — never winding. `--bis likos` = 5 bodies for winding a rope/string, including the corpus's own windlass twin ffct-23691, which renders the identical English "Turning the handle easily winds the rope" as "pagtuyok sa kuptanan naglikos sa pisi", plus ffct-23858 "likosi ang pisi sa lawas niini" (EN "wind the string around its body"). The intransitive form I used, molikos, is itself attested in 9 Cebuano bodies with exactly the coil/wrap sense (ffct-02509 tendrils "molikos sa sanga" = wrap around a branch; ffct-05110 python "molikos ug mohugot"; ffct-00333 roots that "molikos sa punoan"), and it parallels the clause's existing "moakyat ang timba". I deliberately did NOT touch "balon" despite the finding: `--bis balon` shows the corpus itself using balon for "well" in four other bodies (ffct-24723, ffct-24998, ffct-26934, ffct-27630, all EN "well"), so per-card it is not provably a defect and swapping in atabay would be a corpus-wide variant call, not a minimal repair. emphasis_bis span "wheel and axle" is untouched and still present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang thread sa tornilyo usa ka inclined plane nga nakalikot sa silindro! Ang matag pag-ikot nagbalhin sa gamay nga rotational effort ngadto sa dako nga forward force.
proposals.defect: fact_en's subject is the screw's THREAD, but fact_bis said "Ang hikaw sa tornilyo" — hikaw is an earring — so the one part of the screw the card is about is never named in Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: One word changed: hikaw -> thread. `--bis hikaw` = 1 Cebuano body, and it is THIS card — unsourced anywhere else in 47,056 cards. I did not invent a Cebuano coinage: the corpus keeps the English loanword for this exact concept, `--bis thread` = 29 Cebuano bodies, four of them screw threads in the same collocation I used: ffct-23106 "ang mga threads sa tornilyo" (EN "a screw's threads"), ffct-22286 "Ang nagliko-liko nga linya palibot sa tornilyo gitawag og threads", ffct-23115 "ang mga threads niini mokupot", ffct-24751 "naggamit sa screw threads"; singular "thread" is attested at ffct-22047 "nipis kaayo nga glass thread". (`--bis tanod` = 6 bodies but only for sewing/textile thread, so it would have been wrong here.) emphasis_bis span "inclined plane" is untouched and still present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon pag-atras sa sakyanan?

Ang reverse gear sa sakyanan naggamit og idler gear aron baliktaron ang pag-ikot sa wheel axle, moatras ang sakyanan!
proposals.defect: fact_en asks how a car goes BACKWARDS and says the idler gear lets the vehicle back up, but fact_bis used balikwas twice — to flip over/overturn — so the Cebuano told the child the reverse gear makes the car flip over.
proposals.attestation: One root changed, in both occurrences: pagbalikwas -> pag-atras, makabalikwas -> moatras. A raw substring scan of all Cebuano bodies for "balikwas" (any affix, since the tool's word-boundary regex misses prefixed forms) returns exactly 1 hit — this card — so the word is unsourced. `--bis atras` = 7+ bodies for moving backward, decisively including a car: ffct-38640 "Ang awto nga nag-atras gawas sa driveway" (EN "A car reversing out of a driveway"); also ffct-36546 "pa-unahan ug pa-atras", dcard-03322 plates "nag-atras". The two affixed forms I used are separately attested: "pag-atras" in 2 bodies (ffct-02146 "pag-atras sa kamot", dcard-01989 gun recoil) and "moatras" in 8 bodies (ffct-22859/ffct-23029 gun kicks backward, ffct-23512 "Kung moatras ka", ffct-30606 sea pulling back). I used moatras rather than makaatras because maka(-)atras has 0 attestations in any Cebuano body. emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga lapad ug ubos ang mga racing car?

Gilaraw sila aron ubos kaayo ang center of gravity! Dili kini matumba kon moliko sa mga kurba sa taas nga bilis.
proposals.defect: fact_en says the low centre of gravity stops the car ROLLING OVER when CORNERING, but the Cebuano said "maluod" (unattested; luod = nausea, not tipping) and "mo-ligo" (to bathe), so neither the rollover nor the cornering is stated anywhere on the card.
proposals.attestation: matumba: 99 Cebuano bodies and the top word (28 hits) of cards whose EN matches 'tip over|roll over|topple' — ffct-22559 'Mas lisod matumba kung mas ubos ug lapad ang base' is the same centre-of-gravity fact; ffct-08373 'aron dili matumba' = topple over. moliko: 94 bodies for turn/bend (ffct-00705 'Ang punoan sa tanom moliko'). Counter-check: 'luod' = 0 bodies (NOT ATTESTED); 'ligo' = 2 bodies, one is a bath (ffct-23939 'init nga ligoanan') and the other is this defective card. 'kurba' kept verbatim (already on the card, attested ffct-00452). emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsa ang rolling resistance, ug nganong mas daghang gasolina ang gulong nga kulang sa hangin?

Ang rolling resistance mao ang kiskisan sa gulong ug dalan! Ang gulong nga kulang sa hangin adunay mas taas nga rolling resistance, nagdugang sa gasolina.
proposals.defect: fact_en defines rolling resistance as friction between the tyre and the ROAD, but 'daan' in Cebuano means OLD, so the definition sentence named no road and the child could not tell what the tyre rubs against.
proposals.attestation: dalan = road: 67 hits and the #1 word across the 70 cards whose EN matches 'the road' (ffct-14951 'ang tubig sa dalan' = water on the road; ffct-15558 'konkreto nga dalan' = concrete roads; ffct-27102 pairs treads/friction with 'dalan'). Counter-check 'daan': 363 bodies, every sampled one = old (ffct-00063 'daan nga panit sa halas', ffct-00195 'daan nga resipe'). Single word swapped; 'kiskisan' and 'gulong' left untouched. emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Naglutaw ang barko tungod kay ang tubig nga gibalhin niini katumbas sa tibuok timbang niini! Gilaraw sa mga engineer ang hull shape aron masiguro kining Archimedean balance.
proposals.defect: fact_en says the water the ship DISPLACES weighs the same as the ship, but 'gipalit' means BOUGHT in Cebuano, so the displacement idea — the entire fact — was never stated.
proposals.attestation: gibalhin: 29 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus's own word for displaced water in the sibling Archimedes card ffct-18306 — 'ang pataas nga buoyant force sa butang katumbas sa timbang sa tubig nga iyang gibalhin' for EN 'equals the weight of the water it displaces'; also ffct-16036 'gibalhin ang elektron' = transferred. Counter-check 'gipalit': 9 bodies, all buying (ffct-02122 bought bananas, ffct-16568 fish/rice bought at market). One word swapped. emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong sayon mosulod ang matalas nga lansang sa kahoy o dingding?

Nagtipon ang matalas nga tumoy sa puwersa ngadto sa napakagamay nga lawak, naghimo og napakataas nga presyon nga nagmaneho sa lansang!
proposals.defect: fact_en is about a NAIL piercing wood, but 'pako' in Cebuano is a wing/fern, so both the question and the payoff described a sharp wing being driven into wood and nothing on the card restores 'nail'.
proposals.attestation: lansang = nail: 44 Cebuano bodies, all the nail sense — ffct-13172 'natusok sa taya nga lansang' (rusty-nail puncture), ffct-15177 'ang lansang sa tubig' (nail rusting in water), ffct-12617 'sama kabug-at sa usa ka gamay nga lansang' for EN 'the weight of a small nail'. Only that word changed (twice). Left untouched on purpose: 'matalas' (3 bodies incl. ffct-15025 'matalas nga baho'), 'napaka-' (27 bodies), 'lawak' (43 bodies, all = chamber, so clumsy for 'tiny area' but 'napakagamay' still carries the smallness) and 'nagmaneho' (0 bodies, but sentence 1 already says the nail easily goes in) — flagging them rather than widening the diff. emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Delikado ang mga matalas nga butang sama sa lansang ug kutsilyo tungod kay ang gamay nga tumoy nagpugos sa tanan nga puwersa sa gamay nga lugar, naghimo og dako nga presyon nga dali nga mosulod sa panit!
proposals.defect: fact_en names NAILS and knives as the dangerous sharp things, but 'pako' is a wing in Cebuano, so the load-bearing exemplar object was wrong and the title ('Mahait nga Butang') never restores it.
proposals.attestation: lansang = nail: 44 Cebuano bodies, nail sense throughout (ffct-13233 'Sa lansang ra ba gikan ang tetanus?', ffct-15177, ffct-12617). One word swapped; everything else byte-identical, so emphasis span 'presyon' is still present verbatim (verified).

proposals.defect: None provable in the body: the sweep's defect ('Lebre' = hare for 'Levers') is in title_bis, which this task cannot change, and the Cebuano body delivers fact_en — ancient people lifted heavy stones with long poles used as levers, before writing.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the only body-level divergence is 'kawayan' (bamboo) for EN 'sticks', which still delivers 'long sticks used as levers' and is a localisation, not a fact loss — Rule 1 says a clumsy-but-delivering body is a HOLD. Rewriting the body would also risk the emphasis span 'lever' (present verbatim) while leaving the actual defect, the title, unfixed; the title needs the Cebuano teacher.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Naabtan ka sa gawas samtang may kidlat? Yumuko nga ubos, ipundok ang mga tiil, itago ang ulo sa tuhod. Ayaw paghigda! Mas gamay ang target nimo ug mas luwas ka.
proposals.defect: fact_en instructs CROUCH LOW WITH FEET TOGETHER, but 'Paglubo' is not an attested Cebuano crouch verb and 'duhaon ang mga tiil' is unattested, so the two instructed actions — the whole safety posture — were missing while only 'don't lie down' and 'head to knees' survived.
proposals.attestation: yumuko: 2 Cebuano bodies, both lightning-crouch cards with this exact EN — ffct-24472 'yumuko ug gamay ang imong lawas' for 'crouch down low and make yourself small', ffct-24473 'yumuko ka sa uma'. ipundok ang mga tiil: taken verbatim from the sibling card ffct-35122, 'lingkodi ang lawas ug ipundok ang mga tiil' for EN 'crouch low with your feet together'; ipundok = 5 bodies, pundok = 44. Counter-check: 'duhaon' = 1 body (this card only); 'lubo' as a root = 0 (the 31 'lubo*' hits are lubog/lubot/lubos, different words) and 'paglubo' hits are paglubong/paglubok/paglubog. emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang eardrum usa ka manipis nga lamad sa sulod sa imong tainga. Kung matamaan sa mga sound wave, mokurog kini sama sa panit sa tinuod nga tambol!
proposals.defect: fact_en says that when sound waves HIT it, the eardrum VIBRATES like a drum skin; the Cebuano said 'nalingkod' (it sits) and 'matahasan' (from tahas = a job/task), so the one fact the card teaches was absent.
proposals.attestation: mokurog = vibrate: 55 Cebuano bodies and the corpus's word in this exact card family — ffct-03181 'moabot kini sa eardrum, nipis nga panit nga mokurog' for EN 'the eardrum, a thin skin that vibrates'; ffct-09699 'mokurog ang imong eardrum'; also #10 word across the 231 cards whose EN matches 'vibrate'. matamaan = to be hit: 5 bodies (ffct-30098 'matamaan sa kilat' = hit by lightning, ffct-33304 'matamaan sa meteorite', ffct-29170), same patient-focus slot as the word it replaces; cf. motama (35 bodies) in ffct-02659 'motama sa eardrum'. Counter-check: 'matahasan' = 1 body, this card itself; 'tahas' = 4 bodies, all 'job/role'. Emphasis span 'eardrum' untouched and verified present.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang cochlea usa ka spiral nga organ sa inner ear nga adunay gagmayng hair cells. Kung mokurog sila, nagapadala sila og electrical signals sa utok ingon tunog!
proposals.defect: fact_en makes VIBRATION the trigger that sends the hair cells' electrical signals to the brain, but 'nagalingkod' means 'when they sit', so the conversion mechanism was missing and no other clause restores it.
proposals.attestation: mokurog = vibrate: 55 Cebuano bodies (ffct-09699 'mokurog ang imong eardrum, ug ipasa sa tulo ka gagmayng buto sa middle ear kining mga kurog ngadto sa cochlea' — same organ, same mechanism; ffct-03181; ffct-12428 'ang hangin mokurog'). Exactly one word changed; 'nagapadala' and the rest of the naga- styling left alone. emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang imong inner ear adunay tulo ka semicircular canals nga puno sa likido! Kung molihok ang likido, nagisulti kini sa utok kung asa ka nagtuyok aron mabalanse ka.
proposals.defect: fact_en says the moving fluid tells your brain WHICH WAY YOU ARE TURNING, but 'nagikod' is not a Cebuano word (Tagalog-shaped 'ikot'), so 'kung asa ka nagikod' left the turning unsaid — note the sweep's own finding is about title_bis ('bali'), which this task cannot repair.
proposals.attestation: nagtuyok = turning/spinning: 161 Cebuano bodies, including the two inner-ear balance cards that state this very mechanism — ffct-00912 'magpadayon gihapon paglihok ang likido sa sulod sa imong dalunggan — mao nga mura kag nagtuyok pa' and ffct-02068 'maghunahuna ang imong utok nga nagtuyok pa gihapon ka'. Counter-check: 'nagikod' = 1 body (this card), root 'ikod' = 0 bodies, NOT ATTESTED. One word changed; title_bis 'Canals sa Bali' is still broken and needs the Cebuano teacher. emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong ang mas dagkong gong sa kulintang nagahatag og mas ubos nga tunog?

Ang kulintang usa ka grupo sa gagmayng gong gikan sa Mindanao! Ang mas dagkong gong nagahatag og mas ubos nga pitch tungod kay mokurog nga mas hinay.
proposals.defect: fact_en answers the headline question with 'because they VIBRATE more slowly', but 'nagalingkod' means 'sit', so the causal clause — the only answer on the card — said the gongs 'sit more slowly'.
proposals.attestation: mokurog = vibrate: 55 Cebuano bodies (ffct-03181 eardrum 'panit nga mokurog'; ffct-12428 'ang hangin mokurog sulod sa guwang'); the corpus also pairs slow vibration with 'mas hinay' in ffct-06615 'mas hinay kini mag-uyog' for 'they vibrate more slowly'. Exactly one word replaced in the same grammatical slot, so the emphasis span 'mas ubos nga pitch' is untouched and verified present.

proposals.defect: Real defect (fact_en: the AIR COLUMN VIBRATES and its length sets the pitch; the Cebuano says the air 'sits' — nagalingkod), but it is unrepairable here: the defective phrase is itself the emphasis span.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: emphasis_bis contains 'nagalingkod nga air column' verbatim. Fixing 'nagalingkod' (attested replacement would be mokurog, 55 bodies, e.g. ffct-12428 'ang kawayan mahimong himoong plawta... kay ang hangin mokurog sulod sa guwang niini' — the same bamboo-flute fact) deletes that span and silently kills its bold rendering, and leaving the second occurrence to save the span would leave the mechanism still wrong. Per the emphasis rule this goes to the Cebuano teacher, who can update text and span together.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga lahi-lahi ang tunog sa mga bar sa marimba ug xylophone?

Ang mas taas nga bar mouyog nga hinay para sa mas ubos nga pitch, samtang ang mas mubo mouyog nga paspas para sa mas taas nga pitch!
proposals.defect: The English says long bars VIBRATE slowly and short bars vibrate fast, but the Cebuano says they "nagalingkod" (sit) slowly/fast, so the card never states the vibration that causes the pitch difference.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: mouyog (replacing nagalingkod twice). `--bis uyog` = 216 Cebuano bodies for vibration (ffct-01639 "pag-uyog" = vibration, ffct-02659 "nag-uyog nga hangin" = vibrating air). The exact construction is attested on the twin pitch cards: ffct-22172 "ang mas mubo ... nga kuwerdas MOUYOG NGA MAS PASPAS, mao nga mas habog ang tono" and ffct-22173 "Ang mas taas ... nga kuwerdas MOUYOG NGA MAS HINAY, mao nga mas halawom ang tono" (mouyog = 22 bodies). `--bis lingkod` = 8 bodies, all literal sitting (ffct-03853 tul-id ang lingkod human mokaon), confirming the defect.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Kung sagolon nimo ang tanang kolor sa pintura, magsipsip sila og daghang wavelength sa suga — gamay ra ang mobalik, maong mogawas ang madulom ug malapot nga kolor nga duol sa itim!
proposals.defect: The English cause is MIXING every paint colour together; the Cebuano says "Pagkat-on nimo" (when you LEARN the colours), so the card never states the mixing that produces the muddy near-black colour.
proposals.attestation: Introduced sagolon (and the function word kung). `--bis sagol` = 286 Cebuano bodies = mixing; `sagolon` specifically = 30 bodies, incl. the paint card ffct-19604 "ang 3 ka primarya nga kolor sa pintura ... pwede rang SAGULON para sa laing kolor" and ffct-15016 "KUNG SAGOLON kini sa lain-laing paagi", ffct-16082 "mo-react sila kung sagolon". `--en "mix.*paint"` shows pagsagol/sagulon as the corpus renderings for paint mixing. The "Kung <verb>on nimo ang ..." frame = 82 bodies (ffct-15184 "Kung kutawon nimo ang asin sa tubig"). No emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Sa transverse wave, ang mga particle nag-vibrate perpendicular sa direksyon sa pagbiyahe sa alon! Sama kini sa mga alon sa pinayog nga pisi ug mga suga.
proposals.defect: The definition turns on the particles VIBRATING perpendicular to travel; the Cebuano says the particles "nagalingkod" (sit) perpendicular, i.e. static, which is the opposite of wave motion.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: nag-vibrate. `--bis vibrate` = 110 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus's word specifically for PARTICLES: ffct-16917 "ang particles niini nagkurog o NAG-VIBRATE gamay sa ilang lugar", ffct-18242 "NAG-VIBRATE lang sila sa ilang dapit", ffct-18367 "nag-vibrate sila sa tiyak nga frequency". `--bis lingkod` = 8 bodies, all = sitting. Emphasis span "transverse wave" is untouched and still present verbatim in the first three words.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga makita ang flashlight beam sa maitom nga kwarto nga abogon?

Kini ang Tyndall effect! Ang suga nagkatag sa gagmayng particles sa hangin sama sa abog o usok, makita ang beam!
proposals.defect: The English mechanism is light SCATTERING off the dust/smoke particles; the Cebuano "nagawagtang" says the light makes the particles vanish/removes them, so the scattering that makes the beam visible is never stated.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: nagkatag. `--en scatter` (125 cards) ranks nagkatag (31) / magkatag (17) as the corpus's scattering words, used for light specifically: ffct-16633 "ang kahayag MOKATAG sa lain-laing direksyon", ffct-16408 "dili niini MAGKATAG ang kahayag", ffct-18510 "medium particles nga NAGKATAG sa kahayag". Sibling Tyndall cards confirm the same clause shape: ffct-17928 "NAGKATIBULAAG ang kahayag sa gagmay nga particle" and ffct-24173 "GIKATAG sa gagmayng partikulo ang kahayag". `nagkatag` = 77 bodies overall. Emphasis span "Tyndall effect" untouched and still present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ibutang ang imong kamot sa tutunlan samtang nagasulti aron mabatyagan ang vibration! Nagpamatuod kini nga ang imong boses gihimo sa nag-uyog nga vocal cords.
proposals.defect: The English teaching claim is that the voice is made by VIBRATING vocal cords; the Cebuano says "nagalingkod nga vocal cords" (seated vocal cords), so the card never says the cords vibrate.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: nag-uyog. Vocal-cord cards in the corpus use uyog for exactly this: ffct-06615 "Kon luag ang vocal cords, mas hinay kini MAG-UYOG", ffct-11741 "Kon higpiton ug banaton ang vocal cords, mas paspas kini MAG-UYOG". The attributive frame "nag-uyog nga X" = 28 bodies (ffct-02659 "NAG-UYOG NGA hangin" = vibrating air; ffct-23790 "nag-vibrate nga dila"). `--bis lingkod` = 8 bodies, all sitting. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon pagsilaw sa glow-in-the-dark nga mga bituin sa kisame sa kangitngit?

Nagsipsip sila og suga kung hayag ug hinay-hinay nga nagpagawas niini sa kangitngit! Mahitabo kini tungod sa phosphorescence sa materyal.
proposals.defect: The English says the stars slowly RELEASE the absorbed light in the dark; the Cebuano "hinay-hinay ginhawa" says they slowly breathe and drops the light as object, so the give-back step that explains the glow is missing.
proposals.attestation: Introduced nagpagawas niini. `nagpagawas` = 297 Cebuano bodies meaning emit/release (ffct-00470 sweat glands "NAGPAGAWAS ug pawis", ffct-00506 decomposers "NAGPAGAWAS og carbon dioxide"). The same absorb-then-slowly-release sentence exists twice: ffct-18165 (same phosphorescence fact) "nagsipsip sa kahayag ug HINAY-HINAY kini NAGPAGAWAS sa kangitngit" and ffct-35910 "nag-absorb sa sobra nga ulan ug HINAY-HINAY NGA NAGPAGAWAS NIINI sa dry seasons" — which supplies the adverb+linker+object exactly as used here. `--bis ginhawa` usage in the corpus is breath/breathing, confirming the defect. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang screw nagpasayon sa paghugpong sa duha ka butang o pagpataas sa mga butang; gibalhin niini ang pagtuyok ngadto sa kusog nga puwersa!
proposals.defect: The English second use of a screw is "lift things"; the Cebuano says "pagpataas sa TUBIG" (raise WATER), teaching a different device (an Archimedes screw).
proposals.attestation: Introduced only butang, a word this same sentence already uses ("paghugpong sa duha ka BUTANG") — the preferred-word case in the brief. The frame "pagpataas sa X" = 16 bodies (ffct-25721 same simple-machines series "gigamit sa PAGPATAAS SA bug-at", ffct-22304/25719 "pagpataas sa bandila", ffct-01020 "pagpataas sa asukal sa dugo"). I deliberately did NOT try to restore "forward" in "strong forward force": the corpus renders the screw's forward action as "pasulod" (ffct-22287 "ang pagtuyok mahimong galihok nga PASULOD sa materyal"), which is "inward", not "forward", so inserting it would be my own coinage; "kusog nga puwersa" is incomplete but not false, and the incompleteness stays flagged for the teacher. No emphasis spans.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis "Ilha si Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit, ang naghimo sa Fahrenheit temperature scale!" already delivers what fact_en says (Fahrenheit created the Fahrenheit temperature scale).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Fahrenheit Buhag Scale"), which is out of scope for a fact_bis repair, and the finding itself concedes the body restores the fact. The body's own word is the corpus-correct one — `--bis naghimo` is the standard maker verb, while `--bis buhag` reports 0 Cebuano BODIES (9 titles only) = NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY, i.e. the corruption lives exclusively in titles. Dropping "clever scientist"/"we use today" is compression, not a factual failure.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Gipalambo pag-ayo ni James Watt ang steam engine (makina nga gipalihok sa alisngaw)! Gihimo niya kini mas maayo ug mas episyente.
proposals.defect: The English subject is the STEAM engine; the Cebuano gloss — the card's only explanation of what drives the machine — says "gipalihok sa aso" (driven by SMOKE).
proposals.attestation: Introduced only alisngaw. `--bis aso` = 206 Cebuano bodies and they are smoke: ffct-00504 "Ang ASO sa sigarilyo", ffct-01274 "ASO gikan sa sigarilyo ug polusyon", ffct-03801 "aso sa sigarilyo". `--bis alisngaw` = 216 bodies = vapour/steam (ffct-15608 "pagpabukal niini ngadto sa ALISNGAW", ffct-02560 "ALISNGAW sa tubig", ffct-17396 "init nga alisngaw"). `--en "steam engine"` gives the corpus convention on the sibling cards: ffct-25699 "makina nga DE-ALISNGAW (steam engine)", ffct-25820/25821 "makinang de-singaw". No emphasis spans.

proposals.defect: No body defect that fact_en can prove: "Nagpakita kini sa nawong sa imong kausap, sama ra sa video call karon" does say the videophone shows the face of the person you are talking to, which is exactly what fact_en says.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding's real target is title_bis ("Kausab" = change), out of scope for a body repair. The only body objection is that "kausap" is a Tagalog loan rather than Cebuano "kaistorya" (`--bis kaistorya` = 3 bodies, incl. the videophone cards dcard-06925 "makita ug madungog nimo ang KAISTORYA" and dcard-06926; `--bis kausap` = 2 bodies, one of which is this card itself). That is a lexical/language-purity issue, not a failure to deliver the English fact, so under Rule 1 it is not mine to rewrite — send it to the Cebuano teacher together with the title.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang cheetah mao ang pinakapaspas nga hayop sa yuta, makadagan og grabe ka paspas, mga 110 km/h!
proposals.defect: The English restricts the claim to the fastest LAND animal; the Cebuano "pinakapaspas nga hayop sa TIBUOK yuta" = fastest animal in the whole world, which drops the qualifier and makes the sentence false (a peregrine falcon is faster).
proposals.attestation: No new word is introduced at all — the repair deletes "tibuok", leaving the corpus's own standing phrase for "fastest land animal". `--en "fastest land animal"` returns it verbatim on five sibling cards: ffct-08350 "Ang cheetah mao ang PINAKAPASPAS NGA HAYOP SA YUTA", ffct-14896 and ffct-24544 (same words), plus ffct-04434/14030 with mananap. None of them carries "tibuok"; the inserted "tibuok" is what converts the land qualifier into a worldwide scope. No emphasis spans.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis "Gusto ba nimo mahibal-an kung paila ka katig-a ang bato? Ang Mohs scale nagsukod sa hardness sa mga mineral!" delivers both halves of fact_en (how hard a rock is; the Mohs scale measures mineral hardness).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Kagwang" = the Philippine flying lemur), out of scope for a fact_bis repair, and the finding itself names the body as the evidence that the title is the outlier. Corpus check confirms the split: `--bis kagwang` = 52 bodies, all the colugo/flying lemur (ffct-01101 "Ang kagwang o Philippine flying lemur"), while `--bis katig-a` = 27 bodies for hardness — the word the body already uses correctly. Nothing to change in the body.

proposals.defect: None in the body — the Cebuano body delivers everything fact_en says (who improved the steam engine, that he was a Scottish engineer, and the 1760s/1770s dates).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Pahuwat"), not fact_bis. The body already reads "Kinsa ang nagpalambo sa steam engine aron mas episyente kini? ... Gipalambo niya ang steam engine niadtong 1760s ug 1770s" — palambo is the correct improve verb and the finding itself cites this body as the evidence that the TITLE is the outlier. Nothing in the body is refutable against fact_en, so no body edit is warranted.

proposals.defect: None in the body — the Cebuano body carries the same speed as the English (~300 km/h), so the number conflict the finding describes lives only in the title.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: fact_en says "about 300 kilometers per hour" and fact_bis says "mga 300 ka kilometro kada oras" — an exact match, including the hedge. The invented 320 is in title_bis ("Bullet Train Shinkansen 320"), which is out of scope for a body repair. No word in the body is defective.

proposals.defect: None provable in the body — it states reflection as light returning off a surface like a mirror, which is what the English says.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding targets title_bis ("Pamalandong sa Hayag"), not the body. fact_bis "Ang reflection mao ang pagbalik sa kahayag gikan sa usa ka surface sama sa samin!" matches fact_en. I checked the one word that could look Tagalog: `--bis samin` = 27 Cebuano BODIES, including mirror-sense optics cards (ffct-26869 "sa usa ka patag nga samin" EN "in a flat mirror"; ffct-26873 "Kung moigo ang kahayag sa samin" EN "When light hits a mirror"), so it is attested and not a defect. The only gap vs English is the adjective "shiny", which is not a meaning error. Emphasis span "reflection" is present and untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Gipabilin sa Stanley Classic vacuum bottle nga init ang mga likido gamit ang vacuum layer taliwala sa mga bungbong niini aron pugngan ang heat conduction!
proposals.defect: The English says the bottle KEEPS liquids hot, but "Gipainit" says the bottle HEATS the liquids — it makes the vacuum layer a heater instead of an insulator.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `gipabilin` + `init`. `--bis gipabilin` = 30 Cebuano BODIES, all in the "keeps X in state Y" sense and in the same frame I used (ffct-01057 "Gipabilin sa lawas nga balanse ang asukal sa dugo" EN "The body keeps blood sugar balanced"; ffct-17364 "gipabilin nga sinaw" EN "keeps it shiny"). `--en "keep[s]? .{0,20}hot"` (18 cards) frequency table: init 19, magpabilin 5, nagpabilin 4, pagpabilin 3 — and the two thermos cards render this exact physics that way: ffct-19758 "Magpabilin nga init ang imnonon sa thermos" EN "A thermos keeps your drink hot", ffct-20374 "Magpabiling init ang ilimnon sulod sa thermos". Word order, agent, vacuum layer, walls and heat-conduction clause are unchanged; emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Moinit ang panit nimo kung maglingkod duol sa campfire! Ang nasunog nga kahoy nagpagawas og infrared radiation nga moagi sa hangin.
proposals.defect: The English says sitting near a campfire WARMS your skin; "Mokusog ang panit nimo" says your skin becomes STRONG, so the card never states that the fire warms you.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `moinit`. `--bis moinit` = 149 Cebuano BODIES, all "becomes warm/hot" (ffct-00161 "Kung mohubag, mapula, moinit" EN "swollen, red, warm"; ffct-01703 "Kon moinit na usab ang panahon" EN "When the weather warms again"). Exact-concept check `--en "warm.{0,6} your skin"`: ffct-27221 EN "generating heat to warm your skin" → BIS "para moinit ang imong panit". Defect word confirmed by `--bis mokusog` = 62 bodies, every one meaning grow stronger/faster (ffct-01118 "mokusog ang atong mga bukog" EN "make our bones stronger"). One-word swap; the second sentence and the emphasis span "infrared radiation" are untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Gusto ba nimo patindoga ang imong buhok gamit ang science?

Makagama ka og static electricity pinaagi ra sa pagkuskos og balloon aron ma-transfer ang mga electron!
proposals.defect: The English generates the charge by RUBBING a balloon; "pag-uyog" says shaking it, which transfers no electrons, so the card teaches a method that does not work.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `pagkuskos`. `--bis pagkuskos` = 28 Cebuano BODIES for rubbing/scrubbing (ffct-01476 "pinaagi sa pagkuskos sa mga pako" EN "by rubbing its wings together"). `--en rubbing` (115 cards) top Cebuano words: pagkuskos 27, pagkiskis 17, kuskuson 12. Exact-concept check `--en "rub.{0,15}balloon"`: ffct-17082 EN "Rubbing a balloon on your hair builds static electricity" → BIS "Kung kuskuson ang lobo sa buhok, makabaton kini og static electricity" — same experiment, same root. Defect word confirmed: `--bis uyog` = 216 bodies, all vibrate/shake (ffct-01639 "Ang tingog mao ang pag-uyog" EN "Sound is a vibration"). One-word swap; the question line, "og" marker and emphasis span "static electricity" are untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong madulas kaayo ang nabasa nga dahon sa saging?

Ang hapsay ug mamantika nga nawong niini nagpakunhod sa friction! Mao nga madulas kaayo kini kung mabasa.
proposals.defect: The English asks why a wet banana leaf is SLIPPERY and concludes it is super slippery when wet; "maligid" says it ROLLS, so the observable property the card is about is never stated.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `madulas`. `--bis madulas` = 30 Cebuano BODIES, including adjectival use on a wet surface: ffct-24781 "sa madulas nga daan pagkahuman sa ulan" EN "on slippery roads after rain"; also the adjacent friction cards ffct-27024 and ffct-27088 ("aron dili madulas"). Defect word confirmed: `--bis maligid` = 5 bodies, and the four that are not this card all mean roll (ffct-23835 "maligid lang kini sa ehe" EN "you roll them on an axle"; ffct-26884 "sayon maligid sa kabayo ang bug-at nga karga"). Note for the record: `--en "\bslippery\b"` (83 cards) ranks danlog 38 / madanlog 14 above madulas, so madanlog was an equally attested option; I chose madulas because this is a friction-series card and its own batch sibling ffct-27277 already uses "dili madulas" for the same physics. Two-word swap; emphasis span "friction" and the middle sentence are untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Mahimo bang mahimong magnet ang lansang nga puthaw?

Oo! Kung ibalot nimo kini og wire ug mo-agi ang electric current, mo-align ang magnetic domains niini, mao nga temporaryo kini nga mahimong magnet!
proposals.defect: The English object is a simple iron NAIL, but "pako" is a wing, so the Cebuano gives the child an "iron wing" to wrap with wire and the hands-on fact is unrecoverable.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `lansang`. `--bis lansang` = 44 Cebuano BODIES, unambiguously nail (ffct-13172 "natusok sa taya nga lansang" EN "a rusty nail wound"; ffct-15177 "Unsay mahitabo sa lansang sa tubig" EN "a nail in water"). Exact-concept check `--en "iron nail"`: ffct-16309 EN "a solid iron nail" → BIS "ang solido nga lansang nga puthaw" — the verbatim collocation I used. Defect word confirmed: `--bis pako` = 359 bodies meaning wing (ffct-00006 "gamit ang iyang kaugalingong mga pako" EN "using its own wings"). Caveat recorded: three corpus cards (ffct-19808, ffct-20228, ffct-20784) repeat the same pako-for-nail slip, i.e. one translator cluster, not independent attestation; lansang is the correct and dominant form. One-word swap; emphasis span "magnetic domains" untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang Venus flytrap nagtipig ug chemical energy sa iyang mga dahon! Kung matandog ang sensitive trigger hairs niini, dali kaayo kining mo-convert ngadto sa kinetic energy.
proposals.defect: The English trigger is TOUCHING the sensitive trigger hairs; "mahipos" means tidied away/collected, so the card states a nonsense trigger condition.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `matandog`. `--bis matandog` = 13 Cebuano BODIES meaning to be touched/disturbed, and the corpus uses it for this exact card concept: ffct-08544 EN "When a Venus flytrap's tiny trigger hairs are touched twice within twenty seconds" → BIS "Kung ang sensitibo nga trigger hairs sa Venus flytrap matandog og duha ka beses sulod sa baynte ka segundo" — same object, same verb form, same frame. Supporting: ffct-05907 "pila ka beses natandog sa insekto ang trigger hairs" EN "how many times an insect touches its trigger hairs"; ffct-08512 "kung aksidente matandog ka niini" EN "if it accidentally touches you". Defect word confirmed: `--bis mahipos` = 1 body (this card itself), `--bis gihipos` = 1 body meaning collect (ffct-08734 "gihipos sa mga tawo ang liso" EN "people collect seeds"). One-word swap; I did not restore the dropped "to snap shut" since that would add a fact. Both emphasis spans intact.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Kung hingpit nga gibira ang bow, nagtipig kini ug mga 50 joules nga elastic potential energy! Mo-transfer kini sa arrow isip kinetic energy inig buhian.
proposals.defect: The English stores the energy in a fully DRAWN (pulled) bow; "gihuyop" means blown, so the card gives a false condition for storing elastic potential energy.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `gibira`. `--bis gibira` = 144 Cebuano BODIES meaning pulled/drawn, including the same elastic-storage frame: ffct-09067 "sama sa gibira nga goma" EN "like a stretched rubber band" (storing energy in tendons before a jump); also ffct-12019 "Gibira sa bulan ug adlaw ang kadagatan" EN "The moon and sun pull on the oceans". Root `--bis bira` = 173 bodies. Defect word confirmed: `--bis huyop` = 16 bodies, every one blowing (ffct-19054 "Kon huyopan ang globo" EN "When you blow into a balloon"; ffct-16356 "huyop sa hangin" EN "blowing wind"). One-word swap; the 50 joules, the arrow clause and the emphasis span "elastic potential energy" are untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga magaspang ang mga bato sa trail sa Mayon Volcano?

Ang magaspang nga volcanic rocks naghatag og friction aron dili madulas ang mga nag-hike!
proposals.defect: The English asks why the rocks are ROUGH and says their roughness is what raises friction; "garbo/garbong" means proud, so the property that causes the friction is never stated and the child cannot answer the card's own question.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `magaspang`. `--bis magaspang` = 29 Cebuano BODIES meaning rough, including the exact question frame: ffct-16493 "Ngano nga magaspang ang sinina sa gahi nga tubig?" EN "Why do clothes feel rough in hard water?", and the exact attributive frame ffct-15954 "sa magaspang nga nawong" EN "on a rough surface". Root `--bis gaspang` = 36 bodies (ffct-02546 "gaspang ang panit sa iho" EN "a shark's skin is rough"). `--en "\brough\b"` (127 cards) ranks gaspang 35 / magaspang 24 as the rendering. Defect word confirmed: `--bis garbo` = 11 bodies; the only use outside the ffct-27xxx/28xxx friction batch is ffct-05090 "Garbo sa Palawan ang tandikan" EN "Palawan is proud of the tandikan" — the other nine are the same translator's cluster repeating the error, so they do not attest it. Two-word swap; "naghatag og friction", the hikers clause and the emphasis span "friction" are untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang kabayo nga nagdagan ug nagguyod sa kalesa adunay espesyal nga energy?

Oo! Samtang naglihok kini sa mga bato-batong kalsada sa Vigan, adunay kini kinetic energy tungod sa iyang paglihok!
proposals.defect: The English has the horse PULLING the kalesa; "naggukod" means chasing, which reverses the relationship — the horse is running after the carriage instead of drawing it.
proposals.attestation: Introduced `nagguyod`. The corpus renders this exact English concept with guyod: ffct-04130 EN "The kalesa is a horse-drawn carriage" → BIS "karwahe nga giguyod sa kabayo"; ffct-24886 EN "A kalesa is a carriage pulled by a horse" → BIS "sakyanan nga giguyod sa kabayo"; ffct-27189 EN "the horse's pulling force" → BIS "ang paguyod sa kabayo". Form checks: `--bis giguyod` = 9 bodies, `--bis guyod` = 7 bodies, `--bis nagguyod` = 2 bodies (ffct-28242 "kanunay nga nagguyod sa likido" EN "constantly pulls the liquid"; ffct-18027 "ang asin nagguyod sa moisture" EN "salt pulls out moisture") — the form I used is attested. Defect word confirmed: `--bis gukod` = 1 body only. (nagbira, 54 bodies, was the alternative — ffct-10360 "nagbira og karomata" EN "pulls carts" — but guyod is what the corpus uses specifically for a horse and a kalesa.) One-word swap; emphasis span "kinetic energy" untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ginapapasayon ba sa single fixed pulley ang pag-alsa?

Ang usa ka fixed pulley nga gibit sa kisame dili makapamenos sa kusog nga imong pag-alsa! Usbon lang niya ang direksyon sa imong bira.
proposals.defect: The English says the pulley does not reduce LIFTING effort and that it ONLY changes the direction of your PULL, but the Cebuano says it does not reduce the force of your TOUCHING (pagahikap) and that it only SOMETIMES (usahay lang) changes the direction of your SHAKING (pag-uyog), which reverses the card's payload.
proposals.attestation: pag-alsa: 65 bodies = lift (ffct-00436 'pag-alsa og 10x sa iyang gibug-aton' / EN 'lift 10 times its weight'); it is also the word this card's own question already uses. 'Usbon lang niya' follows the attested pattern 'Usbon lang niini ang anggulo' (ffct-00766, EN 'It just changes the angle'); usbon = 148 bodies = change (ffct-00107 'usbon ang kolor' / EN 'changes its color'); 'usbon lang' 6 bodies. 'imong bira' = 'your pull' is attested verbatim in a fixed-pulley card: ffct-22304 'nag-usab sa direksyon sa imong bira' / EN 'changes your pull's direction'; bira = 173 bodies. Defect words confirmed: hikap = 169 bodies, all TOUCH (ffct-01050 'ayaw kini hikapa' / 'never touch one'); uyog = 216 bodies, all SHAKE/vibrate (ffct-01639 'pag-uyog' / EN 'vibration'). Left 'gibit' untouched (1 body, this card only) — its meaning is uncertain to me and 'sa kisame' still delivers the ceiling; not a word I would introduce.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon pag-akyat ang gagmay nga insekto sa narra tree nga dili madulas?

Ang magaspang nga panit sa narra tree nagdugang friction, mao nga ang gagmay nga insekto makakapyot sa kahoy nga dili madulas!
proposals.defect: fact_en says the ROUGH BARK of the narra increases friction, but the Cebuano says 'garbong kahoy' (proud/elegant wood), losing both the mechanism (roughness) and the part of the tree (bark), so the Cebuano answers 'why don't the insects slip?' with nothing but 'because narra wood'.
proposals.attestation: garbo = pride, confirmed: 11 bodies, e.g. ffct-05090 'Garbo sa Palawan ang tandikan' for 'Palawan is proud of the tandikan bird'. (The only 'garbong = rough' hits are ffct-27054/27105/27277, the same defective ffct-27xxx family, so they cannot vouch for it.) Replacement 'magaspang' = rough: 29 bodies, always English rough/bumpy (ffct-15954 'magaspang nga nawong' = 'a rough surface'; ffct-22330 'magaspang nga kahoy' = 'bumpy wood'); 'magaspang nga' as a modifier frame is attested in 12 bodies. Replacement 'panit' = bark on a tree: 1,206 bodies, and specifically tree bark in ffct-07674 'Adunay kahoy nga hapsay ang panit ug adunay magaspang' for 'Some trees have smooth bark, others rough' — the exact magaspang/panit pairing — and ffct-00238 'nagpilit sa panit sa mga kahoy' for 'clinging to tree bark'. Second 'kahoy' left alone since it renders fact_en's 'trunk'. Emphasis span 'friction' verified present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang magaspang nga abaca ropes adunay high friction! Mao nga dili sila madulas kung ang mga mangingisda magtali sa ilang gagmay nga bangka sa kahoy nga pier.

proposals.attestation: luspad = pale/faded, confirmed: 40 bodies, all colour (ffct-02800 'luspad man ang mga mananap sa langob' = 'cave animals so pale'; ffct-03260 'luspad nga dalag' = 'pale yellow' urine). Replacement 'madulas' = slip: 30 bodies, all English slip (ffct-24780 'aron dili ka madulas' = 'so you don't slip'; ffct-27024 'Nganong dili ta madulas sa basa nga bathroom tiles?' = 'Why don't we slip on wet bathroom tiles?'), and --en 'from slipping' ranks madulas 11 as the corpus's word for exactly this concept. The repaired frame 'dili ... madulas' is attested in 24 bodies. One word changed; the body's own correct 'magaspang' for rough is untouched; emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang magaspang nga texture sa abaca fibers mopataas sa friction! Mao nga maayo kini gamiton sa pagbugkos sa bug-at nga karga nga lig-on.

Contrast garbong: only 10 bodies, ALL of them one friction-card family (ffct-27054/27105/27277/27821/27891/28006/28338/28569/35384 + this card), while the single independent body use is ffct-05090 "Garbo sa Palawan ang tandikan" = Palawan is PROUD of the bird, and the only garbo title is ffct-30347 "Garbo ka nga Sandstorm" for "Thick Sandstorms" -- i.e. a self-vouching defect family, not real usage; ffct-28006's own title is "Magaspang Kennon Road" for "Rough Kennon Road" while its body says garbong. pagbugkos: 4 Cebuano bodies, and ffct-12971 renders EN "tying its very first strands" as "pinaagi sa pagbugkos sa unang lugway" -- the corpus word for this exact English concept (paghigot was checked and is NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY, so it was not used). pag-ukit refuted as carving: 21 bodies, all carving (ffct-19745 carving a bamboo flute, ffct-21055 carving bulul statues). proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang kusog nga neodymium magnet dali ra makadani sa mga lansang nga puthaw, pero dili makaapekto sa aluminum nga lata ug copper nga mga kable!
proposals.defect: English says the magnet attracts iron NAILS; the Cebuano says "mga pako nga puthaw" = iron WINGS, so the object the magnet picks up is a different thing.
proposals.attestation: pako refuted as nail: 359 Cebuano bodies and the independent ones all mean wing or fern -- ffct-00006 "makalupad gamit ang iyang kaugalingong mga pako" = bat's wings, ffct-00651 "Ang pako sa Philippine Eagle" = wingspan, ffct-00676 "Walay bulak ug liso ang pako" = fern. lansang: 44 Cebuano bodies, all nails, including the identical collocation -- ffct-16309 "ang solido nga lansang nga puthaw" for EN "a solid iron nail", ffct-15177 and ffct-16425 nail-rusting cards, ffct-12617 "sama kabug-at sa usa ka gamay nga lansang" for "the weight of a small nail". Single-word swap; emphasis span "neodymium magnet" untouched and the aluminum/copper contrast left exactly as written.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Isuksok ang copper nga lansang ug zinc nga lansang sa gipiga nga calamansi—ug wow! Nakahimo ka og gamay nga electrical current!
proposals.defect: English instructs the child to push a copper NAIL and a zinc NAIL into the calamansi; the Cebuano says "copper nga pako ug zinc nga pako" = a copper wing and a zinc wing, so the hands-on demo names an object that does not exist.
proposals.attestation: Same false friend as ffct-28090, same evidence: pako in independent corpus bodies = wing/fern (ffct-00006 bat wings, ffct-00405 "bukton, pako, ug palikpik" = arms/wings/flippers, ffct-00676 fern). lansang: 44 Cebuano bodies, all nails (ffct-16309 "lansang nga puthaw" = iron nail; ffct-13172 "taya nga lansang" = rusty nail). The sibling calamansi-battery card ffct-28373 keeps the English "copper ug zinc nails", confirming the object, not the Cebuano word, is what this card gets wrong. Two-word swap only; no emphasis spans on this card; the em-dash, "wow" and the current fact are unchanged.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Sa water cycle, ang gravity mao ang puwersa nga nagabira nga maoy hinungdan nga ang precipitation mohulog gikan sa panganod paingon sa yuta!
proposals.defect: English says gravity is the PULLING force; the Cebuano calls it "ang puwersa nga nagahuyop" = the force that BLOWS (with air/breath), which is a different kind of force from the one the card exists to teach.
proposals.attestation: huyop refuted: 16 Cebuano bodies, all blowing air -- ffct-19054 "Kon huyopan ang globo, mapuno kini sa hangin" for EN "when you blow into a balloon", ffct-20172 "Pag-huyop ug hangin sa campfire", ffct-16356 "huyop sa hangin" = blowing wind. Replacement nagabira keeps the card's own naga- prefix shape and is attested for gravity pulling specifically: ffct-28611 "kanunay nga nagabira paubos ang gravity sa rattan ball" for EN "gravity constantly pulls the rattan ball downward", ffct-34036 "grabidad sa Bulan nga nagabira sa tubig sa dagat"; 3 Cebuano bodies for nagabira, with the wider bira family at 173 bodies (nagbira 54, mobira 139) and "pagbira" the top word in cards whose English says "pulling force". Single-word swap; emphasis span "gravity" untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang Pacific electric ray sa mga coral reef sa Pilipinas nagpagawas og kalit nga electrical currents aron paluyahon ang gagmay nga isda una kaunon!
proposals.defect: English says the shock STUNS the small fish before the ray eats them; the Cebuano says "aron PATINDOG ang gagmay nga isda" = to make the fish STAND UP, stating a different effect for the shock that is the whole point of the card.
proposals.attestation: patindog refuted: 48 Cebuano bodies, all standing/upright/vertical -- ffct-08818 "Naglutaw ug patindog sa tubig, nga daw nagtindog" for "floating straight up... like it's standing", ffct-10814 "patindog ang tunga sa mata sa buaya" = vertical slit pupil. Replacement paluyahon: 3 Cebuano bodies, and the decisive one is the corpus's other electric-ray card, ffct-06527: "gigamit niini ang kuryente aron paluyahon ang isda nga kaonon" for EN "it uses its shock to stun the fish it wants to eat" -- same animal, same English verb, same clause shape (also dcard-10020 "babagan o paluyahon ang mosulod nga tsunami waves" = weaken). Cross-checked alternatives that the corpus also uses for stun (maparalisa, 2 bodies, ffct-27501 electric eel; malipong, 14 bodies, ffct-04340 cyanide fishing), but took the electric-ray rendering. Single-word swap; no emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.defect: No body defect is provable: the flagged "kulob" is in title_bis only, while the body already has the correct verb, "pwede mokulo sa room temperature" = can boil at room temperature.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason. The finding is explicitly a title-outlier claim ("The card's own body has the correct verb"), and title repair is out of scope here. The body delivers every element of fact_en: liquid water boils at room temperature if you lower the air pressure with a simple vacuum pump. "ibanan nimo ang pressure sa hangin" drops only the English intensifier "surrounding... enough", which is register/compression, not a factual defect, and Rule 1 forbids rewriting for that. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang Philippine gumamela (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis) adunay hayag nga pula nga mga petalo! Nag-reflect kini sa red light wavelengths aron makadani sa mga pollinating butterflies.
proposals.defect: English says the gumamela has bright red PETALS that reflect red light; the Cebuano says "mga talong" = EGGPLANTS, so the thing that is red and reflects the light is named as a vegetable growing on a hibiscus.
proposals.attestation: talong refuted: 28 Cebuano bodies, every one an eggplant -- ffct-00919 "mga tanom sama sa kamatis ug talong" for EN "plants like tomatoes and eggplants", ffct-03150 "Ang talong, kamatis, ug okra" for "Eggplant, tomato, and okra". Replacement petalo: 13 Cebuano bodies, and the corpus uses it for this exact concept on this exact flower -- ffct-02649 "Dugmoka ang mga petalo sa gumamela" for EN "Crush some gumamela petals"; also ffct-05438 "mabulukon nga mga petalo" = colorful petals, ffct-06137 "sepal, petalo (talulot), stamen, ug pistil" for "sepals, petals, stamens, and the pistil". petalo is the top Cebuano word (15 occurrences) across cards whose English contains "petals". Single-word swap; no emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon paghimo og temporary magnet gikan sa lansang nga puthaw?

Sa proseso sa magnetization, ihaplas kini gamit ang permanent magnet! Mag-align kini sa internal magnetic domains sa parehas nga direksyon.
proposals.defect: English builds the whole instruction on an iron NAIL; the Cebuano question says "gikan sa pako nga puthaw" = from an iron WING, so the object the child is told to stroke with a magnet is never named correctly anywhere in the body.
proposals.attestation: pako refuted as nail: independent corpus bodies all mean wing/fern (ffct-00006 bat wings, ffct-00021 "pako sa buyog" = bee's wings, ffct-00250/00676 ferns). lansang: 44 Cebuano bodies, all nails, with the exact collocation this card needs -- ffct-16309 "ang solido nga lansang nga puthaw" for EN "a solid iron nail". Single-word swap in the question line only; the \n\n break, the "magnetization" emphasis span, "ihaplas kini" (stroke it) and the magnetic-domain sentence are all left verbatim -- "kini" still refers back to the nail, so the edit does not disturb the anaphora.

proposals.defect: No body defect is provable: the flagged "lubog" is in title_bis only, and the body already carries both the pull and the fall -- "Ang gravity nagbira... paingon sa ilawom" and "samtang nagahulog".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason. The finding is a title-outlier claim and concedes "The body has the correct word"; title repair is out of scope for a fact_bis pass. The body's verbs are the corpus-standard ones (nagbira: 54 Cebuano bodies for EN "pulls", e.g. ffct-00080 "ang mga kaunuran nagbira sa mga bukog" = muscles pull on your bones). Its only divergence from fact_en is compressing "a strong, hard shell" to "lig-on nga shell", which drops an adjective but no fact and is not worth touching under minimal edits. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsa ang fluid friction o drag?

Mahitabo kini kung ang mga butang molihok sa likido sama sa tubig o gas sama sa hangin, ug makapahinay kini kanila!
proposals.defect: English answers the question "what is drag?" with "...slowing them down!", the defining property; the Cebuano stops at objects moving through liquid or gas and never says drag slows them, so the card's own question goes unanswered.
proposals.attestation: Restores the dropped English clause with the corpus's own rendering of it. makapahinay: 30 Cebuano bodies for EN "slow down" -- ffct-09972 "Ang makapahinay sa photosynthesis" for "What can slow down photosynthesis?", ffct-05836 "makapahinay sa ilang pagtubo" for "slow down their growth". The drag cards specifically use this same root: ffct-22965 "Ang drag mao ang puwersa sa hangin nga nagsumpaki sa lihok sa eroplano ug NAGPAHINAY niini!" for EN "drag... pushes against the plane and slows it down", and ffct-24270 "usa ka babag nga mobira balik ug MOPAHINAY sa bangka" for "a resistance that pulls back and slows the boat". kanila: 310 Cebuano bodies, used as a verb object exactly this way in ffct-00180 "makakuha kanila" = removes them. Nothing else in the body was touched -- same question line, same \n\n, same examples; no emphasis spans.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the Cebuano body carries the giant clam, the iridocytes, the scattering of sunlight and the protection of the algae; the sweep's finding is about title_bis ("Tahong"), which is out of scope for a body repair.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason. The only body wording that could look thin is "i-scatter ang adlaw" for "scatter sunlight", but bare `adlaw` for sunlight is standard corpus practice: 179 Cebuano bodies whose English says "sunlight" render it as bare `adlaw` (e.g. ffct-00789 EN "make their own food from sunlight" -> BIS "gamit ang adlaw"; ffct-00872 "when sunlight hits them" -> "kung masilawan sa adlaw"). `--en scatter` also shows `nag-scatter`/`nagkatag` both in use, so the card's `i-scatter` is in-corpus. Nothing provable to change.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Kanunay nga moadto ang kainit gikan sa mas init nga butang paingon sa mas bugnaw! Mao nga ang metal nga kutsara moinit sa nagbukal nga sabaw.
proposals.defect: The English says the metal spoon GETS HOT in boiling soup, but `mokusog` means becomes strong/stronger/faster, so the Cebuano never states that the spoon heats up.
proposals.attestation: `--bis mokusog`: 62 bodies, all "grow strong/faster" (ffct-00748 "maulian ug mokusog" = recover and grow stronger; ffct-01118 "mokusog ang atong mga bukog" = bones grow stronger; ffct-01173 "mokusog ang kaunoran") -- never heat. `--bis moinit`: 149 bodies, exactly "gets hot/warm" (ffct-00161 "mohubag, mapula, moinit" = swollen, red, warm; ffct-02088 "moinit ang tibuok Kalibutan" = the whole Earth warms; ffct-03738 "mas paspas kini moinit" = it warms up faster). One-word swap; no emphasis spans on this card.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the Cebuano body states brain -> paspas nga electrical impulses -> nerves -> kalamnan sa tiil, which is what fact_en says; the sweep's finding is about the stray "Bulan" in title_bis, not the body.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding itself concedes "body is correct", and re-reading fact_bis against fact_en confirms every element of the English (rapid electrical impulses, through the nerves, telling the leg muscles to kick) is present. Title repair is out of scope here.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang short circuit molaktaw sa normal nga electrical path, hinungdan nga ang electrons molabay nga walay limitasyon ug maghimo og delikado nga kainit nga makatunaw sa wires!
proposals.defect: The English says the short circuit BYPASSES the normal electrical path, but `mopasulod` means lets in / feeds into / enters it -- the definitional fact is inverted.
proposals.attestation: `--bis mopasulod`: 3 bodies, all "let in / enter" (ffct-12620 "mopasulod og hangin ug sustansya sa balas" = lets air and nutrients reach the sand; ffct-35841 EN "What makes a star officially ENTER its main sequence stage?"), i.e. the opposite of bypassing. `--bis molaktaw`: 5 bodies, all "skip" and one in the identical frame -- ffct-21293 "ang solid dry ice molaktaw sa liquid phase" for EN "skips the liquid phase"; also ffct-37532 "dili molaktaw" = never skip steps, ffct-38437 "molaktaw og usa ka henerasyon" = skips a generation. Single word changed; the rest of the sentence (unrestricted flow, melting heat) left untouched. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Makapalutaw ba gyud ang magnet sa buhi nga baki?

Oo! Ang pinakakusog nga continuous magnetic field gikan sa lab electromagnets nakaabot og 45 Tesla, nga makapalutaw sa buhi nga baki!
proposals.defect: The English asks whether a magnet can make a frog FLOAT and answers that 45 Tesla can LEVITATE a live frog, but `makapahuyop` means to blow (with breath/wind), so neither the question nor the answer states floating.
proposals.attestation: `--bis huyop`: 16 bodies, every one about blowing air (ffct-19054 "Kon huyopan ang globo" = when you blow into a balloon; ffct-20172 "Pag-huyop ug hangin sa campfire" = blowing air onto a campfire; ffct-16356 "huyop sa hangin" = blowing wind) -- never floating. `--bis makapalutaw`: 3 bodies, exactly the causative "makes/lets float" (ffct-00553 "sudlanan og gas nga makapalutaw niini" for EN "bladders that let it float"; ffct-20864 "Nganong makapalutaw ang foam life jacket?" for EN "Why do foam life jackets keep you floating?"; ffct-26370 "ang puwersa nga makapalutaw" = the upward force). Root also attested broadly: `--bis molutaw` 257 bodies. Only the two verb tokens changed; "45 Tesla" and every other element preserved. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Sa reflection stage sa vision, motalbog ang light rays gikan sa dili nag-sidlak nga butang sama sa libro ug mo-adto sa imong mga mata!
proposals.defect: The English says light rays BOUNCE OFF the non-luminous object, but `mopakpak` in the corpus means to flap/snap (wings, claws), so the card's one mechanism -- reflection as bouncing -- is not stated in Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: `--bis mopakpak`: 5 bodies -- ffct-00021 "mopakpak ang pako sa buyog" (a bee flaps its wings), ffct-08864 pistol shrimp snapping its claw, ffct-10690 mantis shrimp punching; no bounce sense anywhere. `--bis motalbog`: 20 bodies, and ffct-22652 is the same sentence as this card -- EN "light bounces off them and travels straight into our eyes" -> BIS "ang kahayag motalbog gikan niini paingon sa atong mga mata", which also attests the exact `motalbog ... gikan sa` frame kept here; see also ffct-03973 "motalbog ang kahayag sa mga butang" and ffct-22648 "motama sa usa ka ibabaw ug motalbog pabalik" for reflection. Verified emphasis span "reflection stage" is present verbatim in the new text. Note: the sweep's own finding for this card is title-only; this body defect was re-derived independently from fact_en.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang fiberglass insulation nag-trap sa hangin aron mapugngan ang pag-balhin sa kainit, mao nga mapainit gihapon ang balay sa tingtugnaw!
proposals.defect: The English says the insulation TRAPS air, but `nag-trapo` means wipes / rag, so the trapped-air mechanism -- the card's only explanation for the slowed heat transfer -- is missing.
proposals.attestation: `--bis trapo`: 6 bodies, all rag/wipe (ffct-15671 "Trapohan lang kini gikan sa magneto" for EN "wipe it off the magnet"; dcard-01666 and dcard-05442 both "trapo" = cleaning rag; ffct-17379 "mapahid sa trapo"). `--bis nag-trap`: 5 bodies, all for English "traps", including the identical `nag-trap sa` frame -- ffct-20987 "Ang pressure cooker nag-trap sa steam" for EN "A pressure cooker traps steam"; also ffct-19954 "porous structure nag-trap og hangin" and ffct-20178 "nag-trap ug hangin" for EN "trap air". Only the verb changed. No emphasis spans.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong makalukso ka ug taas sa luksong-tinik?

Ang kusgang unod sa imong mga bitiis motulod sa imong lawas paibabaw! Apan ang gravity mobira kanimo balik sa yuta.
proposals.defect: The English question asks how you JUMP so high in luksong-tinik, but `maka-tulon` is "can swallow", so the Cebuano question asks why you can swallow high.
proposals.attestation: `--bis tulon`: 2 bodies -- ffct-13839 "tibuok nilang tulonon ang biktima" for EN "they swallow their prey whole", and this card; the only attested sense is swallowing. `--bis makalukso`: 22 bodies for English "jump/leap", including the same person-subject frame ffct-00080 "makalakaw, makakumo, ug makalukso ka!" for EN "every step, wave, and jump"; also ffct-00578 "Unsa kataas makalukso ang baki?" and ffct-03941 "Unsa kalayo makalukso ang tipaklong?". The card's own title_bis already uses "Paglukso". Only the question verb changed; verified emphasis span "gravity" still present verbatim in the second sentence.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis already says the solid, opaque brick walls of the Vigan heritage houses block light energy and keep the inside dark and cool ("nagbabag sa light energy ... ngitngit ug bugnaw"), which is exactly fact_en; the "Luto Malamig" problem is in title_bis only.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding itself notes "only the body carries the fact" and that the body uses the correct Cebuano `bugnaw`. Nothing in the body is provably wrong against fact_en, so no body edit is warranted; the title goes to the title pass.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the body uses `kasingkasing` (heart) correctly and carries the sinoatrial node, the tiny electrical impulses, the muscle contractions and the pumping of blood; the truncated `Kasing` (spinning top) is a title_bis problem.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding states the body uses kasingkasing correctly and that the defect is title-only. Re-reading fact_bis against fact_en confirms every element of the English is present. No body edit.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Human makalupad sa ibabaw sa ocean waves, gibira sa gravity ang flying fish pabalik sa tubig aron luwas!
proposals.defect: The English says gravity PULLS the flying fish back down, but `gihurot` means used up / depleted, so the card's single claim about what gravity does becomes consumption rather than a downward pull.
proposals.attestation: `--bis gihurot`: 3 bodies, all "use up / deplete" (ffct-02422 "ilang gihurot ang asukal ug luna" for EN "using up the sugar and space"; dcard-07802 "ilang gihurot ang samang limitado nga resource" for EN "they use the same limited resource"), never pull. `--bis gibira`: 144 bodies for English "pull", including gravity itself in the identical `gibira sa X ang Y` frame -- ffct-12019 "Gibira sa bulan ug adlaw ang kadagatan" for EN "The moon (and sun) pull on the ocean"; also ffct-13710 "mas daghang tubig ang gibira pataas" for "more water gets pulled up". One word changed; verified emphasis span "gravity" present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang imong vocal cords mo-vibrate ug maghimo og sound waves, nga molakaw sa hangin aron madungog sa uban!
proposals.defect: The English says the vocal cords VIBRATE to produce sound waves, but `mobati` means to feel, so the vibration mechanism is never stated in Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: `--bis mobati`: 55 bodies, every one "to feel" (ffct-00905 "mobati kita og kasakit" = we feel pain; ffct-01244 "para mobati sa mga butang pinaagi sa paghikap" = to feel things by touch; ffct-02561 "mobati ang panit" = the skin senses). `--bis mo-vibrate`: 18 bodies, all for English "vibrate" (ffct-24203 "Mo-vibrate ang eardrum" for EN "The eardrum vibrates"; ffct-20681 "water molecules mo-vibrate ug mas paspas"; ffct-23796 bamboo "hapsay mo-vibrate"), and the two near-duplicate vocal-cord cards use it in this exact context: ffct-28570 "mo-vibrate ang imong vocal cords" and ffct-28638 "Ang imong vocal cords nag-vibrate". `--en vibrat` also ranks `nag-vibrate` (46) and `mag-vibrate` (38) among the characteristic words. One word changed; verified emphasis span "sound waves" present verbatim.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang mga wooden shafts sa tradisyonal nga kalesa nagsilbi isip lever! Nagtabang kini sa kabayo nga pagbira sa bug-at nga kariton.
proposals.defect: The English says the shafts help the horse PULL the carriage, but the Cebuano says "pagduso" = push, which teaches the opposite of the force direction the card is about.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced: pagbira (duso -> bira). `--bis duso`: 19 bodies, all = push (ffct-22432 "Kon mas kusog ang imong duso" EN "The stronger your push"; ffct-22428 "usa ka duso o bira" EN "a push or a pull" -- the corpus itself opposes the two). `--bis pagbira`: 109 Cebuano BODIES (ffct-01170 "Unsaon pagbira sa hantik sa layo nga dahon" EN "How do weaver ants pull distant leaves"; ffct-09495 EN "Why are weeds so hard to pull out"). Sibling card ffct-28628 is the same scene: EN "the horse pulls it" -> BIS "gibira sa kabayo", title "Puwersa sa Pagbira". `--en pull` frequency table: mobira 141, gibira 126, pagbira 110. Emphasis span "lever" untouched and still verbatim; single-word diff, no other change.
