proposals.new_fact_bis: Bugnaw ang mga polo sa Yuta kay pahilig ang kahayag sa adlaw ug mokatag, maong huyang ang init. Gipasanag pa balik sa puti nga yelo ang kadaghanan sa kahayag!
proposals.defect: The English says the polar sunlight is SLANTED (which is why it spreads thin and warms weakly), but the Cebuano says it is "hapdos" = stinging/burning, so the card's entire causal mechanism — light arriving at an angle — is absent and is replaced by a claim that contradicts "huyang ang init".
proposals.attestation: Introduced one word: pahilig. ceb_usage.py --bis pahilig = 11 Cebuano bodies, all for slant/slanted, incl. dcard-08404 "pahilig ang pag-igo sa kahayag sa adlaw" (EN "sunlight strikes objects at a slanted angle") and dcard-08406 "Ang pahilig nga silaw sa kahayag" (EN "Slanted light rays"); --en slant ranks pahilig 13x, the top candidate. Defect side: --bis hapdos = 2 bodies only, the other being dcard-08166 "naay hapdos o burning effect" for acids, confirming hapdos = stinging/burning, not slanted. Nothing else touched; emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Mahitabo ang total solar eclipse kay halos managsama og gidak-on ang Adlaw ug Bulan gikan sa Kalibutan, bisan og mas dako gyud ang Adlaw!
proposals.defect: The English says the Sun and Moon look almost the same SIZE from Earth, but the Cebuano uses "magkasinglaki", and in Cebuano laki = MALE (Tagalog laki = size), so the equal-apparent-size fact — the reason a total solar eclipse can happen — is never stated.
proposals.attestation: Introduced "managsama og gidak-on". ceb_usage.py --bis "managsama og gidak-on" = 2 bodies, one of which is the corpus's own twin of this card, ffct-32030: "halos managsama og gidak-on ang Adlaw ug Bulan" for EN "the Sun and Moon look almost the same size" — a verbatim frame match. gidak-on = 363 bodies; --en "same size" ranks gidak-on 46x top. Defect side: --bis magkasinglaki = 1 body (this card alone), --bis kasinglaki = 0 bodies (NOT ATTESTED), while --bis laki = 260 bodies, all meaning male ("Ang laki nga baka gitawag og toro"). Emphasis span "total solar eclipse" is present verbatim in the new text (verified by exact substring check).

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga importante ang mga report sa intensity human sa linog?

Nagpakita kini kon asa pinakakusog ang pag-uyog! Makatabang kini sa mga responder kon asa magpadala ug tabang ug rescue.
proposals.defect: The English asks about intensity REPORTS after an earthquake, but Cebuano "ulat" = SCAR (the Tagalog ulat = report does not carry over), so the card asks about earthquake scars and no sentence in it ever names a report — the answer sentences inherit the wrong referent.
proposals.attestation: Introduced one word: report (English loan the corpus itself uses). ceb_usage.py --bis report = 36 Cebuano bodies, incl. ffct-36397 "importante ang unang report sa PHIVOLCS" — same domain and same "importante ang ... report" frame. --bis "mga report" = 2 bodies, incl. the corpus's sibling earthquake-intensity card ffct-39531 "Nagkolekta sila og mga report ... mahitungod sa gibati nga pag-uyog" (EN "They collect reports ... how people felt the shaking"), and ffct-39640 "Ang mga report sa NDRRMC". Defect side: --bis ulat = 3 bodies; the unambiguous one is dcard-05197 "gamay nga ulat sa liso" = the scar on a seed. I did NOT use "taho": every --bis taho hit is the substring inside "tahong" (mussel), so taho-as-report is unattested. Emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the English "natural warning signs of a tsunami ... strong earthquake at the coast or a loud roar from the sea" is fully delivered by the body ("Unsa ang natural nga timailhan sa tsunami? Kon mabati nimo ang kusog nga linog sa baybayon o madunggan ang kusog nga dahunog gikan sa dagat...").
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Natural nga Babag"), not fact_bis, and this task repairs the body. The body already uses the correct word timailhan for warning signs, and dahunog for the roar is corpus-normal (ceb_usage.py --bis dahunog = 11 bodies, e.g. ffct-24258 "ang dahunog sa dalugdog" for thunder's rumble). Nothing in the body is refutable against fact_en.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the body states every element of the English — very strong destructive winds, arrival within about 12 hours, heavy damage to many houses ("grabe ka kusog ug makaguba nga hangin nga moabot sulod sa mga 12 ka oras ug makaguba sa daghang balay").
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding itself concedes "body ... is correct, so only the title is defective" — the non-word "Kapeckan" occurs only in title_bis, which is out of scope for a fact_bis repair. No number or unit differs from fact_en.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Naggamit ang PAGASA og color-coded rainfall warnings: dalag nagpasabot pag-amping, kahel nagpasabot pangandam, ug pula nagpasabot mobakwit! Gipakita niini kung unsa kakusog ang ulan ug ang peligro sa baha.
proposals.defect: The English names YELLOW as the first of three warning colours, but the Cebuano says "dalaw", which is not a colour word in Cebuano, so the first colour-to-action pair of the card's three-way mapping is unrecoverable — a child cannot learn which colour means "be aware".
proposals.attestation: Introduced one word: dalag. ceb_usage.py --bis dalag = 166 Cebuano bodies, all yellow (ffct-00296 "dalag nga dahon" for EN "yellow leaves"); --en yellow ranks dalag 168x, far ahead of dilaw (41). I chose dalag over the also-attested dilaw purely on corpus dominance; both were checked. Defect side: --bis dalaw = 1 body, this card alone. The other two colours (kahel, pula) and every other word are untouched; emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the English ("Strong wind isn't the only danger! Ang kusog nga ulan sa bagyo maoy hinungdan sa baha ug landslide, nga kasagarang mas daghan pa ang madisgrasya."
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is title-only ("Kapeckan sa Bagyo") and says so ("Body is fine and delivers the fact"). I checked the one body word that could have hidden a second defect: ceb_usage.py --bis disgrasya = 2 bodies used for accidents/harm (ffct-27456, ffct-27474), so "madisgrasya" for "harm" is clumsy at worst, which Rule 1 puts out of scope.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang erosion mahitabo kung ang kusog nga ulan ug hangin makabanlas sa tambok nga topsoil!
proposals.defect: The English defines erosion as rain and wind WASHING AWAY topsoil, but the Cebuano verb "maghanas" means to train/practise (hanas = skilled), so the card's single defining sentence never says the soil is carried off.
proposals.attestation: Introduced one word: makabanlas. ceb_usage.py --bis makabanlas = 1 body, ffct-29286 "kusog nga sulog nga makabanlas sa tawo ug balay" (EN "current that sweeps away people and houses") — the identical actor + makabanlas sa + patient frame I used. Root confirmed: --bis banlas = 5 bodies and --bis banlasan = 3, incl. ffct-32494 "mas sayon nga banlasan sa ulan ang dato nga topsoil" and ffct-30049 "Kon banlasan kini sa erosion" — same rain/erosion/topsoil domain. I rejected magbanlas and mobanlas: both returned NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY. Defect side: --bis hanas = 8 bodies, all "skilled/good at" (ffct-00093 "Hanas usab mangayam"), and --bis maghanas = 1 body, this card alone. I deliberately left "tambok nga topsoil" alone: --bis "tambok nga yuta" = 7 bodies for EN "rich soil" and ffct-30676 uses "tambok nga topsoil" for EN "fertile topsoil", so it is corpus-attested, not a defect. Emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the English ("The Sun doesn't disappear at night! The Earth simply turns around, making our side face away from it") is delivered exactly by "Wala mawala ang Adlaw sa gabii! Nagtuyok lang ang Yuta, busa ang atong bahin nag-atubang palayo niini."
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding concerns title_bis ("Tirok"); the word tirok never appears in fact_bis. The finding itself states "The body uses the right word (Nagtuyok lang ang Yuta)". Nothing to repair in the body.

proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Uma" = farm); the body contains no such word. I verified the body's one risky verb rather than assuming: ceb_usage.py --bis mohabok = 5 bodies meaning swell (ffct-18788 "Mohabok ang bugas" for EN "The rice grains swell up big"), so the swelling fact is correctly carried.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the English ("It is rare for an animal to become a fossil! It must be buried quickly before it rots or is eaten by others") is delivered by "Panagsa ra mahimong fossil ang usa ka mananap! Kinahanglan kini dali nga matabunan sa dili pa madunot o kan-on sa lain."
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Lalim"); the word does not occur in fact_bis, and the body already carries rarity with "Panagsa ra", which the finding concedes ("The card's own body has it right"). No body word is refutable against fact_en.

proposals.defect: None in the body: fact_en says gold never rusts and keeps its shine after many years, and fact_bis says exactly that ("dili magkalawang", "Bisan paglabay sa daghang tuig, magpabilin pa rin kining masinaw").
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is entirely about title_bis ("makaunod"), which this task does not repair; it explicitly concedes the body has the correct word ("dili magkalawang"). The only body oddity is the Tagalog particle "pa rin" where Cebuano would say "gihapon" — that is register, which is out of scope, and the sentence still delivers "it still stays shiny". No word introduced, so no attestation needed.

proposals.defect: None in the body: fact_en's two claims (limestone and seashells are both mostly calcium carbonate; same chemical as seashells and snail shells) are both present in fact_bis via "Pareho silang halos puro calcium carbonate" and "ang samang kemikal nga naghimo sa mga kabibe ug kabhang".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding targets title_bis ("Bingkil") only and itself notes the body uses the correct words. Verified the body words are real: `--bis kabhang` = 142 Cebuano bodies, all shell (ffct-00331 "nanghulam og kabhang ang hermit crab" / EN "borrow a shell"; ffct-00258 "gawas nga kabhang" / EN "outer shell"). Nothing introduced.

proposals.defect: None in the body: fact_en's age (about 13.8 billion years), its subject (the universe) and its source (scientists, from scientific evidence) are all in fact_bis — "Ang uniberso", "mga 13.8 ka bilyon ka tuig", "Nahibaw-an kini sa mga siyentipiko gikan sa siyentipikong ebidensya".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Edad sa Kalibutan" = age of the world), not the body; the body uses the correct "uniberso". The body drops only the adjective "solid" from "solid scientific evidence", which is a descriptor, not a fact. Nothing introduced.

proposals.defect: None provable in the body: fact_en says plates slide past each other in opposite directions and the grinding causes earthquakes; fact_bis carries all three parts — "maglampasanay ang mga plaka", "sa magkasumpaki nga direksyon", "ang pagkiskisan maoy makapahinabog linog".

"maglampasanay" is unusual (`--bis lampas` = 0 bodies, though the tool's \b anchor cannot see the mag- prefix), but the opposite-directions phrase plus "pagkiskisan" (`--bis kiskis` = 28 bodies, friction/rubbing sense: ffct-04117 "ang kiskisanay maghimo og kainit" / EN "friction ... makes heat") already delivers the English. proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Lipad-lipad"), not the body, and concedes the body has the right word. Verified `--bis danlog` = 39 Cebuano bodies, all the slippery sense (ffct-00133 "Ang ngabil ug sulod sa tabo-tabo danlog" / EN "rim and walls of a pitcher plant are slippery"). Nothing introduced.

proposals.defect: None provable in the body: fact_en contrasts a sharp crack from nearby lightning with a long rumble from far-off lightning, explained by sound arriving from different parts of the bolt; fact_bis keeps all of it — "hait nga putok", "taas nga lagubo", "ang tingog moabot gikan sa lain-laing bahin sa kilat".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Butkon ug Kurug"), not the body. "lagubo" is thin but attested — `--bis lagubo` = 2 Cebuano bodies, the other being ffct-39005 "makadungog ka og lagubo nga static sa radyo" (EN "crackling static"), a low rolling-noise sense that carries the crack/rumble contrast here. Existing word, nothing introduced.

proposals.defect: None material in the body: fact_en says thunder is just a sound that cannot hurt you while the lightning that makes it is dangerous, and fact_bis says exactly that — "Ang dalugdog tingog ra ug dili ka masakitan, apan ang kilat nga naghimo niini delikado".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Tunod" for tunog), not the body, and the body carries the correct "tingog ra". The body omits only the adjective "loud"; the claim of the card (thunder = merely sound, harmless; lightning = dangerous) survives intact, and adding a word would be an edit the English does not force. Nothing introduced.

proposals.defect: None in the body: fact_en says a rainbow forms when sunlight shines through raindrops and separates into different colors; fact_bis says "Maporma kini kung moagi ang silaw sa adlaw sa mga tulo sa ulan, mabahinbahin sa lainlaing bulok".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Pagbuto" = explosion), not the body, which uses "Unsaon pagporma"/"Maporma" correctly. "bulok" (color) is one of the false-friend entries the audit already refuted — see the ceb_usage.py header, which names bakal/lana/bulok as refuted — so it is not a defect. Nothing introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsa ang aurora?

Ang aurora mao ang nagkidlap nga lunhaw o rosas nga kahayag sa langit duol sa mga polo sa Kalibutan! Maporma kini kung moigo ang gagmay nga tipik gikan sa adlaw sa hangin sa atmospera.
proposals.defect: fact_en locates the aurora "near Earth's poles", but fact_bis says "duol sa mga poste sa Kalibutan" — poste is a physical post/pillar, so the card's one locating fact is not stated anywhere in the Cebuano.
proposals.attestation: One word introduced: polo. `--bis polo` = 48 Cebuano bodies, geographic-pole sense repeatedly attested: ffct-29107 "Bugnaw ang mga polo sa Yuta" (EN "Earth's poles stay cold"), ffct-32136 "Dili duol sa mga polo sa Earth" (EN "Not at Earth's poles"), ffct-29110 "mas bugnaw duol sa mga polo" (EN "colder near the poles"), ffct-29101 "Sa tundra duol sa mga polo", ffct-09834 "gikan sa Amihanang Polo paingon sa Habagatang Polo" (EN North Pole / South Pole). `--bis poste` = 72 Cebuano bodies and every one is a physical post: ffct-15069 "mga poste sa kuryente" (EN "power poles"), ffct-02318 "poste ug tabla sa balay" (EN "posts and boards for building houses"), ffct-01526 lamp posts — never a geographic pole. `--en "Earth's poles"` returns 6 cards; the sound ones render it polo/pole, the two poste ones are this card and ffct-29848. emphasis_bis is empty, so no span is touched; diff is poste -> polo only.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Makita ba nato ang aurora sa Pilipinas?

Kasagaran dili, kay duol ta sa ekwador! Mas sagad makita ang aurora sa mga dapit nga duol sa amihanan o habagatang polo sa Kalibutan.
proposals.defect: fact_en says auroras are seen most often near Earth's north or south poles, but fact_bis says "amihanan o habagatang poste sa Kalibutan" — poste is a post/pillar, so the Cebuano names the wrong object for the place the English is about.
proposals.attestation: One word introduced: polo, in the exact collocation the corpus uses. `--bis polo` = 48 Cebuano bodies with the geographic sense attested directly (ffct-29107 "mga polo sa Yuta" / EN "Earth's poles"; ffct-32136 "duol sa mga polo sa Earth"; ffct-29110 "duol sa mga polo"), and the north/south collocation attested verbatim in ffct-09834 "gikan sa Amihanang Polo paingon sa Habagatang Polo" (EN "from near the North Pole to near the South Pole"). `--bis poste` = 72 bodies, all physical posts (power poles ffct-15069, house posts ffct-02318, lamp posts ffct-01526). I did not touch title_bis ("Aurora sa Ekwador"), which the finding flags, since only the body is in scope; "ekwador" inside the body is correct there (EN "because we are near the equator") and is left as-is. emphasis_bis is empty; diff is poste -> polo only.

proposals.defect: None in the body: fact_en says rainbows need only light and tiny droplets and can be seen in waterfall, fountain or hose spray; fact_bis carries all of it — "sa tinilamsik sa busay, tubod, o hose kung silawan sa adlaw" and "Kinahanglan lang og kahayag ug gagmay nga tulo sa tubig".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Talon", the Tagalog false friend), not the body, and states the body is the counter-evidence. Verified `--bis busay` = 13 Cebuano bodies, all waterfall (ffct-22020 "balangaw sa yamog sa busay" / EN "Waterfalls often show a rainbow in their mist"; ffct-22420 "mga suba ug busay" / EN "rivers and waterfalls"), and `--bis tubod` = 7 bodies in the spring/fountain sense (ffct-22374, ffct-23935 "init nga tubod" / EN "hot spring"). Nothing introduced.

proposals.defect: None in the body: fact_en says some areas may face longer and harsher droughts that can damage crops, and fact_bis says "makasinati og mas taas ug mas grabe nga huwaw nga makadaot sa mga tanom".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Kahuol"), not the body, and concedes the body uses the correct "huwaw". Verified `--bis huwaw` = 5 Cebuano bodies, all drought/dry-spell (ffct-28883 "mas grabe nga huwaw, baha, ug kainit" / EN "more intense droughts, floods, and heat"; ffct-28867 "taas nga huwaw" / EN "longer dry spells"). Nothing introduced.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the Cebuano delivers every element of the English (clean energy from sun, wind and water cutting the carbon dioxide that warms the Earth).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is scoped to title_bis ("Hinaw nga Kusog"), not to fact_bis. The body already says "limpyo nga enerhiya gikan sa adlaw, hangin, ug tubig ... pagkunhod sa carbon dioxide nga mopainit sa Kalibutan", which matches fact_en clause for clause, so there is nothing in the body to repair. No words introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang katig-a sa usa ka mineral mao kung unsa kalisod kini gasgason!
proposals.defect: The English names exactly one action — scratching — but the Cebuano says "kalisod kini kalason o gasgason", adding "kalason", a word the corpus never uses for scratching and which reads off "lason" (poison), so the body asserts a second, poison-flavoured property the English never states.
proposals.attestation: Deletion-only edit: zero new words introduced ("kalason o " removed; every remaining word was already in the card). Evidence: ceb_usage.py --bis kalason = 1 Cebuano body, 0 titles, and that single body is this card itself, i.e. NOT ATTESTED anywhere else in 47,056 cards. ceb_usage.py --bis lason = 6 bodies, all poison/toxin (ffct-04878 "fat-soluble nga lason sama sa DDT", ffct-05467 "natural nga lason nga nagpatay sa insekto", ffct-11990 "delikadong lason"). The corpus's verbs for scratching a mineral are gasgason / kalmuton / kalaskasan: ceb_usage.py --bis gasgason = 6 bodies, 0 titles, and ffct-19672 renders the identical English clause "how hard it is to scratch" as "kung unsa ka lisod kini gasgason" — the same construction the repaired sentence now uses; cf. ffct-19060 "unsa kalisod kalmuton ang usa ka mineral" and ffct-35001 "pwede ra kaayong gasgason gamit ang kuko". emphasis_bis is empty, so no span is at risk.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the Cebuano asks how scientists measure mineral hardness and answers with the Mohs scale from 1 to 10, exactly as the English does.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding targets title_bis ("Mohs Scale sa Katinig"). fact_bis uses "katig-a" twice, correctly, and keeps the numbers 1 and 10 and the name "Mohs scale" intact. Nothing the English says is missing from the body. No words introduced.

proposals.defect: No body defect: the Cebuano delivers both halves of the English asymmetry — a harder mineral can scratch a softer one, a softer one cannot scratch a harder one.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding targets title_bis ("Pagkalot nga Test sa Katinig"). The body uses "katig-a" and "gasgas/makagasgas" correctly (ceb_usage.py --en scratch shows makagasgas 13x and katig-a 8x as the characteristic words of scratch-hardness cards). "Unsaon pagtrabaho ang pagsulay" is clumsy phrasing, which is register and therefore out of scope. No words introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang streak plate usa ka piraso sa unglazed nga porselana nga gigamit aron makuha ang streak sa mineral!
proposals.defect: The English's defining property of a streak plate — that the porcelain is UNGLAZED — is absent from the Cebuano, which says "wala-mabordahi" (un-embroidered, from borda = embroidery), naming a textile property instead, and no other part of the card mentions glaze.
proposals.attestation: Word introduced: "unglazed". ceb_usage.py --bis unglazed = 3 Cebuano bodies, 0 titles — ffct-36341 "unglazed porcelain streak plate" (the very same object as this card), ffct-28016 "Ang unglazed clay pot nag-conduct og heat", ffct-36062 "gihimo gikan sa unglazed clay"; ceb_usage.py --en glaze confirms the corpus keeps the English term and renders the noun as glaze (ffct-15062 "Ang glaze usa ka sama-salamin nga sapaw nga gibutang sa seramika"). The replaced word is unsourced: ceb_usage.py --bis borda and --bis bordahi both return 0 bodies / 0 titles, NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY. "porselana" was kept because the card already uses it (--bis porselana = 2 bodies, incl. ffct-18939). Everything else in the sentence is byte-identical, and the emphasis_bis span "streak plate" is present verbatim in the new text (checked programmatically).

proposals.defect: No provable body defect: the Cebuano delivers soft, heavy, never-rusting gold that is highly valuable for jewelry.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding targets title_bis ("Dili Makaunod"); the body's "dili magkalawang" is the correct rendering of "never rusts" (ceb_usage.py --en "never rusts" shows magkalawang/mokalawang/matayaan as the corpus forms, e.g. ffct-15042, ffct-15104). The untranslated "soft ug heavy" is house style, not a failure to deliver: --bis soft = 61 Cebuano bodies, --bis heavy = 16, and sibling ffct-15104 likewise leaves "gold" in English. The English's "Because it stays shiny" is compressed into "Mao nga bililhon kaayo kini", which keeps the same causal chain (doesn't rust, therefore valuable) as ffct-15042/ffct-15104; restoring shininess would mean adding a clause rather than changing a wrong word, so it fails the minimal-edit test and goes to a teacher instead. No words introduced.

The only gap is the modifier "tectonic" in "ang mga plate", which names the same referent and leaves the mechanism (moving plates lifting mountains) fully intact, so it is not a delivery failure worth a body edit. proposals.new_fact_bis: Nagkalainlain ang porma sa panganod! Ang cumulus murag humok nga gapas, ang stratus patag nga sapaw, ug ang cirrus taas ug mahimulmol.
proposals.defect: fact_en says cumulus look like fluffy COTTON balls, but fact_bis says "murag humok nga bulak" = like a soft FLOWER, naming a different object, and the comparison is the card's only content for cumulus.
proposals.attestation: `--bis bulak` = 458 Cebuano bodies, all flower (ffct-00022 "buyog ug bulak" = EN "bee and flower"; ffct-00264 Rafflesia flower) — never cotton. Replacement 'gapas' checked and attested: `--bis gapas` = 23 Cebuano bodies, all cotton (ffct-01270 "Ang gapas usa ka tanom nga mamunga og humok, puti nga lanot" = EN "Cotton is a plant that grows soft, white fibers"; ffct-15423 "tanom nga gapas" = EN "cotton plant"). The corpus uses exactly 'gapas' for this same cumulus/cotton-ball comparison: `--en "cotton ball"` -> ffct-33916 "morag puti nga GAPAS" = EN "puffy like white cotton balls"; `--en cumulus` -> ffct-30899 "Ang cumulus morag GAPAS" = EN "Cumulus look like puffy cotton" and ffct-30900 "morag naglutaw nga GAPAS" = EN "look like floating cotton". Only word changed is bulak->gapas; 'humok' and everything else kept verbatim. emphasis_bis spans "cumulus" and "stratus" both still present verbatim (verified programmatically).

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unhang scale ang gigamit sa mga siyentista karon para sa dagko kaayong mga linog?

Para sa dagkong mga linog, ang mga siyentista karon naggamit sa moment magnitude scale (Mw) — mas tukma kini kay sa daan nga Richter scale!
proposals.defect: fact_en says the Mw scale is for "really big" / "huge" earthquakes (size), but fact_bis says "daghan kaayong mga linog" / "daghang mga linog" = very MANY earthquakes (quantity) in both the question and the answer, so the Cebuano-only reader is told Mw is used when quakes are numerous.
proposals.attestation: `--bis dagko` = 824 Cebuano bodies for big/large (ffct-00290 "duha ka dagko nga kumo" = EN "two big claws"). The corpus's own twin card for this exact fact uses the replacement wording in BOTH slots: ffct-34318 BODY "Unhang scale ang gigamit na karon sa mga siyentista para sa DAGKONG MGA LINOG? Para sa DAGKONG MGA LINOG, ginagamit na karon sa mga siyentista ang moment magnitude scale imbes nga ang Richter scale!" and ffct-31179 "para sa DAGKONG MGA LINOG ... Sa DAGKONG MGA LINOG"; also ffct-34003 "alang sa dagkong linog" and ffct-34004 "ilabi na sa dagkong linog", both moment-magnitude cards. The intensifier form 'dagko kaayong' is attested in 16 bodies (ffct-01323 "dagko kaayong mata", ffct-28863 "dagko kaayong balod", ffct-14203 "dagko kaayong ngipon"), which preserves EN "really big". Two words changed (daghan->dagko, daghang->dagkong); 'kaayong', 'mga linog' and the whole answer clause kept verbatim. emphasis_bis is empty, so no span risk. 'Unhang' left alone: `--bis unhang` = 13 Cebuano bodies, all interrogative "what" (ffct-18712 "Unhang klase sa charge" = EN "What kind of charge"), so it is corpus-normal, not a defect.

proposals.defect: fact_en says the Moon's PULL (gravitational attraction) causes the tides, while fact_bis "Ang birik sa Bulan" names a spin/rotation — but the word carrying the defect is also the emphasis span.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason — emphasis constraint plus unsettled attestation. emphasis_bis is exactly ["birik"], so any repair replaces the span verbatim-match string and silently kills the bold at render time; the task's span rule says HOLD in that case. Independently, the finding self-rates low-to-medium: 'birik' occurs only 3x corpus-wide and all 3 render English "pull" (ffct-16313 "birik sa grabidad", ffct-32028 "birik sa Adlaw"), i.e. it is one translator's consistent choice, so whether it is wrong is a native-speaker call on all three cards together. Correct destination is a Cebuano teacher.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis "Ang gabon morag panganod nga naglingkod sa yuta! Hinimo kini sa gagmay nga tulo sa tubig nga naglutaw, mao nga malabo ang tan-aw — sama sa Baguio o sa kabukiran!" delivers every clause of fact_en; the yabo=spill error is in title_bis only.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: 'yabo' does not appear anywhere in fact_bis — the body uses 'gabon', which the finding itself identifies as the correct word. Nothing in the body contradicts the English.

That's why their shapes and positions keep changing" is delivered by fact_bis ("Nagalupad ug naglihok ang mga panganod kay gidala sa hangin! Mao nga kanunay nga mausab ang ilang porma ug posisyon"); liwat=resemble is in title_bis only.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: 'liwat' does not occur in fact_bis; the body already uses 'naglihok', the movement word the finding endorses. No English content is missing from the body.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_en "The Sun shines by using its hydrogen like fuel through fusion in its core" is delivered by fact_bis ("Nagsidlak ang Adlaw pinaagi sa paggamit sa hydrogen niini nga morag sugnod pinaagi sa fusion sa ubod"); sobra=excess is in title_bis only.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: 'sobra' does not occur in fact_bis; the body uses 'sugnod' (fuel) in both the question and the answer. I also checked the one body word that looked like a typo, 'Unong': `--bis unong` = 15 Cebuano bodies, all interrogative "what" (ffct-18898 "Unong gas ang labing daghan sa atmospera sa Yuta?" = EN "Which gas is the biggest ... in Earth's atmosphere?"; ffct-19793 "Unong liquid fuel" = EN "What liquid fuel"), so it is corpus-normal and not a defect.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_en "They are called fossil fuels because they come from ancient plants and animals that died millions of years ago" is delivered by fact_bis ("Gitawag sila og fossil fuels kay naggikan kini sa mga tanom ug hayop nga namatay milyon ka tuig na ang milabay"); the truncated "Fue" is in title_bis only.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the truncation is not in fact_bis, and the body says "fossil fuels" in full — which is also the emphasis_bis span, so it must stay verbatim and already does. 'Ancient' is carried by "namatay milyon ka tuig na ang milabay".

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Mahimo bang tukbon sa black hole ang Yuta?

Dili angay mahadlok! Ang pinakaduol nga black hole libo-libong light-years ang layo—layo kaayo nga dili makabira sa Yuta.
proposals.defect: fact_en asks whether a black hole could swallow Earth and answers that they are too far TO pull Earth, but fact_bis reverses agent and patient ("tukbon sa Yuta ang black hole" = can the EARTH swallow the BLACK HOLE) and then drops the negation ("layo kaayo nga makabira sa Yuta" = so far THAT IT CAN pull the Earth).
proposals.attestation: No new content word introduced. (1) The question fix is a pure reordering of words already in the card. The agent/patient reading is confirmed inside the corpus: `--bis tukbon` as a verb (excluding the noun 'tukbonon') hits only ffct-04943 "panagsa ra nila TUKBON ANG TAWO" = EN "they rarely prey on humans" — with the -on patient-focus verb the ang-phrase is the one being eaten, so in this card "ang black hole" was the thing eaten. Swapping to "tukbon sa black hole ang Yuta" puts Earth in the ang-slot, matching fact_en. (2) The only word added is 'dili': `--bis dili` = 8,101 Cebuano bodies. The exact construction "X kaayo nga dili <verb>" for English "too X to Y" is attested in 12 bodies: ffct-21647 "dako kaayo nga DILI MAKALUSOT" = EN "too big to pass through"; ffct-05288 "taas kaayo nga DILI na kini madungog sa tawo" = EN "too high for people to hear"; ffct-13055 "gagmay kaayo nga DILI makita". 'makabira' was already in the card and is corpus-attested anyway (`--bis bira*` = 173 bodies, e.g. ffct-01170 "birahon ang layo nga dahon" = EN "pull the faraway leaf"). emphasis_bis span "black hole" is still present verbatim twice (verified programmatically).

proposals.defect: No body defect: the English (sensors detect quakes/water changes and send warnings so people can leave early) is delivered by "makina ug sensor ... makabati sa linog o kausaban, mopadala og pasidaan aron makabiya dayon ang mga tawo".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is about title_bis ("Babag sa Tsunami"), which is out of scope for a fact_bis repair; the sweep itself states the body uses the correct word (pasidaan). 'makabati' is attested for sensing/detecting in Cebuano bodies (ceb_usage --bis motuyok output, ffct-09083: "Kini ang makabati kon motuyok o molihok ang imong ulo" = EN "They sense the moment your head turns"). Nothing in the body to change.

proposals.defect: No body defect: EN "A lake forms when a hollow in the ground—left by ice, a volcano, or shifting land—fills up with rain, streams, or groundwater" is fully delivered by "Maporma ang lanaw kung mapuno og tubig-ulan, sapa, o groundwater ang usa ka lungag sa yuta nga gibilin sa yelo, bulkan, o paglihok sa yuta".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding targets title_bis ("Pagbuto sa Lanaw"), not the body; the sweep note itself concedes the body uses the correct verb (maporma). Hollow=lungag, forms=maporma, all three agents (yelo/bulkan/paglihok sa yuta) and all three fillers present. No word to replace.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Carbon dioxide ra ba ang greenhouse gas?

Dili! Ang water vapor ang labing daghang greenhouse gas sa atmosphere. Mao nga mas init ang gabii kon umog ang hangin, pero dili direktang makontrol sa tawo ang gidaghanon niini.
proposals.defect: EN says humid nights feel warmer, but the Cebuano says nights are warmer "kon humok ang hangin" = when the air is SOFT, so the water-vapour/humidity link the card exists to teach is never delivered.
proposals.attestation: humok: 525 Cebuano bodies, all 'soft' (ceb_usage --bis humok: ffct-00018 "humok nga puti nga larva" = soft white larvae; ffct-00134 "humok lang ang anemone" = the anemone is soft) — it never renders 'humid'. Replacement 'umog': 51 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus word for humid AIR specifically — ffct-22239 "Sa umog o halumigmig nga hangin" for EN "In damp or humid air", and ffct-01783 "init ug umog ang atong klima" for EN "our warm, humid climate" (same predicative frame as this card's "kon umog ang hangin"). ceb_usage --en humid ranks umog 18 across the 134 humidity cards. One word swapped; emphasis_bis empty; no numbers, units or facts touched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Duha ka lihok! Matag gabii, moagi ang mga bituon gikan sa sidlakan paingon sa kasadpan tungod kay motuyok ang Earth. Apan ang pag-ilis sa tibuok konstelasyon matag bulan? Tungod kini sa paglibot sa Earth sa Adlaw sulod sa usa ka tuig!
proposals.defect: EN attributes the nightly east-to-west star motion to Earth's SPIN and the monthly constellation swap to its ORBIT, but the Cebuano uses libot (orbit) for both, so the two moves the card promises collapse into one and the nightly motion is blamed on the orbit.
proposals.attestation: Replacement 'motuyok': 108 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus verb for Earth spinning — ceb_usage --en "Earth spins" (22 cards) ranks motuyok 6 / nagtuyok 6 / magtuyok 3 against libot for orbit; ffct-24006 "Ang Kalibutan motuyok sama sa dako nga kasing" = EN "The Earth spins like a giant top"; ffct-30441 "tungod kay nagtuyok ang Earth sa iyang axis" = EN "because Earth spins on its axis" (same tungod-kay frame). The second, correct libot (orbit of the Sun) is left untouched, matching ffct-29704 "molibot sa Adlaw". emphasis_bis span "Duha ka lihok" is present verbatim in the new text (verified programmatically).

proposals.defect: No provable body defect: EN "letting food scraps like fruit peels rot in the soil so they become natural fertilizer for plants" is delivered by "pagpadunot sa mga basura sama sa panit sa prutas sa yuta aron mahimo kining natural nga abono para sa mga tanom".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is a title_bis defect ("Balat" = sea cucumber), and the sweep itself confirms the body uses the correct word, panit sa prutas. The only body-level quibble is 'basura' (trash) for 'food scraps', which is grounded immediately by "sama sa panit sa prutas" and is a register/specificity matter, not a wrong fact — out of scope. No word introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Managsama ba ang weathering ug erosion?

Dili! Ang weathering moguba sa bato sa nahimutangan niini. Ang erosion pagdala sa tubig, hangin, o yelo sa naguba nga mga tipik palayo!
proposals.defect: EN asks "Are weathering and erosion the same thing?" and answers "Nope!", but the Cebuano asks "Lahi ba...?" (Are they DIFFERENT?) while keeping "Dili!", so the card tells the child the two ARE the same — the exact misconception it exists to correct, and it contradicts its own next two sentences.
proposals.attestation: Replacement 'managsama': 303 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus rendering of "the same thing" in this exact question-then-Dili frame — ffct-07712 "Managsama ba ang rabies ug tetano?" = EN "Are rabies and tetanus the same thing?", and ffct-08970 "Managsama ba ang kapok ug gapas? Dili diay!" = EN "Are kapok and cotton the same plant? No!". ceb_usage --en "the same thing" lists managsama among the characteristic words. Only the question's first word is changed; "Dili!" and both explanatory sentences are untouched, so no fact, number or unit moves. emphasis_bis empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang libot sa Earth sa Adlaw mokabat og mga 365.25 ka adlaw! Mao nga matag ikaupat ka tuig, modugang ta og usa ka adlaw, Pebrero 29, para sa leap year.
proposals.defect: EN says the orbit takes about 365 AND A QUARTER days, but the Cebuano says "365 ug tunga" = 365 and a HALF, which is both a wrong orbital period and destroys the card's own logic (a half-day surplus would need an extra day every two years, not the "matag ikaupat ka tuig" in the next clause).
proposals.attestation: tunga = half/middle, not quarter: 488 Cebuano bodies (ceb_usage --bis tunga: ffct-00075 "ang dermis sa tunga" = the dermis in the middle; ffct-29139 "Sa katunga nga bulan"). The replacement introduces NO new Cebuano word — only the numeral. "mokabat og mga 365.25 ka adlaw" is the corpus's own phrasing for this identical fact: ffct-33098 "Mokabat og mga 365.25 ka adlaw ang Yuta para mo-orbit sa Adlaw!" = EN "Earth takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun!" (the same leap-year card). Word-based alternatives were checked and are thin — 'ikaupat nga bahin' 2 bodies (ffct-33392 "mga ikaupat nga bahin (1/4)"), 'kapat' 1 body (ffct-34433), 'kinaupat' NOT ATTESTED — so the attested numeral was preferred. emphasis_bis empty; the four-year rule now follows from the number.

proposals.defect: No body defect: EN "Do microplastics rot or dissolve in water like dirt? Nope! Plastic is not alive and does not dissolve. It stays as tiny plastic pieces for a very long time" is delivered intact, polarity included, by "Madunot ba o matunaw...? Dili! Ang plastik dili buhi ug dili matunaw. Magpabilin kining gagmay nga tipik sa dugay kaayo nga panahon."
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is explicitly a title_bis false friend ("Dili Mabulok"), and the sweep itself states the body uses the correct Cebuano verb madunot in both question and answer. Nothing in fact_bis to change.

proposals.defect: Real body defect: EN "Mangrove water is muddy and shady! Big fish can't see tiny fish in this murky water" becomes "Mabugnaw ug malandong ... sa mabugnaw nga tubig" = COLD water, so the child learns coldness, not murkiness, is why predators cannot see the fry.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: TWO independent blockers. (1) emphasis_bis is ["Mabugnaw ug malandong"] and the defective word sits inside that span — repairing it would break the exact-substring bold, and repairing only the second occurrence would leave the emphasised sentence still claiming cold water while "this murky water" refers back to nothing. (2) The needed word is not safely attested: ceb_usage --bis malubog returns only 5 Cebuano bodies and none of them means murky water — ffct-29220 "malubog nga puti nga linya" = a faint band, ffct-32547 "pwede malubog" = may be submerged, dcard-02524 "unlan nga malubog kung pug-on" = a pillow that squishes. (mabugnaw itself is correctly attested as cold, 66 bodies, confirming the defect.) Needs a Cebuano teacher who can also reissue the emphasis span.

proposals.defect: Real body defect: EN "Because Earth rotates!" becomes "Kay molibot ang Earth!" = because Earth goes around/orbits, handing the child the classic rotation/revolution misconception as the cause of time zones.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: emphasis_bis is ["molibot"] — the defective word IS the emphasis span, so the only possible repair (molibot -> motuyok, attested 108 bodies; ffct-30441 "nagtuyok ang Earth sa iyang axis" for EN "Earth spins on its axis") would delete the span verbatim and silently kill the bold, and keeping molibot while correcting the sense would require adding content the card does not contain. Per the emphasis-span rule this goes to a Cebuano teacher, who can change the span alongside the body.

proposals.defect: No body defect: EN "lives on warm ocean water's heat and moisture, acting like fuel! When hitting land or cool water, it loses this fuel, so the eyewall weakens and slowly falls apart" is delivered by "Mabuhi ang eyewall sa init ug alisngaw sa init nga dagat, nga sama sa gasolina niini! ... mawad-an kini sa gasolina, mao nga mohuyang ug maguba."
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is a title_bis issue ("Sobra") and the sweep itself flags it as lower confidence precisely because the body restores the fuel concept (gasolina, twice). Heat, moisture, the land/cool-water trigger, the loss of fuel and the weakening are all present in the Cebuano. No word introduced.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang cumulus mabulo ug puti nga parehas sa gapas! Sagad kini makita sa maayong panahon ug dili kasagaran naghatag og ulan.
proposals.defect: EN says cumulus clouds are puffy and white "just like cotton", but the Cebuano says "parehas sa bulak" = like a FLOWER, so the child gets the wrong picture and the cotton comparison the card is built on is never delivered.
proposals.attestation: bulak in Cebuano bodies = flower, not cotton: 458 bodies, all floral (ceb_usage --bis bulak: ffct-00092 "bulak sa niyog-niyogan" = niyog-niyogan flowers; ffct-00264 "polen gikan sa usa ka bulak" = pollen from one flower). Replacement 'gapas': 24 Cebuano bodies, and it is the corpus word for cotton in exactly this comparative sense — ffct-01270 "Ang gapas usa ka tanom nga mamunga og humok, puti nga lanot" = EN "Cotton is a plant that grows soft, white fibers"; ffct-11447 "Sama sa gapas ang tan-awon sa kapok" = EN "Kapok fiber looks fluffy like cotton"; ffct-08970 "Managsama ba ang kapok ug gapas?" = EN "Are kapok and cotton the same plant?". One word swapped; "mabulo ug puti", the fair-weather clause and the no-rain clause are untouched, and the emphasis_bis span "cumulus" is present verbatim (verified programmatically).

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang yuta adunay mga sapaw! Ang itom nga nutrient-rich topsoil sa ibabaw, subsoil sa ubos, ug solid bedrock sa pinakaubos.
proposals.defect: The English places the subsoil BELOW the topsoil, but the Cebuano says "subsoil sa kinaadman" (kinaadman = wisdom/knowledge), which names no position at all, so the card's whole point -- the order of the layers -- is unrecoverable for the middle layer.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced is "ubos". ceb_usage.py --bis kinaadman: 1 Cebuano BODY, 0 titles -- and that one body is this card itself, so it is unsourced. --bis ubos: 945 Cebuano bodies (ffct-00147 "ang takup sa taas, ang tangkay sa ubos" / EN "the cap on top, the stalk below"); --bis "sa ubos": 268 bodies. Exact-concept precedent from --en subsoil: ffct-02587 "samtang ang subsoil sa ubos mas gahi" / EN "while the subsoil below is harder", and ubos/ibabaw/pinakaubos are the recurring layer words in that hit set. The card already uses "pinakaubos" for the bottom layer, so "sa ubos ... sa pinakaubos" mirrors EN "below it ... at the very bottom". Emphasis spans "topsoil" and "bedrock" are untouched.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis says "Hinay kaayo ang pagporma sa yuta! Mahimong moabot og gatusan ka tuig aron makahimo lang og usa ka nipis nga sapaw sa rich topsoil", which delivers everything fact_en says (slow formation, hundreds of years, one thin layer of rich topsoil).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the sweep's finding is explicitly about title_bis ("Hinay nga Pagbuto sa Yuta"), and it concedes the body already uses the correct word pagporma. new_fact_bis cannot carry a title fix, and rewriting a correct body to chase a title defect would be a diff with no defect behind it.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang go-bag adunay mga emergency essentials sama sa pagkain, tubig, tambal, importante nga dokumento, ug flashlight! I-andam kini sa wala pa moabot ang bagyo.
proposals.defect: The English go-bag list contains "medicine", but the Cebuano lists "gamot", which in Cebuano is a plant ROOT, so the medicine item is missing from the safety list a child would pack.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced is "tambal". ceb_usage.py --bis gamot: 495 Cebuano bodies, uniformly = root (ffct-00053 "Ang gamot mao ang nagasuyop og tubig ug sustansya gikan sa yuta" / EN "The roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil"; ffct-00051, ffct-00083 same). --bis tambal: 285 Cebuano bodies = medicine (ffct-00137 "Ang antibiotic usa ka tambal nga mopatay ... sa daotang bacteria" / EN "An antibiotic is medicine that kills harmful bacteria"; ffct-00408 "Unsay kalainan sa bakuna ug tambal?" / EN "What's the difference between a vaccine and medicine?"). No emphasis spans on this card; nothing else changed ("pagkain" left alone -- it still delivers EN "food", so it is not a provable meaning defect).

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong nagbag-o og direksyon ang monsoon winds makaduha sa usa ka tuig?

Tungod sa temperatura sa yuta ug dagat! Sa ting-init, mas init ang yuta mao nga mohuyop ang hangin gikan sa dagat. Sa tingtugnaw, mas mainit ang dagat mao nga mag-reverse ang hangin!
proposals.defect: The English says the wind reverses "in winter", but the Cebuano says "sa ting-ulan" (the RAINY season), which puts the reversal in the wet season -- the opposite half of the monsoon cycle from the one the English describes.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced is "tingtugnaw". ceb_usage.py --bis ting-ulan: 75 Cebuano bodies, all = rainy/wet season (ffct-02497 "panahon sa ting-ulan" / EN "during the rainy season"; ffct-02976 "lunhaw ... sa ting-ulan, brown ug uga sa ting-init" / EN "green in the wet season, brown and dry in the dry season"). --bis tingtugnaw: 73 Cebuano bodies = winter (ffct-01095 "walay dahon sa tingtugnaw" / EN "without leaves in winter"; ffct-04081 "Matulog ba ang hipon sa tingtugnaw?" / EN "Do shrimp sleep in winter?"). --en "in winter" over 32 cards ranks tingtugnaw the most characteristic Cebuano word at 20 hits. "Sa ting-init" for summer is left as-is (correct). No emphasis spans.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis delivers each English claim -- floodplains good for farming, "maayo kaayo nga farmland tungod sa rich sediment gikan sa suba", and "taas gihapon ang risk of flooding".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is explicitly title-only ("Matabang Floodplain") and concedes the body never uses matabang -- it paraphrases fertility as good farmland from rich sediment, which is what fact_en asserts. Swapping in "tabunok" would be an unforced retranslation of a sentence that is not wrong, and new_fact_bis cannot repair a title anyway.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Mahitabo ang double rainbow sa dihang mag-reflect og makaduha ang kahayag sulod sa water droplets! Mas mapusyaw ang ikaduha ug balit-ad ang ayos sa kolor.
proposals.defect: The English says the second rainbow's colors are in REVERSE order, but "binalikbalik" reads as the order being repeated/done over and over, so the card's one distinguishing fact about the secondary bow is not delivered.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced is "balit-ad". ceb_usage.py --bis balit-ad: 7 Cebuano bodies, all = flipped/reversed/upside-down, including two double-rainbow cards: ffct-28985 "Ngano nga balit-ad ang kolor sa double rainbow?" / EN "Why do colors flip in a double rainbow?" and ffct-29841 "balit-ad ang kulay" / EN "has reversed colors". --en "reverse order" returns only 2 cards: this one and ffct-24175, whose near-identical EN ("has its colors in reverse order") is rendered "sukwahi nga kolor" -- so the corpus renders the concept with balit-ad/sukwahi, never with balik-balik. I kept the card's own "ang ayos sa kolor" so "order" survives, and "balit-ad ang <noun>" is the attested frame (ffct-08916, ffct-28985, ffct-29841). Emphasis span "double rainbow" is untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon pagtagna sa atong mga katigulangan sa panahon?

Nagtan-aw sila sa mga natural nga palatandaan! 'Ang singsing palibot sa buwan nagpasabot og ulan' ug 'daghang hulmigas nga nagbalhin nagpasabot og ulan' — gipamatud-an sa modernong siyensya ang pipila niini!
proposals.defect: The English folk sign is "many ants moving means rain is coming", but the Cebuano says "daghang langgam", which in Cebuano means BIRDS, so the child is taught a different weather sign (migrating birds) than the card states.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced is "hulmigas". ceb_usage.py --bis langgam: 697 Cebuano bodies, uniformly = bird (ffct-00214 "ang atong pambansang langgam" / EN "our country's national bird"; ffct-00187 migratory birds). --bis hulmigas: 99 Cebuano bodies = ant (ffct-00110 "Pila ka hulmigas ang naa para sa matag tawo?" / EN "How many ants are there for every person?"; ffct-00154 "daghan silang magtinabangay" / EN "many ants work together"); --en ants ranks hulmigas 114 in the hit set. I checked the alternative "guyam" first: --bis guyam returns 0 Cebuano bodies, "NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY", so it was not used. "nagbalhin" (moving) is the card's own word and is unchanged. Emphasis span "natural nga palatandaan" is untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Nganong importante kaayo nga magpabilin ang mga kahoy ug balili sa mga bukid sa Pilipinas?

Ang kusog nga ulan sa mga dik-as nga daplin nagkuha sa mataba nga topsoil pinaagi sa erosion! Ang mga kahoy ug balili maghupot sa yuta.
proposals.defect: The English answer's second sentence -- "Trees and grass hold the soil in place" -- is missing entirely from the Cebuano, so the card's own question (why trees and grass must stay on the mountains) is never answered.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced is "maghupot"; "mga kahoy ug balili" is lifted verbatim from this card's own question and "yuta" is the card's own topic word. ceb_usage.py --en "hold the soil" (18 cards) shows the corpus verbs: maghupot 4, mokupot 3, naggunit 2 -- e.g. ffct-29403 "Ang mga gamot sa tanom maghupot sa yuta" / EN "Plant roots hold the soil tightly together", and ffct-29768 "Ang mga gamot sa tanom ug kahoy maghupot sa yuta sama sa pukot" / EN "Plant and tree roots hold the soil together like a net". --bis maghupot: 9 Cebuano bodies, all = hold/grip in place (ffct-01417, ffct-05172 roots gripping sand). --bis balili: 25 Cebuano bodies = grass (ffct-02551 "Ang balili motubo gikan sa duol sa yuta" / EN "Grass grows from near the ground"). Nothing else edited; emphasis span "erosion" is untouched.

proposals.defect: No body defect: fact_bis says "Grabe ka hait kini" -- exactly the English "It is extremely sharp" -- and also delivers the black glassy rock, rapid lava cooling, no crystals, and ancient tools/weapons.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the matarong/hait swap the finding describes exists only in title_bis ("Obsidian nga Matarong"); the finding itself states the body is the correct outlier. A fact_bis rewrite cannot reach the title, and the body needs no change.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsang klase sa bato ang gihimo sa mga bulkan sa Pilipinas?

Ang andesite usa ka komon nga volcanic rock sa mga bulkan sa Ring of Fire, lakip ang mga sa Pilipinas! Kini mas baga (viscous) kaysa basalt ug mahimong maghatag og mas kusog nga mga pagsabog.
proposals.defect: The English says andesite "can produce more explosive eruptions" (a hazard), while the Cebuano says "mas mapuslanon nga mga pagsabog" = more USEFUL/beneficial eruptions, inverting the card's point; and the English is a question ("What kind of rock...") while the Cebuano opens with "Unang klase" (= first kind), which carries no interrogative at all.
proposals.attestation: Two words introduced, both checked. (1) kusog: ceb_usage.py --bis mapuslanon = 140 Cebuano bodies, uniformly useful/beneficial (ffct-01038 "mapuslanon nga makatabang sa organismo" / EN "beneficial and help organisms"), confirming the inversion; --en "explosive erupt" (13 cards) gives the corpus rendering: ffct-29953 "kasagaran maghimo ug mas kusog nga pagbuto" / EN "often causes more explosive eruptions" -- a near-identical EN sentence about thick viscous lava -- and ffct-32801 "hinungdan sa grabe kusog nga pagsabog" / EN "erupt so explosively"; --bis "mas kusog" = 305 bodies, --bis "kusog nga pagsabog" = 4 bodies. The card's own noun "pagsabog" is kept. (2) Unsang: --bis "unsang klase" = 14 Cebuano bodies used exactly as this interrogative (ffct-07142 "Unsang klase sa bulak ang sampaguita?" / EN "What kind of flower is the sampaguita?"), whereas --bis "unang klase" = 35 bodies that are all "nag-unang klase" = main class/type (ffct-00345, ffct-10222), never a question word. Emphasis span "andesite" is untouched.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Kung nayanig: DUCK (magduko), COVER ang ulo ubos sa lig-on nga lamesa, ug HOLD ON nga hugot! Ayaw dagan palabas samtang nayanig pa.
proposals.defect: On a safety card the English instruction is "DUCK down", but the only Cebuano gloss given is "(magtaob)", and taob in this corpus is the rising/high TIDE -- so the one explanation of the action tells a child nothing about getting down.
proposals.attestation: Only word introduced is "magduko". ceb_usage.py --bis taob: 54 Cebuano bodies, all tide (ffct-06178 "Kung mosaka ang taob" / EN "When the tide rises"; ffct-07128 "sa taliwala sa taob ug hunas" / EN "between high and low tide"). --en "Duck, cover" (6 cards) shows the corpus's duck-cover-hold vocabulary: ffct-33001 "kinahanglan MAGDUKO, MOTAKIP sa ulo ug liog, ug MOHAWID sa mga lamesa" / EN "must DUCK, COVER their head and neck, and HOLD ON to their desks" -- the same drill sentence and the same mag- form I used; also ffct-30697 "moduko" / EN "duck", ffct-30242 "Pangduko" / EN "Drop down", ffct-38479 "duko, tago, ug kumot" / EN "drop, cover, and hold". --bis magduko returns 2 bodies (ffct-33001, ffct-07622), so the exact form is attested. Emphasis spans "DUCK" and "COVER" are kept verbatim -- only the parenthetical gloss changed.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Asa ang usa sa labing dagkong geothermal complex sa kalibutan?

Ang MakBan sa Laguna ug Batangas, Pilipinas! Naggamit kini og mainit nga steam gikan sa ilalom sa yuta duol sa Mt. Makiling ug Mt. Banahaw.
proposals.defect: The English hedges -- "ONE OF the world's biggest geothermal power plants" -- but the Cebuano question asks for "ang labing dagkong geothermal complex sa kalibutan" (the single largest on Earth) and answers it flatly, so a Cebuano-only child learns a false superlative the card never claims.
proposals.attestation: No content word introduced -- only the hedge "usa sa" inserted before the card's own "labing dagkong". ceb_usage.py --bis "usa sa labing": 72 Cebuano bodies, exactly this hedging frame (ffct-00311 "usa sa labing delikadong mananap sa dagat" / EN "one of the most dangerous animals in the sea"). The same frame with this card's own adjective is attested: --bis "labing dagko" gives ffct-13933 "usa sa labing dagkong nasod" / EN "one of the world's biggest ... nations" and ffct-32947 "usa sa labing dagko nga freshwater wetlands" / EN "one of the Philippines' largest freshwater wetlands". --en "one of the largest" (33 cards) confirms the hedge is standard: "usa sa pinakadako" 28 hits, and question-form precedent ffct-02816 "Unsa ang usa sa pinakadako nga kabog sa kalibotan?". The answer sentence is left untouched: it answers "where" and asserts no superlative once the question is hedged. No emphasis spans.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis delivers everything fact_en says (steam rushes up through drilled wells, spins the blades, blades turn a generator that makes electricity).
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the finding is entirely about title_bis ("Singaw nga Tuyo Turbine"), and the word 'tuyo' never appears in fact_bis. The body uses the spin verb correctly twice — "mopalikid sa turbine blades" / "Ang paglikid sa blades mopalikid sa generator" — and the finding itself concedes this. Repairing a title is out of scope for a fact_bis repair, so there is no body edit to make.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis carries unlock hot underground rock without water, engineers drill deep, pump water, capture steam, expand geothermal energy.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the 'buto' (bone/blast) defect is in title_bis only; the body says "Nagbutas ang mga inhinyero og lawom" (butas = hole/bore), which is the correct rendering of "Engineers drill deep" and which the finding itself cites as proof of the intended word. No word in fact_bis contradicts fact_en.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang mga hayop sa Philippine Trench makabuhi sa grabe ka taas nga presyon sa tubig, kapin sa 1,100 ka pilo kaysa sa ibabaw sa dagat! Ang amphipod crustaceans ug sea cucumbers adunay espesyal nga adaptasyon alang sa maong giladmon.
proposals.defect: The English quantifies the pressure as "over 1,100 times the surface" and the Cebuano gives only "grabe ka taas nga presyon" — the card's one number is missing, so a child cannot say how much pressure the trench animals withstand.
proposals.attestation: Only the missing figure was inserted; the rest of the sentence and the emphasis span "Philippine Trench" are untouched (verified present verbatim). Introduced words, all corpus-attested in Cebuano BODIES: 'kapin' = over/more than, 201 bodies (ffct-00028 "kapin sa 2,000 tonelada" for EN "over 2,000 tonnes"). 'pilo' = times/multiple, 136 bodies, 86 with the exact "ka pilo" classifier (ffct-02826 "1,141 ka pilo sa iyang kaugalingong timbang" for EN "1,141 times its own body weight"; ffct-07635 "kapin sa 1,000 ka pilo" for EN "more than 1,000 times"). The whole comparative template comes from dcard-11575: "kapin sa 100 ka pilo ang gidak-on kay sa atong Adlaw" for EN "more than 100 times the size of our Sun". 'kaysa' = than, 1,439 bodies (ffct-00028 "mas bug-at pa kaysa sa"). 'ibabaw sa dagat' = sea surface, 16 bodies (ffct-13774 "duol sa ibabaw sa dagat" for EN "near the ocean's surface"; ffct-05781 for EN "near the surface").

proposals.new_fact_bis: Sa pag-bisita sa langub, kanunay og helmet ug dala ang suga, ug adunha og giya! Ayaw kalimoti nga ayaw paghikap o pagbali sa mga stalactite ug stalagmite.
proposals.defect: The English prescribes a helmet as cave gear; the Cebuano says 'sumbrera', which is a hat, so the card tells a child head protection for a cave is a hat.
proposals.attestation: One-word swap, nothing else touched; emphasis spans "stalactite" and "stalagmite" verified present verbatim. 'helmet' (the English word kept in Cebuano) is attested in 25 Cebuano BODIES, always for EN "helmet": ffct-01511 "Ang pagsul-ob og helmet kung magbisikleta" (EN "Wearing a helmet when biking"), ffct-03252 "sama sa helmet nga nagbantay niini" (EN "like a helmet keeping it safe"), ffct-04514 "nagsul-ob ta og helmet". Counter-evidence for the current word: 'sumbrera' appears in exactly 1 body in the whole corpus — this card. I left the pre-existing typo "adunha" (for adunay) alone as out of scope for a minimal word repair; it is not a false statement, only a misspelling.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis states Galileo's heliocentric claim exactly as fact_en does, including the "not the other way around" contrast.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the 'nituyo' error is in title_bis only; the body uses the correct orbit verb twice — "Nagtuyok ba gyud ang Adlaw sa Kalibotan?" and "ang Kalibotan ug ubang planeta nagtuyok sa Adlaw, dili ang Adlaw sa Kalibotan" — and the finding confirms the body is right. No body edit is derivable from fact_en.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Asa nagporma ang dakong deposito sa nickel ug iron ore sa Mindanao?

Sa Surigao del Norte! Nagporma kini gikan sa weathering sa ultramafic rocks sama sa peridotite sulod sa milyon-milyon ka tuig.
proposals.defect: The English says the ores formed "over millions of years"; the Cebuano says "gatusan ka milyon ka tuig" (hundreds of millions), inflating the card's timescale by two orders of magnitude.
proposals.attestation: Only the quantity phrase changed; emphasis span "Surigao del Norte" verified present verbatim. 'milyon-milyon' is the corpus's own rendering of English "millions of years": 66 Cebuano BODIES, e.g. ffct-00250 "mitungha milyon-milyon ka tuig una pa ang bulak" for EN "appearing millions of years before flowers existed", ffct-02310 "nagtubo na sila milyon-milyon ka tuig" for EN "growing millions of years", ffct-00984 "milyon-milyon ka tuig na ang milabay" for EN "millions of years ago". The surrounding words ('sulod sa', 'ka tuig') were already in the card.

proposals.defect: Arguable only: the English's "In about 5 billion years" is rendered "Mga 5 bilyong tuig na karon", which is clumsy about time direction — but the futurity is still carried by the verbs, and the headline defect ('Uma' = farm) is in the title, not the body.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the body's tense is not actually false — "ang atong Adlaw molapad ngadto sa red giant" and "Unya, mobiya kini" are both future forms, so a child does read this as the Sun's future, and per the rule a clumsy-but-delivering Cebuano is a HOLD. The alternative phrasing is also too thinly sourced to impose: the corpus's future-time form "gikan karon" appears in exactly 1 Cebuano body in 47,056 cards (dcard-03820 "50 ka milyon ka tuig gikan karon" for EN "50 million years from now"), which is not enough attestation to justify rewriting a sentence that is not wrong. 'panloob nga planeta' (inner planets) is a Tagalog-flavoured loan (2 bodies, incl. ffct-25280 "panloob nga resistensya" for EN "internal resistance") but it does deliver the English meaning, and register/dialect is out of scope. The title fix belongs to a title pass.

proposals.defect: None that is a wrong word: the body states Polaris sits above the north pole, appears not to move while other stars circle, and is a sailors' direction guide; only the English adverbial "for centuries" has no counterpart.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the 'amihan' (monsoon wind vs north) defect is in title_bis only — the body never uses 'amihan' at all, it carries "North Star" and "north pole" as English strings and uses "naglibot" (155 bodies) correctly for the circling stars. The single English element absent from the Cebuano is the duration "for centuries", which is an omission that introduces no false claim; restoring it would mean adding a clause rather than correcting a wrong word, which is outside the minimal-edit mandate. The title needs a separate fix.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Ngano nga mas dugay ang phase cycle sa Moon?

Mo-orbit ang Moon sa Yuta sulod sa 27.3 ka adlaw (sidereal period), apan naglibot usab ang Yuta sa Adlaw, kaya kinahanglan pa og dugang ang Moon aron maulit ang phase, busa ang synodic period 29.5 ka adlaw!
proposals.defect: The English's reason clause is "since Earth also moves around the Sun"; the Cebuano says "nagdala usab ang Yuta sa Adlaw" — the Earth CARRIES the Sun — so the causal fact the whole 27.3 vs 29.5 day contrast rests on is replaced by a false relation.
proposals.attestation: One verb replaced, numbers, units and the rest of the sentence untouched; no emphasis spans on this card. 'naglibot' is attested in 155 Cebuano BODIES and is the corpus's verb for exactly this orbital relation: ffct-29109 "tungod sa pagkiling sa Yuta samtang naglibot sa adlaw" for EN "because of Earth's tilt as it orbits the Sun"; ffct-21952 and ffct-26528 "samtang naglibot sa Yuta" for EN "while orbiting / circling Earth"; the same-root form in ffct-23811 "padayon tang molibot sa Adlaw" for EN "keeps us orbiting around the Sun", and ffct-28853 "Molibot usab sa Adlaw (revolution) matag tuig" for EN "It also revolves around the Sun yearly" — that last one is the same "also ... around the Sun" sentence shape this card needs. I left the Tagalog connective 'kaya' and the vague "kinahanglan pa og dugang" alone: register is out of scope and neither states anything false.

proposals.new_fact_bis: Ang nawong sa Moon natakpan sa regolith — crushed rock ug abug nga adunay hait nga mga kilid! Bilyun-bilyong tuig sa meteorite impact ang naghimo, ug walay hangin o tubig nga makapahamis niini.
proposals.defect: The English says regolith has "sharp edges" and that "no wind or water ever smoothed it"; the Cebuano says the edges are 'matalinghaga' (figurative/obscure) and ends on 'mipakin', which is not a word — so both halves of the card's distinguishing fact, sharpness and the absence of smoothing, are unreadable.
proposals.attestation: Two wrong words replaced, nothing else; no emphasis spans on this card. (1) 'hait' = sharp, 236 Cebuano BODIES, and the exact phrase is attested: dcard-05901 "adunay hait nga mga kilid" for EN "have sharp, angular edges", plus dcard-05444 "hait nga kilid" for EN "sharp edges" and ffct-00209 "init o hait" for EN "hot or sharp". Counter-evidence for the current word: 'matalinghaga' appears in only 2 bodies corpus-wide — this card and ffct-33243, where it is likewise a mis-rendering of "sharper" — so it has no attested 'sharp' usage to stand on. (2) 'makapahamis' = makes it smooth, attested in dcard-08137 "Ang pag-polish sa usa ka surface makapahamis kini" for EN "Polishing a surface makes it smoother", with the same root in dcard-00897 "pinaagi sa pagpahamis sa mga surface" for EN "by making the surfaces smoother" and ffct-27241 "Ipantay ug ipahamis" for EN "Make its wings even and smooth"; the bare root 'hamis' is in 140 bodies for EN "smooth". I deliberately chose the attested prefixed form 'makapahamis' over the past form 'mipahamis', which the corpus does not attest. Counter-evidence for the current word: 'mipakin' occurs in exactly 1 body — this card.

proposals.defect: None in the body — fact_bis gives the English's full causal chain: droplets in clouds join, grow too heavy to float, and fall.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason: the 'moulaw' (shame) error is in title_bis only; the body has the correct rain verb twice, "Nganong moulan?" and "Moulan kung ang mga tulo sa tubig sa panganod magtapok", as the finding itself notes. The "mabug-at na kaayo aron molutaw" rendering of "too heavy to float" is clumsy but delivers the English, which per the rule is a HOLD, not a rewrite.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Kinsa ang unang tawo nga ni-spacewalk, ug unsay nahitabo sa iyang biyahe?

Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov! Niadtong Marso 1965, ang iyang 12-minutong spacewalk nagkaproblema sa dihang naghubag sa gawas ang iyang spacesuit.
proposals.defect: The English says the spacesuit "ballooned outward" (inflated); the Cebuano says 'nagsabog' (scattered / blew apart), so the card answers its own question — "unsay nahitabo sa iyang biyahe?" — with an event that did not happen.
proposals.attestation: One verb replaced, date and duration untouched; no emphasis spans on this card. 'naghubag' = swelled / puffed up is attested in 10 Cebuano BODIES with exactly the inflation sense, including the puff-up cases: ffct-03378 "Kung naghubag na ang butete" for EN "When a pufferfish puffs itself up", ffct-01043 "Nganong tunokon ang naghubag nga butete?" for EN "Why does a puffed-up pufferfish look spiky?", ffct-05882 "kining mga bula ang naghubag sa pan" for EN "the gas bubbles puff up the bread", and ffct-00227 for EN "swell up". The same root is the corpus's rendering of English inflate elsewhere: ffct-16873 "makapahubag sa lobo" for EN "inflate a balloon", ffct-12826 "mohubag ang butete" for EN "puff up". Counter-evidence for the current word: 'sabog' is NOT ATTESTED IN ANY CEBUANO BODY (0 of 47,056). I kept the card's existing "sa gawas" rather than substituting an unattested 'pagawas'.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsay nahimo nga planeta sa usa ka butang?

Niadtong 2006, nagbutang ang IAU og tulo ka lagda: kinahanglan maglibot sa Adlaw, adunay igo nga gravity aron mahimong lingin (hydrostatic equilibrium), ug 'gipaalis' na ang iyang orbit sa ubang lawas. Ang Pluto wala makatagbaw sa ikatulong lagda!
proposals.defect: The English says rule 2 is "have enough gravity to be round", but the Cebuano says "adunay igo nga gravity aron manghikog" — to hang/kill oneself — so the body never says round anywhere and rule 2 is unrecoverable.
proposals.attestation: Introduced only "mahimong lingin". ceb_usage --bis lingin = 253 Cebuano BODIES, always for English "round" (ffct-02448 "lingin sama sa bola" = "round like a ball"; ffct-01592 "Ang lingin ug puti nga bulak" = "The round white flowers"). ceb_usage --bis "mahimong lingin" = 7 bodies, and the near-identical sibling card ffct-36030 renders "It is big enough to be round, making it a dwarf planet" as "Igo kini ka dako aron mahimong lingin, mao nga kini usa ka dwarf planet" — the exact construction and the exact concept. ceb_usage --bis malingin = 0 bodies (NOT ATTESTED), so that shorter form was rejected. ceb_usage --bis mahimong = 3238 bodies. Confirmed --bis manghikog = 1 body, this card alone. emphasis_bis is empty; nothing else touched ("makatagbaw"/"gipaalis" left alone as recoverable and unflagged).

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsaon pagsupak sa pag-anod sa yuta sa mga tarik nga bakilid?

Ang pagtanom og vetiver grass nga adunay lawom nga gamot sa tarik nga mga bakilid sa Benguet makapugong sa topsoil nga maanod!
proposals.defect: The English is entirely about soil WASHING AWAY on STEEP SLOPES, but the Cebuano says "pag-uwang"/"ma-uwang" (howling/barking) and "taluktok nga bukid" (mountain summits), so neither erosion nor the slope appears anywhere in the body.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Natinggala ka ba nganong dili kanunay nga modaog ang mga bug-at sa lumba sa pagkahulog?

Ang timbang mao ang birahay sa gravity! Mas dako nga mass adunay mas dako nga timbang, pero dili kini nag-inusara nga rason ngano nga una kini motugpa.
proposals.defect: fact_en says heavy things don't always WIN a falling RACE, that weight is gravity's PULL, and that bigger weight doesn't make it LAND first — fact_bis instead says they don't "go there" in a "res" (not a word), that weight is gravity's SHAKING (pag-uyog), and that it STOPS (mohunong) first, so the card's definition is false and its hook is unanswerable.
proposals.attestation: Defect words: uyog = vibrate/shake, 182 bodies, e.g. ffct-01639 "Ang tingog mao ang pag-uyog" for EN "Sound is a vibration" — never pull; moana and res each occur in exactly ONE Cebuano body in all 47,056 cards, this card itself (unsourced); mohunong = stop, 248 bodies, all cessation (ffct-00296 "mohunong ang photosynthesis"). Introduced words, all corpus-attested: birahay = gravity's pull, 5 bodies, with ffct-14924 rendering this card's identical English sentence — EN "weight is gravity's pull" -> BIS "weight mao ang birahay sa gravity" (also ffct-23809, ffct-23814 "kusog ang birahay sa gravity paubos"); modaog = win, 20 bodies, incl. the race sense ffct-03289 "Unsang mananap ang modaog sa layo nga dagan?" for EN "What animal wins the long-distance race?"; lumba = race, ffct-23893 / ffct-26272 / ffct-28777 as above; motugpa = land, 36 bodies, incl. this exact falling-objects context ffct-24314 "dungan motugpa ang bato ug bola" for EN "a rock and a ball hit the ground together" and ffct-26850 "dungan matugpa ang balhibo ug martilyo". Three spans swapped, sentence structure, facts, numbers and the untouched words (incl. "Natinggala") left as-is; emphasis_bis is empty.

proposals.new_fact_bis:
Unsa ang naa sa tropical rainforest biome sa Pilipinas?

Adunay daghang lain-laing ecosystem, gikan sa lasang sa bukid hangtod sa lamakan sa ubos nga lugar!
proposals.defect: The English says the biome ranges from mountain FORESTS to lowland swamps, but the Cebuano says "gikan sa gubat sa bukid" — gubat is the war/battle word in this corpus, so the mountain-forest half of the example is not delivered.
proposals.attestation: Only one word introduced: lasang. `--bis lasang` = 230 Cebuano BODIES, all forest sense (ffct-00025 "talagsaong lasang sa Palawan" EN "Palawan's special forest"; ffct-00101 "lasang sa Mindanao" EN "Mindanao's rainforests"; ffct-00103 "salog sa lasang" EN "forest floor"). `--en rainforest` frequency table: lasang 30, kalasangan 11 — lasang is the corpus's word for this exact English concept. `--bis gubat` = only 7 bodies: 5 are unambiguously war/battle (ffct-02516 "tinuod nga gubat", ffct-03039 "ebidensya sa gubat", ffct-12088 "gubat sa lawas batok sa impeksyon", ffct-14803, ffct-26273 EN "used in war"); the only two forest-sense uses are this card and ffct-39516, i.e. defects, so gubat cannot vouch for itself. Phrase shape "lasang sa <place>" is attested 39x in bodies (e.g. ffct-04897 "yuta sa lasang sa Bukid...", ffct-31479 "lasang sa mountain range" for EN "Mountain forests"); "sa bukid" was already in the card. emphasis_bis is empty — no span touched. Diff = one word.

proposals.defect: Finding does not hold: the English analogy "like thread winding around tiny spools" IS delivered by "sama sa hilo nga molikop sa gagmay nga spools".
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason — the hilo=POISON-only false-friend claim is refuted by the corpus. `--en thread` (128 cards): the single most characteristic Cebuano word is hilo (61 occurrences), used for exactly this concept: ffct-00171 "Aron makuha ang hilo sa seda" EN "To collect silk thread"; ffct-00206 "Nagpagawas sila og hilo nga seda" EN "They spin a thread of silk"; ffct-00538 "dili pilit nga hilo sa ... sapot" EN "non-sticky threads of its own web"; ffct-00843 "usa lang ka tuluy-tuloyon nga hilo" EN "a single silk thread". DNA-context precedent: ffct-14388 "sama sa taas nga hilo nga maayong gibugkos" for EN "like a long thread carefully bundled up" — the same DNA-packing analogy, same word. hilo is a homonym (poison AND thread/fibre) and the corpus uses the thread sense freely; register/ambiguity is out of scope. No edit.

proposals.defect: Finding does not hold: fact_en's "weak bonds between the two strands break, and the double helix unwinds into two separate strands" is delivered — "hilo" carries the strand/fibre sense in this corpus, and the numbers, direction and double helix are all intact.
proposals.attestation: HOLD reason — the hilo=POISON-only claim is refuted. `--en strand` (66 cards) frequency table lists hilo 10 alongside strand 30 / hibla 5, and the hilo hits are genuine strand renderings: ffct-17916 "tag-as ug kulot nga mga hilo" EN "long, coiled strands"; ffct-33927 "morag mga hilo sa buhok" EN "look like strands of hair"; dcard-04823 "mga hilo sa sulod sa punoan ug dahon" EN "strands inside stems and leaves"; dcard-01209 / dcard-07765 "nipis nga mga hilo" EN "thin strands" (optical fibers); dcard-09956 "taas ug niwang nga mga hilo" EN "long, skinny strands". hibla (ffct-01800, ffct-06606) is an equally valid corpus variant, so swapping would be a preference, not a repair — and Rule 1 forbids rewriting for variation. proposals.new_fact_bis: Kung nagluto kung magsugod ang linog, palonga ang kalan kung maabot nga luwas, dayon duko, tago, ug kumot!
proposals.defect: The English's third safety step is "hold" (hold on), but the Cebuano says "kumot", which in this corpus is a blanket / crumpling, so the child is never told to hold on.

Evidence: `--bis kumot` = 4 bodies and every non-subject one is the blanket sense (ffct-23641 "Sama kini og kumot aron magpabilin nga init ang pagkaon" EN "acts like a cozy blanket"; ffct-28851 "sama sa dako nga dili makita nga kumot" EN "like a giant invisible blanket"; ffct-13451 "morag berde nga kumot sa nawong sa linaw"); no hold sense anywhere. Replacement kupot is attested: `--bis kupot` = 17 Cebuano BODIES, all grip/hold (ffct-11914 "kusog kaayo ang kupot sa gagmayng balhibo sa iyang tiil" EN "the grip from tiny hairs on its feet"; ffct-24495 "mas lig-on ang kupot" EN "a firmer grip"; ffct-13840 "Buhian nila ang ilang kupot" EN "They let go of their grip"). `--en "hold on"` (46 cards) ranks the same root top: mokupot 9, makakupot 8, and `--bis pagkupot` = 33 bodies (ffct-02509 "aron makakupot og hugot" EN "to hold on"). Bare root matches the card's existing bare-root chain (duko, tago). emphasis_bis empty — no span touched.
